06_marg25: OF ALL THE MEN OF ISRAEL FIT FOR WAR etc. ORIGEN. Allegorically. Septuagint: Every one that goeth forth in the strength of Israel etc. He therefore who goes forth in strength is numbered, and only in the strength of Israel. For there is a virtue of the mind which the philosophers of the Greeks teach, which is exercised not for God but for human glory. There is also a virtue of the Assyrians or Chaldeans in the studies of astrology, but it is not Israelite nor pertaining to God. Only the Israelite virtue is numbered with God, which is taught by God, learned through the divine Scriptures, and handed down through the faith of the Gospel and the apostles.
06_marg26: RABAN. Morally. Ruben, the firstborn of Israel, which is interpreted "seeing sons" or "seeing in the midst", can signify the first Church, which was in Jerusalem, which the Lord himself first founded in the apostles; whom Elisur signifies, that is, my father is strong. For he it is of whom it is said: "The Lord who is strong, the Lord mighty in battle." This Ruben therefore, under such a prince, sees sons, that is, the faithful, flocking to him. Whence, at the preaching of Peter, three thousand were baptized in one day, and the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul.
06_marg27: Morally. The prince of the tribe of Ruben signifies generally those who, living well in the midst of the brethren, take care of those subject to them, instruct them by word and example, and nourish them as sons for the warfare of God. In this tribe the prince is Elisur, that is, "my father is strong" or "my father who straitens", the son of Sedeur, that is, "of the hidden one". For he who by the authority of mastership and fatherly discipline rules and corrects those subject to him well, not outwardly for human praise but in the hidden place of the heart for the glory of God, is by right the prince of the tribes and houses, that is, of the married, the continent and the virgins, having care of both sexes.
06_interl10: It is interpreted hearing, and signifies the devotion of the Gentile Church; of which: "At the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me."
06_interl11: In this Salamiel rules, that is, "God my peace", namely Jesus, "our peace, who hath made both one", when he showed the signs of his power through the words and works of the faithful.
06_marg28: RABANUS. Simeon generally signifies all the obedient, whose prince is Salamiel, that is, "God repaying me" or "God my peace"; the son of Surisaddai, that is, "of one who holds back from the thing"; since he who ponders the just retribution of God with a peaceful heart, calm and humble, appears worthy of veneration in the assembly of the faithful. "For he that humbleth himself shall be exalted." For such turn their whole intention to the good pleasure of God, and according to what is contained in the Scriptures confidently promise to obey, saying: "To thee have I lifted up my eyes, who dwellest in heaven."
06_marg29: Morally. THE SAME. In Juda can be signified all who rightly call upon the name of the Lord, dissenting neither in sense nor in word from the rule of faith, whose prince by merit was Nahasson, namely he who not only instructs others by preaching, but also slays in himself the poisoned darts of vices by chastising his body, according to that: "I chastise my body, and bring it into subjection" etc.
06_marg30: Allegorically. Juda, from whom are the kings, which is interpreted confession or praise. This signifies the people of the Church, whose head is the lion of the tribe of Juda, that is, Christ. For the praise or confession of true faith, that is, right preaching, is only in the Church. Nahasson therefore, that is, serpentine or augury, the son of Aminadab, namely of a willing people, is understood as the Saviour, begotten of the patriarchs, servants devoted to God, who by his death destroyed the devil. For in the serpent, from which the first cause of death, that is, sin, came forth, death is figured. Whence: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up etc.
06_marg31: RABANUS. Issachar not unfittingly expresses the monks, who, spurning all the business of the world, with the gift of God, that is, the Holy Ghost, protecting them, seek the eternal reward by a strict life, pleasure being mortified; and trampling on the pomps of the world, embracing lowly things, desire to please God alone.
06_marg32: Allegorically. Of those who piously exercise themselves that they may receive a reward in heaven, the prince is Nathanael, that is, my God, or the gift of God; the son of Suar, that is, of the little one, namely of Christ, who appeared little among men. For he himself is the leader, and he himself also the reward.
06_marg33: THE SAME. Zabulon figures the patient, who persevere unconquered by the defence of virtues against all adversities; whose prince is God alone, without whom they can do nothing, saying with the Apostle: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress?" etc.
06_marg34: ALLEGORICALLY. The dwelling of strength has for its prince Eliab, which is interpreted my God the Father, namely God, who is the Father of the faithful, whom he orders and rules. And he is the son of Helon, that is, of the oak. For the Church is rightly called the dwelling of strength, namely against heretics and schismatics.
06_marg35: THE SAME. Joseph, father of two tribes, signifies Christ, the father of two peoples and the corner stone. Ephraim, the younger, preferred to Manasses the firstborn: the Gentile people preferred to the Jewish. Whence: "Amen I say to you, I have not found so great faith in Israel."
06_marg36: Elisama signifies Christ, of whom it is said: He became obedient to the Father unto death etc. Who says of himself: The things I have heard of him, these same I speak in the world. He is the son of Ammiud, that is, of my renowned people, namely of the stock of the patriarchs and prophets.
06_marg37: Elisama, prince in the tribe of Ephraim, signifies those who attentively hear the word of God with a good and very good heart, and bring forth fruit in patience.
06_marg38: My renowned people, or forgetful; forgetting, namely, the things that are behind, stretching forth to those that are before, that they may receive the crown of life which God will render to them that love him.
06_marg39: Gamaliel: God has repaid me; the son of Phadassur, that is, of strong redemption, is prince in the tribe of Manasses, which is interpreted forgotten or forgetful; since Christ, whom the Father sent into the world to call the Jewish people, found in his kingdom a forgetful nation. For Israel forgot his Creator. Yet not all perished: when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in, all Israel shall be saved.
06_interl21: Which is interpreted the temptation of iniquity, or of my humility.
06_marg40: Benjamin signifies Jerusalem, which is in his tribe, whose people, according to the prophecy of Rachel, was "Benoni, that is, the son of sorrow", because he afflicted his mother with grievous sorrow. For he shed the blood of the prophets, and conspiring in the death of Christ said: "His blood be upon us, and upon our children." But in those who believed, according to the father's prophecy, the son of the right hand. Benjamin can also signify the Gentile people, which was a son of sorrow by persecuting the Christians. He can also be called the son of the right hand, because in the judgment he will be at the right hand of God, or because he does right things, that is, good works. Of this people Abidan, that is, my father is judge, the son of Gedeon, which is interpreted the temptation of iniquity or of humility, is prince. Because Christ, whom the Jew despised as lowly and the devil wickedly tempted, is the head of believers, and the judge who is to come of the living and the dead.
06_marg41: The son of the right hand signifies those who fight bravely against the enemies, and bravely press down the goads of temptation, nor allow anything womanish or soft to rule in them.
06_marg42: Dan: judgment or judging. These are they who do all things with discernment, who set up Ahiezer, that is, a brother helper, as their prince, and do all things according to the rule of the fathers, or ascribe all their good things to God.
06_marg43: Dan: judgment or judging. Ahiezer: my brother is a helper. Ammisaddai: my people sufficing. In Dan we take the Gentiles, who fled from the cold of unbelief to the grace of Christ. Whence, in what follows, Dan first pitches his camp toward the north by the tents. Ahiezer therefore, the son of Ammisaddai, is prince in this tribe, since the apostles of Christ, as brothers, sufficient in word and deed, rule over the Church of the Gentiles, and exhort them with brotherly love to the fellowship of spiritual grace.
06_marg44: Aser: blessed, or having riches, signifies the faithful rich in virtues, over whom is the rule of Phegiel, that is, the meeting of God. The son of Ochran, which is interpreted "he troubled them": namely Christ, "the mediator of God and men", who came to meet the human race in its peril, and troubled the evil spirits by driving them back. Whence: "Going up to him, he bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine" etc.
06_marg45: In Aser are figured those who do all things with counsel, and wish to be rich not in perishing things but in virtues; they give their substance to the poor and lay up treasures in heaven; whence: They shall be blessed: for recompense shall be made them at the resurrection of the just.
06_marg46: ALLEGORICALLY OR MORALLY. Gad: girded. Eliasaph: the protection or ascent of my God. Duel: knowing God. Gad therefore signifies the people of the faithful, which always girds the loins of the mind with justice, and, furnished with spiritual arms, fights down the spiritual wickednesses; over which presides Christ, begotten of the stock of the Fathers, truly knowing God and obeying him, directing and protecting his own.
06_marg47: Gad can also express the teachers, who, set in readiness, are prepared to resist the enemies; among whom Eliasaph excels, namely he who lifts up his heart to God, whence he sought help. Whence: A cock girded, or girt about the loins; and a ram; and there is no king that can resist him.
06_marg48: Nephtali: turned or enlarged. This is the faithful people, which, turned from error, has been enlarged by the abundance of faith through the ends of the world. To whom Isaias says: "Enlarge the place of thy tent" etc. Ahira, that is, the friend of my brother, the son of Enan, that is, of the fountain of sadness, is set over it; because the Son of God, who was a friend to his brothers, that is, the Jews, when through the law he gave the knowledge of himself, now counselling the Gentiles through the sadness of penance, converted them to the faith, that, numbered in his army, they might enjoy his leadership and rule in the spiritual battle.
06_marg49: In Nephtali are understood the saints who extend the charity of brotherhood even to enemies: their prince is Ahira, that is, the Lord himself, who rules by the leadership of his love those whom he enrols not among servants but among friends. Whence: I will not now call you servants, but friends etc.

06_marg50: ISIDORE. Those chosen for war are numbered from the twentieth year, because from this age wars arise against each of the vices. And therefore they are chosen for the fight, that they may fight against lust, lest they be overcome by wantonness.
06_marg51: BY THEIR KINDREDS etc. AUGUSTINE. It is rightly asked why through all the tribes it is said: according to their kindreds, according to their people, according to the houses of their families, according to the heads, according to the number of their names; and these five are repeated in just the same way until all the tribes are completed; as though it were one thing according to their kindreds, another according to their peoples, another according to the houses of the families, another according to the number of names, another according to the heads, when rather all these seem to signify the same thing in other words. Surely, then, the number itself signifies something, that the same thing is repeated five times in varied ways. For this number, that is, five, is especially commended, as in the five books of Moses in the Old Testament. But the four which are joined after, that is: the males from twenty years and upward, every one that goeth forth in strength, of their reviewing, although these too are repeated in the same way through all the tribes, have a necessary difference. For since the number of the whole multitude belonging to one tribe was being dealt with, the sex had to be distinguished. Therefore it was put: all the males. And lest little ones also be counted, it was added: from twenty years and upward. And lest unwarlike old age be numbered, it was added: every one that goeth forth in strength. And all is concluded with the word for the work that was being done, so that it is said: their reviewing. For the reviewing took place when these thousands of men or names were counted. Those five therefore, kindreds, peoples, houses of families, and number of men, and head, and these four, sex, age, strength, reviewing, perhaps signify something in their very number. For if one of these numbers is multiplied by the other, so that five fours or four fives are taken, they make twenty. By this number too that age of youths is marked, which number is recalled when entry is made into the land of promise, and that age of twenty years is spoken of which had not turned aside to the right or to the left; where the faithful of both Testaments holding the true faith seem to me to be signified. For the Old Testament excels above all in the five books of Moses, and the New in the four Gospels.

06_marg53: SIXTY-TWO etc. GILBERT. I do not think it should be passed over in silence that here the lesser sums of numbers and of lesser mystery go before, and the greater and of greater dignity follow, or the reverse. For the soldiers of Christ go before one another in honour, and count each other better than themselves. Also the married engage more boldly than the continent, the continent than the virgins, and are of greater merit. But sometimes the sums are mingled, lest the whiteness of virginity shrink from the embrace of wedlock; and in the necessities of the flesh the married minister to virginity and continence, that the divine army may have "one heart and one soul".

06_marg55: RABANUS. In the tribe of Levi the priestly order is marked, which is set over the tabernacle of the testimony, that they may take care of the Church, in which the testaments of God are laid up, and that all the vessels, that is, the faithful chosen for the spiritual ministry, may remain without error and the filth of vices. For this order ought to see to whatever pertains to the ceremonies of the law. For it is theirs to teach the people how to live honourably and orderly in the Church according to the law. They carry the tabernacle and its furniture: because the priests, by compassion, by bearing with the ways of the weak, and by consoling, carry the Church as it were on the shoulders of labour and patience.

06_marg57: WHAT STRANGER SOEVER etc. AUGUSTINE. Let the alien who approaches die. Here alien is to be understood also of those children of Israel who were not of that tribe which he commanded to serve the tabernacle, that is, who were not of the tribe of Levi. But it is strange how by a loose use he is called alien, which rather signifies men of another race, allogenes, and not rather allophylos, which signifies men of another tribe; which name Scripture uses rather for the men of other nations, so that they are called allophyli, as if men of other tribes.
06_marg58: He who approaches the sacred ministry unworthily does not escape the punishment of presumption. For no man should take the honour to himself but he that is called by God, as Aaron was. Whence Ozias, who usurped the priesthood, was struck with leprosy.
06_marg59: Allegorically. ORIGEN. Let every one go forward in the camp according to the standards: this Moses commanded, or rather God through Moses. But it can be that by emulation of good works we come from the lower standards to better and more magnificent ones. For if we have ready the zeal for better things, and, forgetting the things behind, stretch forth to those that are before, in the resurrection of the dead (where, as star differeth from star, the merits of each will shine) we shall be transferred from the lower to the better and brighter standards, and be made equal to the more splendid stars. And human nature can even advance so far in this life that in the resurrection of the dead it can be made equal not only to the splendour of the stars but also of the sun, because the just shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of God. Hence therefore it is that he adds: according to their standards by the houses of their families. What he says, by the houses of the families, is in the Greek the same word which the Apostle uses there, of whom "all paternity in heaven and earth is named". What Paul therefore calls paternities, the Latin translator calls families. These therefore are the paternities or families which Paul has already shown in heaven, and Moses describes on earth under legal figures, according to which he warns us to go forward, that we may be joined to the heavenly paternities. For there are families and paternities in heaven, among which perhaps is that which Paul names the church of the firstborn who are written in heaven. To which we shall be joined if we do all things in order, if nothing restless, nothing disorderly, nothing dishonourable be found in us.

06_interl76: Others: of the families; according to the Greek, of the paternities.
06_interl77: No man being a soldier to God entangleth himself with secular businesses.
06_marg60: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. Allegorically. ORIGEN. Septuagint: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Let every man march according to his order and according to his ensigns, according to the houses of their families; let the children of Israel set their camps over against etc. It taught that the army of God going out of the land of Egypt and passing through the desert was visited, that is, numbered, by Moses and Aaron, and set apart by each tribe, counted under a fixed number; which, expounding, we said was a form prescribed for how the people of God, going out of the Egypt of this world and hastening to the land of promise, that is, to the place of virtues or to the glory of the kingdom of heaven, is led by what ranks and degrees of merits. And by these we showed the magnificence of the good things to come foreshadowed in the law. But this reading teaches how the order of the camps is set by those who are bound over to God and do not entangle themselves in secular business, saying: Let every man according to his order, and according to his ensigns etc. Paul also says: Let all things be done decently and according to order. There is therefore one Spirit of God, who speaks both in Paul and in Moses. Moses commands that they march in order in the camp, Paul that all things be done in order in the church. And Moses, who ministered the law, commands order to be kept in the camp; but Paul, the minister of the Gospel, wishes the Christian to be ordered not only in his acts but also in his dress, saying: Women in like manner in decent apparel. Whence I think he wished order to be kept not only in offices and dress, but also signifies a certain order in the soul, according to which it is said each one ought to march; which is shown chiefly by the fruits of works, and no less by the greatness of the understanding. For it often happens that one who has a lowly understanding and minds earthly things occupies the high rank of the priesthood or the chair of the teacher; and one who is spiritual, and so free from earthly things that he can examine all things and be judged by none, holds the rank of a lower ministry, or is left in the multitude of the common people. But this is to despise the statutes of the law and the Gospel, and to do nothing according to order.
06_marg61: Each of us, anxious about food and drink and taking every care in secular things, assigning one or two hours to God and coming to the church to pray, or hearing the word of God in passing, does not hear the precept which says that all things be done according to order. For order is first to seek the kingdom of God and his justice, and to believe that these things shall be added to us in the second place. Every man therefore ought to march according to his order: priest, deacon, virgin, and whoever are seen to be in the profession of religion. For if he has done anything wanton and froward, Moses at once reproves them, saying: Let every man march according to his order etc. Let each one therefore know his order, and understand what is worthy of his order, and so weigh his acts and words, his gait too and his dress, that it may agree with the profession of his order, lest through him the name of God be blasphemed.
06_marg62: According to his ensigns etc. By which, namely, the property of each is marked; for example: We are all alike, but each has his own distinction, either in bearing or in stature or in dress or in posture, by which Paul, because he is Paul, is marked, and Peter, because he is Peter and not Paul. From the voice too of each a diversity of sign is given, so that from the voice and speech you know the one who is speaking. So I think there are also diverse signs in souls; and the motion of one soul is gentler, mild, placid, tranquil, even; of another turbulent, lifted up, harsher, more excitable, more wanton. One is circumspect, cautious, provident, careful, diligent; another slothful, slack, negligent, incautious. In these one has more, another less. And perhaps as great as the diversity in the appearance of the face, so great is it in souls. Whence Solomon: As faces differ from faces, so the hearts of men are diverse. But let each march according to his ensigns, lest he whose ensigns are lowly and despised march more loftily than the ensigns of his soul require. All who know letters know that there are twenty-four elements of letters if they have learned Greek, twenty-three if Latin, and from these they write everything. Yet the alpha which Paul has written has one sign, that which Peter has written another; whence also the handwritings written by the hands of each are known by their own signs and marks; and though the elements are the same, yet in the likeness of the letters there is an unlikeness of signs. Come then to the motions of the mind and of souls by which they are stirred to do something. Look at the handwritings and see how the soul of Paul set before itself chastity, and the soul of Peter. But there is a certain chastity proper to Peter, and another chastity of Paul, even if it seems the same. For the chastity of Paul is that which requires the body to be chastised and brought into subjection, lest perhaps, when I have preached to others, I myself should become a castaway. The chastity of the other does not fear this. Justice too has something proper in Paul, and has in Peter, and so the other virtues. If therefore in these names, which we have set as examples, it can be that, though they are one in spirit through the Spirit of God, there is yet some diversity in the property of the virtues themselves, how much more do the rest of men bear their own signs in the motions of souls and in the virtues of the soul.
06_marg63: RABANUS. All the children of Israel pitched their camps about the tabernacle, three on each side, so that nothing of them is over or lacking: Juda, Issachar, Zabulon, to the east; Ruben, Simeon, Gad, to the south; Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasses, to the west; Dan, Aser and Nephtali, to the north. The tabernacle signifies the Church, of the Old as well as of the New Testament. And the princes pitching their camps by the tabernacle signify the patriarchs or apostles, by whose prayers and doctrine the Church is fortified.

06_marg66: Mystically. The setting up or taking down of the tabernacle signifies the state of the Church, which is set up in believers and taken down in those who deny; in some it is raised by sacred orders, in others it is humbled by excommunication at the judgment of the priests.
06_marg67: RABANUS. The four quarters of the world, by which the camps of the children of Israel are arranged about the tabernacle, signify the calling together and ordering of the Church. For the east, where the entrance of the tabernacle is, expresses the beginning of conversion and confession and the receiving of baptism, and the first Church, which was first founded by the apostles in Jerusalem. To this quarter the tribes of Juda, Issachar and Zabulon are assigned, because the confessors of Christ have entrance into the dwelling of strength, where they labour for the eternal reward, through him who says: "I am the door. By me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved." "I am the light of the world." Of whom also Zachary: "The Orient from on high hath visited us" etc. But the south quarter, which the south side of the tabernacle faces, signifies the ancient people of God, which, receiving the light of the law, burned with the love of the Creator. There Ruben, Simeon and Gad pitched their camps, because the holy fathers sharpened the gaze of the mind to see the will of God, and were zealous for obedience, girded with the arms of justice, that they might be able to resist the noonday devil. But the north quarter, which the other side of the tabernacle faces, figures the multitude of the Gentiles, numb with the darkness and cold of unbelief until the coming of Christ; where Dan, Aser and Nephtali pitch their camps, because when the Jews had rejected the word of God, the Church, by just judgment multiplied and enlarged from the Gentiles, hopes for and desires true beatitude. But the west, which, receiving both walls of the tabernacle into itself, completes it, marks the fulfilment of the whole Church, which is perfected at the end of the world, when through the persecution of Antichrist the elect who have borne good fruit are proved, and, the wicked being handed over to the oblivion of everlasting death, the just are placed at the right hand of God to reign for ever. Whence Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasses well stand in this quarter. The Levites too are near the tabernacle, whom the other tribes surround on the four quarters, so that those who have the care of the tabernacle may securely give themselves to the divine services, fortified outwardly by their brethren against the enemies. Now too the ministers of the altar are so to be fortified and provided for on every side that they can securely fulfil the divine office.
06_marg68: This quarter, receiving both walls of the tabernacle into itself, completes it by joining them in itself, and signifies the consummation of the Church at the end of the world, when the elect shall be proved in the fruit of good works, the wicked handed over to the oblivion of death, the just placed at the right hand of God.
06_marg69: This quarter signifies the multitude of the Gentiles, numb with the cold of unbelief until Christ; but, the Jews being rejected by the judgment of God, enlarged in the Church, it awaits eternal beatitude.
06_marg70: THE PRIESTS THAT etc. RABANUS. Four sons of Aaron were chosen with him for the priesthood; but while two remained in their state, the others were burnt up by divine fire, because they offered strange fire. For although many, raised up in the Church from the four parts of the world, seem to bear the priesthood, only those persist in the ministry who preach the sound doctrine of both Testaments, tried by the fire of the Holy Ghost, and labour at whatever they can for the love of God and neighbour. But those who bring in a strange doctrine, made up by the teaching of worldly knowledge, and, kindled by worldly greed, perform the divine office, are consumed by the fire of divine vengeance.
06_marg71: AUGUSTINE. The alien who touches shall die. It is to be asked how he said in Leviticus: Whoever touches the tabernacle shall be sanctified, when here he says: The alien who touches shall die, meaning those who were not of the tribe of Levi. Or perhaps here "touches" means takes up for the duty of service, which he commanded to be owed to the tabernacle by the Levites alone? For of this he was speaking.
06_interl91: SEPTUAGINT: out of the midst of the children of Israel
06_interl92: although they are not firstborn; but with God they are judged firstborn not by the privilege of birth, but by the purpose of the mind.
06_marg72: AUGUSTINE. What is it that God assigns the Levites to himself for the firstborn of the children of Israel, so that when the firstborn of the people were numbered and were found more than the number of the Levites, they were redeemed with silver, five sicles being given for each, which was not done for the cattle? And since he willed the cattle of the Levites to be his for the firstborn of the cattle of Israel, how afterward did their firstborn, or those of their cattle, belong to God, when he commanded the unclean firstborn, or the human ones, to be exchanged for sheep? How were the sons of the Levites not reckoned for these later firstborn also? For the same tribe remained in their posterity, which could be reckoned for the later firstborn. Unless because it was just that God should now have as his own, as his own from his own, those born of the ones who already belonged to the Lord's portion, given for the firstborn who came out of Egypt; nor could they justly be reckoned for those firstborn who were owed to God thereafter. For from the whole people and from all the cattle of the people a portion was given to God for the firstborn: the Levites, namely, and their cattle; whatever these then begot was God's already; this could not be given by the people, since it already belonged to another. And therefore the firstborn owed thereafter had to be rendered to God, and the posterity of the Levites or of their cattle could not be reckoned for them.
06_marg73: I have taken the Levites out of the midst of the children of Israel for every firstborn etc. The Levites are taken for the firstborn, though they are not firstborn. For Levi is born third of Lia: first Ruben, second Simeon, third Levi. But with God those are not held firstborn who go before in body and birth, but those whom he himself judges, by the purpose of the mind, to be taken into the order of the firstborn. Jacob, later in birth, was judged the firstborn, and received the blessing of the first, procured by God through his father's blindness. For from the purpose of the heart, which was open to God, before they were born in this world or had done any good or evil, it was said: "Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated." The sons of Levi therefore are not firstborn according to the flesh, but are taken for the firstborn, so that it is more to be taken for a firstborn than to be born firstborn.
06_marg74: SEPTUAGINT: Out of the midst of the children of Israel etc. Levi is third among the sons of Israel; out of what midst, then, are the Levites taken? I find the Sunamitess answering the king of Israel confidently: I dwell in the midst of my people. And John saying of Christ: There hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not. I think, therefore, that he who has never turned aside to the right or to the left can be said to stand in the midst, "who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth"; and because he always stands, he is said to stand in the midst. But he who is his imitator, like the Sunamitess, is not said to stand, because at times he leans either to the right or to the left (for no one is clean from defilement, not even if his life be of one day); yet he is said to dwell in the midst of the people. The Levites therefore are taken out of the midst of the children of Israel. For the Levites are those who did not know their right and their left, but, following Moses, that is, the law of God, did not spare father or mother. And you too, if when temptation and the anger of sin come you do not lean to the right or to the left, nor transgress the law of God, but stand in the midst, fixed and steadfast, and do not bow your knees to sin, nor follow the head of a beast, that is, the image of folly, you will be taken out of the midst of the children of Israel and placed in the number of the firstborn.
06_marg75: Not whoever has opened the womb is worthy of the first rank; whence: "The wicked are alienated from the womb, they have gone astray from the womb: they have spoken false things." For how could anyone go astray from the way of God as soon as he came out of his mother's belly? Or how could a child newly born speak false things? It is necessary therefore to seek such a belly and womb as can fit "The wicked are alienated from the womb" etc. And that will be the womb which every firstborn opens who is sanctified to the Lord. The Lord opened the womb of Lia, which was shut, and she bore the patriarchs. Likewise Rachel also, that she might bear, she whose sight was keen and whose appearance comely. And in many places of Scripture you will find wombs opened; if you consider each of them in its place, you will find how the wicked go astray from the womb, and others, opening the womb, are sanctified in the order of the firstborn.
06_marg76: ORIGEN. Because the firstborn of Israel were not sanctified before the firstborn of the Egyptians were struck, and he sets the destruction of these as it were as the cause of the sanctification of those. Whence here too it is to be understood that there are certain firstborn among the Egyptians also, that is, among the contrary powers, as it were chosen in malice, and first among the demons; and unless these are struck and extinguished, the firstborn of the Israelites cannot be sanctified. And these my Lord Christ Jesus struck, who is the firstborn of every creature, who led away the principalities and powers, triumphing over them on the cross. For otherwise the sanctification of the firstborn could not come to us. And that he might give us the sanctifications of the firstborn, he was made the firstborn from the dead, that he might hold the primacy in all things, and take us, believers in his resurrection, for the firstborn, and place us in the order of the firstborn.
06_marg77: NUMBER THE SONS etc. ORIGEN. Let us review more attentively how the twelve tribes are distributed by threes into four parts, and stand in a fixed station on each quarter of heaven, and we shall find Juda on the east with Issachar and Zabulon; Ruben on the west with Simeon and Gad; on the south Ephraim with Benjamin and Manasses; on the north Dan with Nephtali and Aser. These being placed round about as it were at the four cardinal points of the earth, in their midst (as nearest to God) the Levites are set about the tabernacle of God: in the camp of Juda, which is on the east, Moses and Aaron; in the camp of Ruben, Gerson; in the camp of Benjamin, Caath; where Dan set his camp, Merari was placed. And so the sons of Levi seem to be in the midst of the children of Israel on every side round about, as it were set in among the others and resting upon them. Forget then a little the things of earth, and walk with the step of the mind above heaven itself. There seek the tabernacle of God, "whither the forerunner Jesus is entered for us", and now stands before the face of God, interceding for us. There seek the fourfold orders and the stations of the camps. There behold the Israelite hosts and the watches of the saints. There search out the mysteries of the firstborn. But I do not dare to go up there alone; let Paul go before, that he may show me the way. He, the greatest of the Apostles, knowing that there are many churches not only on earth but also in heaven (of which John enumerates seven), wishing to show besides a certain church of the firstborn, says to the Hebrews: For you are not come to a fire that may be touched and burning, but you are come to mount Sion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the multitude of angels praising, and to the church of the firstborn who are written in heaven. Moses therefore writes of the people of God divided into four camps on earth, the Apostle of four orders of saints in heaven, to each of which he says each one of us comes. For not all come to all, but some to mount Sion, and those somewhat better to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. More eminent than these come to the multitude of angels praising. But those who are above all these come to the church of the firstborn. Prepare yourself therefore, and strive as much as you can, if perhaps you may advance in acts, life, manners, faith and practices so that you can come to the church of the firstborn. If you are somewhat lower, come to the multitude of angels praising, or to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, or at least to mount Sion, that you may be saved in the mountain. Only do not stay on the earth, do not remain in the valleys, do not persevere in sunken and low things. So are the firstborn of Levi taken, who minister to God and his altar and celebrate the divine ministries of the tabernacle with perpetual watches.
06_marg78: Levi: added or taken up. This is the order of teachers, which, chosen from the world by the grace of God for the divine service, is united to the companies of angels. Whence: I have chosen you out of the world. And elsewhere: But they are as the angels of God in heaven.
06_marg79: The three sons of Levi signify the preachers of the holy Trinity, renowned in confession, wonderful in faith and hope and charity. For Gerson is interpreted stranger, Caath patience, or the grinding teeth, Merari bitter, or bitterness. For the minister of God knows himself a stranger and a pilgrim in the world, and is patient. He grinds the word of God with the tooth of discernment, according to the capacities of the hearers; and he shows that the world is bitter to him, and calls others back from pleasures. These are numbered from one month, because they ought to consecrate the beginning of life to God, lest, promoted after many crimes, they cause the name of God to be blasphemed. Whence: It behoveth a bishop to be blameless etc.
06_marg80: Where the day is closed, the stars set. In these it is signified that the ministers of the tabernacle ought to flee concupiscence, mortify carnal desires with the help of God, and await the last day and the end of labour, that, dead to the world and living to God, they may be able to say: "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ."
06_marg81: THESE BEHIND etc. The fitting order of the sons of Levi is shown, where, namely, those who are first in order keep the eastern quarter: Moses and Aaron with their sons, having the custody of the sanctuary in the midst of the children of Israel. The Caathites, from whom Moses and Aaron sprang, hold the southern quarter, under the care of Eleazar the priest, who is the elder of the sons of Aaron. After these the Gersonites on the western quarter under the care of Eleazar. Last the Merarites on the northern quarter, under the custody of Ithamar, the younger son of Aaron. In these it is morally expressed that the ministers of the Church ought diligently to keep their order, and not seek greater things than their own place requires.
06_marg82: ON THE SOUTH SIDE. This signifies that after the light of knowledge has been received, preachers ought to bestow on their neighbours with discernment the word of patience and consolation. Under Eleazar, that is, the help of God, according to that: "Unless the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it."
06_marg83: Last, the Merarites, under Ithamar (which is interpreted bitter, or where the palm is), were allotted the northern quarter, where icy dread endures. In which the ministers of the Church are warned not to grow numb with security; because although they have already entered the Church by the door of faith, have received the light of knowledge, and have mortified the desires of the flesh, yet they have not yet come to perfect sweetness, that is, to eternal beatitude. Something bitter remains: they must strive with him who sets his throne toward the north, whose hardness cannot be softened. Whence: His heart shall be as hard as a stone etc. But when he shall be overcome, the palm won, there is to be exulting and rejoicing.
06_marg84: The eastern quarter signifies the rising of faith, where Moses, which is interpreted taken out of the water, and Aaron, mountain of strength, will camp with their sons. For those who preside in the Church, to whom the keys of the heavenly kingdom are committed, ought to know the order of entrance and preach it to others. For each one must enter into the light of faith by the gate of confession to the water of baptism, that, taken out of the water, he may be a son of adoption, and, by the strength of constancy, beget sons of good work. Let him diligently guard the entrance of faith by which he entered the Church, lest he be cast out idle and unprofitable.
06_marg85: Fitly are the Levites entitled with the number twenty-two. For in this number the Hebrew elements are comprised, and, according to some, the books of the Old Testament. The ministers of God are warned by this prescription to live and teach according to the law of God, and in no way to go beyond it.
06_marg86: ORIGEN. There are many differences of numbers written of the children of Israel; but after the number of the children of Israel the Levites are numbered apart. For they had not been reviewed with them, and their number is set apart and special, by which they are all together reported to have been found twenty-two thousand, neither more nor less. After this the Lord commanded the firstborn of the children of Israel also to be numbered in the same order in which the Levites had been numbered, that is, from one month and upward, and they are found twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three. Do you think that by these things Moses wished to teach us only the history of the number, and enclosed no mystery in these diversities of numbers? The number twenty-two is often found in the divine Scriptures ascribed to principal causes. For the first elements of letters among the Hebrews are said to be twenty-two. From Adam to Jacob, from whose seed the twelve tribes take their beginning, twenty-two fathers are recorded. They also say that the kinds of all the creatures of God are gathered within the number twenty-two. For this reason, then, the Levites, that is, those who serve God, and the firstborn of the children of Israel are entitled with this sacred number. And that two hundred and seventy-three are added among the children of Israel does not seem idle: for the generation of the human race in the flesh (as those skilled in such things assert) is contained in the womb for nine months. But it is said not to be moved to birth before three days of the tenth month pass. And so two hundred and seventy-three indicates those days which are gathered from nine months and three days of the tenth month, and together they make these two hundred and seventy-three days, by which entrance into this world is given to the human race. And so in twenty-two the sum of all creatures together is gathered by mystical reckonings; and in those which are found over and above among the firstborn of Israel, the mystery of human generation is also set forth.
06_marg87: Mystically. Whoever wishes to consecrate the beginning of his conversation, will or working to God ought diligently to guard the five senses of the body, lest through wantonness he flow away into error or unclean desires. But according to the sicle of the sanctuary, which is twenty obols, that is, according to the doctrine of the decalogue, which consists in the two precepts of charity, let him refer all his works to the house of the high priest and his sons.
06_marg88: TAKE etc. ORIGEN. Since the sons of Levi are divided into three orders, each order is reckoned under the three names of the princes, and even among them certain differences are ascribed, not without mysteries. For the order of the sons of Caath is placed first, because from it came Moses and Aaron, to whom the height of the priesthood is committed. For from it Amram is born, from whom Moses and Aaron are born. The second order is Gerson, who indeed is first in birth. For the Scripture says: And the sons of Levi: Gerson, Caath and Merari. But from the sons of Caath two orders again are drawn, and those who descend from Aaron are bound over to the priesthood, while the remaining part ministers to the priests; and therefore the offices of the Levites are divided into four parts, so that Aaron and his sons perform the priesthood, the rest of the people of Caath carry the holy of holies on their shoulders. And the things which pertain to the tabernacle of the testimony, or to its courts and skins, or also the coverings and whatever is less hard and light to carry, the sons of Gerson see to. But the pillars of the tabernacle, its sockets and bars, the sons of Merari carry. Therefore the Scripture says pointedly: That the strength of Merari may be reviewed. For strength is needed for carrying such loads. But Paul, looking with the eye of the mind now free and unveiled, and casting off the veil of the Old Testament, says: That the former people served in such constructions as patterns and the shadow of heavenly things. Consider, therefore, whether these four orders of the camps may not be the pattern and shadow of those four orders which Paul, writing to the Hebrews, enumerated in heaven. And again to the four Israelite orders of the camps add the fourfold orders of the Levites; which we do not so much explain as touch upon, and point out to purer senses and those free from worldly things.
06_marg89: Another reading: Take the number of the sons of Caath etc. Behold, another order of numbers is introduced. The sons of Levi have already been numbered from one month and upward. But now the sons of Levi are numbered from the twenty-fifth year, but not, as in the others, "and upward", but until the fiftieth year; and this becomes a special and chosen number. And to these aforesaid is added: Every one that goes forth to minister at the works of the tabernacle of the testimony. These are they who are numbered with a better and special number. For as it was said among the children of Israel: Every one that goes forth to war of the children of Israel, so here: every one that goes forth to the ministry, to do the works in the tabernacle of the testimony.
06_marg90: ORIGEN. The tabernacle of the testimony is all the saints who are reckoned under the testimony of God. In this tabernacle some are higher in merits and grace; and of these some are called the candlestick, perhaps the Apostles, who enlighten those who come to God; and others, who show the light of knowledge and doctrine to those who enter this tabernacle of God; others are the table, who feed with the bread of God the souls that hunger and thirst after justice; others the altar of incense, who give themselves to prayers and fasts day and night in the temple of God. But those to whom God has entrusted hidden mysteries are called the ark of the testament of God. And those who with all confidence, by prayers and supplications, make God propitious again to men and intercede for the sins of the people are the propitiatory. Those who have merited the multitude of knowledge and abundant riches in the knowledge of God can be understood as the Cherubim. For Cherubim is interpreted fulness of knowledge. But all these, who are designated by each of these things, must be carried, and on the shoulders. As I think, the angels, who are appointed for the sake of those who receive the inheritance of salvation, carry them. And when this tabernacle is dissolved and we begin to enter into those holy places and to go on to the place of promise, those who are truly holy and are held among the holy of holies go with the angels carrying them, and until the tabernacle of God rests they are carried on the shoulders and lifted up in the hands. Whence: For he hath given his angels charge over thee, that in their hands they shall bear thee up etc. Which the devil thought was to be understood of the Saviour, but, blinded by malice, he did not understand the mystical words. For the Saviour did not need angels that he might not stumble. But God gives his angels charge for his people, that it may not dash its foot against a stone. Hence Paul says: Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be taken up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ, into the air. They shall be taken up, therefore, by the angels, who have been thoroughly cleansed and made light of sins. So the pillars of the tabernacle and the courts and the other things which Scripture relates are carried by certain ones, not by Israelites, but by Levites.
06_interl98: He sets out the works of the sons of Caath in the midst of the sons of Levi according to their peoples in the tabernacle of the testimony.
06_marg91: Lest perhaps some see it uncovered and die. For he is destroyed who touches the ineffable sacraments, unless he has been promoted to the degree of the priesthood by merits and knowledge.
06_marg92: Seven kinds are numbered which are commanded to be covered. First, that the most precious of all, the ark of the testament, be covered with a veil, and also covered over with a violet skin; and another covering of violet is added on top. Second, the table is covered. Third, the candlestick. Fourth, the golden altar. Fifth, the vessels of the ministry. Sixth, the covering of the altar is put on with certain coverings. Seventh, the laver also is covered, and none of these is left bare. Then it is added: Destroy not the people of Caath out of their tribe; that they might know, namely, that they would be destroyed if they put their hands to move these things before each of them had been covered by the priests. Let us return, then, to the tabernacle of the church of the living God, and see how these several things ought to be observed by the priests of Christ. If anyone is truly a priest, to whom the sacred vessels, that is, the secrets of the mysteries of wisdom, are committed, let him learn how he ought to keep these within the veil of conscience and not easily bring them out in public. Or if the matter requires that he bring them out and hand them on to the less skilled, let him not bring them out bare, and not show them open and wholly exposed; otherwise he commits murder and destroys the people. For everyone is destroyed who touches the secret and ineffable sacraments not yet promoted by merits and knowledge to the degree of the priesthood. For to the sons of Aaron alone, that is, to the priests, is it granted to see the ark itself, and the table, and the candlestick, and the things said above, bare. Let the others see them covered, nay rather carry them veiled on their shoulders.
06_marg93: The sons of Aaron, the priests, to whom it is granted to see all things bare and open.
06_marg94: THE LOAVES ALWAYS. AUGUSTINE. And the loaves which shall always be on it. Not of course always the same ones, but ones like them, because those were taken away and fresh ones were set each day, so long as the table was not left without loaves. Therefore he said: which shall always be on it, that is, because there are always loaves, not because those same are always there.
06_marg95: Another reading: And upon the golden altar they shall cover a garment of violet, and they shall cover it with a covering of violet skin. This expression might seem one which the Latin translators were willing to render as absurd and incomplete, that is: upon the golden altar they shall cover a garment of violet; as though it ought to have been said: and the golden altar they shall cover with a garment of violet; not: they shall cover a garment of violet. This seems to signify that the garment of violet itself was covered from elsewhere. But to me it seems not so much a kind of idiom as a somewhat obscure sense. For this can be understood: Upon the golden altar they shall cover a garment of violet; so that he commanded the garment of violet itself to be covered with something else, the garment being already upon the altar; as though he briefly took in both: that the altar was to be covered with the garment of violet, and the garment of violet to be covered with another covering. He then added with what he wished the garment of violet to be covered, when he put: And they shall cover it with a covering of violet skin.
06_marg96: THEN SHALL THE SONS ENTER etc. ORIGEN. Though they are not priests, yet because they are next to them they can carry these things on their shoulders; but the others put their loads and ministries on wagons. For when wagons were offered by each tribe, the sons of Merari received four of them, and the sons of Gerson two. But those who are better do not receive wagons. See then what kind of division there is in the divine offices and ministries, and how the things that are sanctified are not carried by dumb animals, but they must be rational men who carry on their shoulders the vessels by which the holy of holies are ministered. But the heavier and harder things are laid not so much on rational as on dumb animals, and among these too there is some difference. For those who keep the harder and heavier ministries have more animals. Four wagons are given to the sons of Merari, but to the sons of Gerson, who were next to the sons of Caath, only two. Whence it is shown that for the harder and coarser works there are more who serve as it were like animals. But to the things which are seen to by rational men, few of the less instructed come. For to those things which are mystical and secret (they lie open to the priests alone), not only does no animal man come, but not even those who have some exercise and learning, yet have not yet ascended by merits and life to the priestly grace. And they not only see these through a glass and in a dark manner, but receive them covered and veiled and carry them on their shoulders, so that they know them more by act than by revelation of knowledge. Let us not, then, show ourselves such, we who are made worthy of the order of the priesthood, lest heavy burdens be laid on us as on irrational beings; but let us be assigned to priestly offices as rational and holy. For we are a holy nation and a kingly priesthood; only let us, matching the grace received with the merits of life, be held worthy of the holy ministry, so that when we depart from this life we may merit to be taken up among the priests of God, and, ministering to the ark of the testament, namely in the hidden ministries, may behold the glory of God with unveiled face and enter the holy land, whose inheritance our Lord Jesus Christ will grant us.
06_marg97: ORIGEN. Destroy not the people of Caath etc. Understand first the setting up of the tabernacle, and the holy of holies, which are separated from the holies by a veil set between, which it is not lawful to see except for the priests alone. Then, how, when the children of Israel move camp, the tabernacle is taken down, and Aaron and his sons the priests, within the holy of holies, cover each thing with its coverings, and, leaving them covered there, bring in the sons of Caath, who are assigned to this office, and make them lift on their shoulders what the priestly hand has covered. Therefore it is said by the Lord: Destroy not the people of Caath out of their tribe; as though they would be destroyed in this, if they had touched the holy of holies bare and open, which it was not even lawful to look upon. If anyone among those who minister to God is worthy to grasp and see the divine mysteries which the rest cannot see, he is understood to be Aaron and his sons, who can enter into things which others may not approach. To him alone the ark of the testament lies open and revealed, and the urn having the manna. He considers the propitiatory, the Cherubim, the holy table, the candlestick of light, and the altar of incense; he, namely, who gives his labour to the word of God and the mysteries of wisdom, and is free for God alone in the holies. Let him know, indeed, that it is not lawful for him to open them to those to whom it is not lawful, but to hand them over covered to the others, less capable, to be carried on their shoulders. For when, from mystical words, perfect teachers enjoin works on the peoples, and the people fulfil what is commanded but do not understand the reason, the holy of holies are carried covered upon the shoulders. Moses understood what the true circumcision was, what the true pasch, what the true new moons, the true sabbaths, and yet he foreshadowed them through the forms of bodily things. And though he knew that Christ was to be sacrificed as the true pasch, he commanded a bodily sheep to be sacrificed at the pasch; and the feast to be kept with unleavened loaves of flour, though he knew the feast was to be kept with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. These and the like were the holy of holies, which, when Moses handed them to the others to be carried, that is, to be fulfilled in things and works, he yet handed over veiled in common speech. And the shoulders signify works.
06_marg98: LET NOT OTHERS BY ANY CURIOSITY etc. ORIGEN. In the observances of the Church too there are things which all must do, yet the reason does not lie open to all. For that we bend the knee in praying, and, of all the quarters of heaven, pray turned to the east alone, is not easy for anyone to explain. Of the Eucharist too, which is to be received, or of the rite in which it is performed, or of the things done in baptism, the words, gestures, orders, questions and answers, who would easily explain the reason? Yet we carry these (though veiled) on our shoulders, when we fulfil them as we received them handed down and commended by the great high priest and his sons; unless there is among us an Aaron or a son of Aaron, to whom it is granted to look upon these bare; yet let them know that these are to be veiled by them, unless reason requires that they be given to the others and brought out into work.
06_marg99: Thirty, which is composed of ten multiplied three times, signifies the integrity of faith and the perfection of work, without which no one ought to approach the divine ministries. Joseph at thirty took up the government of Egypt. And David the kingdom, which he completed at seventy, that is, worthy of everlasting rest. And Ezechiel merited the gifts of prophecy. And because through faith adversities must be borne with long-suffering and rewards hoped for on high, the height of the ark or of the temple and the length of the tabernacle are measured at thirty cubits.
06_marg100: FIFTY etc. ORIGEN. In this book too, concerning the spoils of the enemies, some who did not go forth to war offer to God as gifts the fiftieth portion, and some the five hundredth. In Genesis too, where God was treating of pardon for the Sodomites, if perhaps they could come to forgiveness, Abraham, conscious of such mysteries, began to entreat the Lord for pardon from the number fifty, saying: If there be fifty found in the city, wilt thou not spare the city for the sake of the fifty? etc. The Levites therefore must work in the holy things until fifty years; the lower ones, works; the better ones, the works of works. And the higher of these serve in the spiritual offices, and enter into the holy of holies, and there cover what is to be covered, and hand it to the sons of Caath to be carried on their shoulders and borne by their hands.
06_marg101: ALL THAT GO IN etc. ORIGEN. It is said of the Levites that they work from the twenty-fifth year and upward, until the fiftieth year. Every one, he says, that goes forth to the work of works, and to the works that are carried, of the tabernacle of the testimony etc. Note the distinction of words. Where he speaks of the works of the children of Israel, he did not say works of works, but works only; but where of the offices of the Levites, he said works of works. For as there are holies and holy of holies, so there are works and works of works. Whence it seems to me that Moses, where he perceived that there were certain visible works in which a mystical understanding was present, called these not only works but works of works. But those which he understood to be common and of the present time he named only works. There are therefore works of works (as in the present reading, or in Exodus and in other places, they are commanded under hidden mysteries, to be fulfilled partly in the present and partly in the future), which are commanded to be handed over not to anyone, but to the Levites alone, namely from the twenty-fifth year to the fiftieth. Because in twenty-five the perfection of the senses is declared, five being counted five times. Which indicates that he is called to the works of works to be carried out in the ministry who is found perfect, with his senses multiplied and purified on every side.
06_marg102: ORIGEN. And the fiftieth year signifies remission and pardon. For the fiftieth year is that which among the Hebrews is called the jubilee, in which remission is made of possessions, servitude and debt. And the fiftieth day after the pasch is handed down in the law as a feast. And the Lord in the Gospel, bringing in debtors when he taught the parable of remission and pardon, says that one was bound for fifty and the other for five hundred pence. And fifty and five hundred are kindred numbers. For fifty tens make five hundred.
06_marg103: This number is hallowed in another way also. For if to seven weeks the perfection of one number be added, they make fifty days. And if to seventy weeks the completion of one ten be added, they make five hundred.
06_interl101: of the Church; lest they defile the life of the innocent
06_marg104: Allegorically. RABANUS. The lepers are the heretics, defiled with various spots of sins, not having a uniform colour of doctrine or faith; nor do they hide their unskilfulness, but show it. But there is no false doctrine which does not at times mix in some true things. True things therefore mixed with false in any disputation or narration of anyone, appearing as it were in the colour of one body, signify leprosy, which varies human bodies with true and false patches of colour as it were.
06_interl103: who, namely, burns with the wantonness of carnal desires
06_interl106: who, namely, follows the impiety and the examples of those dead in sins, and is stained with their filth
06_marg105: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. A MAN OR WOMAN etc. RABANUS. In this chapter we are admonished that if we offend in anything through negligence, we should wash it away by confession and penance and restore the loss. And if we have brought loss on a neighbour, let us repent before him and restore the loss. But if he does not survive, let us make satisfaction to the Lord by confessing, repenting and giving alms.
06_marg106: Another reading: Man or woman, whoever shall have done any of all human sins, and despising shall have despised and offended, that soul shall declare the sin which it sinned, and shall restore the trespass: the principal, and he shall add the fifths of it over it, and shall render it to him against whom he offended. But if the man have no kinsman, so that he may render the trespass to him, the trespass which is rendered to the Lord shall be the priest's, besides the ram of propitiation, by which he shall make entreaty in it for him. Here those sins are to be understood whose commission is in such things as could be restored with money. For he would not otherwise say how they are to be restored, unless they had been of pecuniary loss. For he commands the principal and the fifths to be restored, that is, the whole of whatever it is, and its fifth part, besides the ram which was to be offered in sacrifice to expiate the trespass. And he commands that what is restored be the priest's, that is, the principal itself and the fifth, if there is no kinsman of him against whom it was committed. Where it is understood that what is to be the priest's is then to be rendered to the Lord, if he who suffered the loss does not survive, nor his kinsman, that is, his heir; but of the man himself he said nothing. But when he says: If he have no kinsman, he briefly hints that his kinsman is then sought if he himself is not there. And if there is no kinsman either, it shall be restored to the Lord, lest the offence remain unpunished. Yet it is not to go into the sacrifice, but to be the priest's: so indeed the words of Scripture are to be distinguished. But if the man have no kinsman, so that he may render the trespass to him: for what he added, "to him", belongs to the idiom. Or perhaps he said "to him" meaning what pertains to him, that is, what he himself possesses. Then follows: The trespass which is rendered to the Lord shall be the priest's. And he says trespass when the thing is rendered which was taken away through the trespass.
06_interl110: that is, with the same sense of the body by which we brought evil, let us strive to render good things
06_marg107: THEY SHALL RESTORE THE PRINCIPAL ITSELF etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked how in Exodus we read: If anyone steal a calf or a sheep, he ought to restore five calves or four sheep, if he has killed or sold it; but if what he took be found alive with him, double is to be restored; whereas here he commands the principal and the fifth to be restored. Which is far even from the double; how much more from the fourfold or fivefold. Unless perhaps, because here he says: Man or woman, whoever shall have done any of all human sins, he wished human sins to be understood as sins of ignorance. For it can happen that through negligence a man carries over another's property into his own, which is a sin for this reason, that if he had paid careful attention it would not have been committed. And these he wished to be restored with the principal and the fifth, not fined as thefts. For if we understand here thefts and frauds which are committed not through ignorance but with the intent of stealing and defrauding, and therefore called human because they are done against men, then (unless I am mistaken) this will be the solution of the question: that he who did it does not render fourfold because he is not caught or convicted, but, when people do not know by whom it was done, or whether it was done, he himself declares his trespass. For when he had said: Man or woman, whoever shall have done any of all human sins, and despising shall have offended, that is, has committed these things in contempt, he added: That soul shall declare its sin which it sinned, and shall restore the trespass, the principal and the fifths of it. Perhaps, then, only so much, because he declared it; and therefore he was not to be punished with the penalty with which a thief caught or convicted must be punished.
06_marg108: The offering of the ram signifies the passion of Christ, in which we trust above all, because without him we can do nothing. He is the priest who reconciles us to the Father by the offering of his flesh. Therefore we offer our gifts to him, by whose intercession we may merit pardon.
06_interl113: of good will, of words and of works
06_interl114: the true Israelites, who look upon God with the mind
06_interl116: Who offered himself for us of his own accord.
06_marg109: To Christ, namely, to whom it is said: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech." Reserving all things, namely, to his judgment, lest perhaps one judge an uncertain matter. Whence: "Judge not before the time, until the Lord come" etc.
06_interl119: of Christ, because whatever is offered in the Church pertains to his dignity and grace.
06_interl121: the one subject, who ought to have obeyed his master in all things, as a wife her husband
06_interl125: namely, be convicted by judicial order
06_interl127: namely, in an open act of heresy
06_interl128: namely, the zeal of justice and of the lost sheep
06_marg110: RABANUS. The barley meal signifies the knowledge of the old law, which is well compared to barley, because as barley, cleansed from the chaff with great labour, is brought to meal, so the letter of the law, ground by the millstone of discernment, gives forth the meal of the spiritual sense; and rightly the tenth part of a measure is offered, because the law consists of ten commandments, of which any commandment is a tenth part, against which the wicked wife is said to have acted. The woman therefore is offered to the priest with the oblation of the tenth part when she is reserved for the judgment of Christ, according to the law divinely given, to be condemned or freed.
06_interl131: of flattery or of indiscreet mercy
06_marg111: RABANUS. etc. It is not fitting that the impenitent be anointed with the oil of flattery or of indiscreet mercy, nor with the frankincense of superfluous praise or of disordered prayer; but that vice be pursued earnestly and in order with the zeal of justice according to the Lord's precept.
06_interl132: because she is kept to be judged by divine judgment
06_interl133: the divine wisdom, namely, contained in the lowly letter of the Law
06_marg112: To this water the priest mixes a little earth from the pavement of the tabernacle, when by the decree of Christ the remembrance of the patriarchs, prophets and apostles is found brought in.
06_marg113: AND THE PRIEST SHALL WRITE etc. Because, namely, the punishment of sinners is set out in holy Scripture. And whoever drinks it piously and faithfully, dreading the punishments of sinners which are told in it and abstaining from sins, for him the most bitter water will become salvation. But he who despises it, his belly swelling, his thigh shall rot, and he shall be a curse and an example, because he will be punished by the just judgment of God, and his desires and acts will be to him a reproach.
06_marg114: AND HE SHALL GIVE HER TO DRINK: that her sin may be made manifest, either here for correction or in the future for damnation. For there is nothing hidden that shall not be revealed. Hence the Lord says: The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge you in the last day.
06_interl136: This is done when the confession of the holy Trinity is found in the sacrifice of the Law, which is worthily offered on the altar of faith.
06_interl144: by falling back into the pleasure of past vice
06_interl145: lest they grow pale with abstinence for vainglory
06_marg115: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. FROM WINE AND FROM EVERY etc. ISIDORE. In the twelfth station, that is, Sinai, the Nazarites are commanded not to drink or eat wine and strong drink and everything that can make drunk. In the Proverbs too it is commanded that the mighty and the wrathful drink no wine, lest they forget wisdom. In the Nazarites the life of the continent is marked; to them wine is forbidden, that is, wantonness; and strong drink, that is, every earthly pleasure. For strong drink is made from diverse kinds, as pleasure from the diverse passion of vices. For those do not drink wine but drink strong drink who, to deceive men, feign certain shadows and images of virtues. They eat dried grapes who stain themselves with the pallor of abstinence before human eyes, that they may take glory from men. They drink vinegar who after holiness of life slip back into the oldness of past vices and delight in the corruption of the old wickedness.
06_marg116: That is: he shall keep neither guile nor malice in his mind, lest, namely, the hair of the head, that is, the thought of the mind, be defiled; but let him keep innocence to the end of life. For otherwise the vow will not be acceptable. But he that shall persevere shall be saved.
06_marg117: That is: he shall not imitate one dead in sins, nor enter the way of his iniquity, lest he lose his labour. For not he who begins, but he who finishes, shall be crowned.
06_marg118: That is: let no carnal affection draw him back; every person, every dignity, every kinship is to be set after the service of Christ.
06_marg119: That is: the grace of the Holy Ghost is poured forth in his heart. Whence: Grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, whereby you are all sealed.
06_marg120: That is: let him persevere to the end without the defilement of sin and trespass.
06_marg121: That is: if he has wished to imitate one defiled by mortal sin, and has gone down as far as consent, let him know that his continence must needs be defiled and his head shaved, that is, his mind cleansed from wicked thought and harmful delight.
06_marg122: In the time, namely, of compunction, when he knows he has offended, let him strive at once to amend himself, and always fear a like fall.
06_interl147: by which the time of the resurrection is signified
06_marg123: The turtles signify chastity, the young pigeons simplicity. He therefore who wishes to come to the resurrection of the good, let him offer to the true priest, that is, Christ, chastity of mind and body, and simplicity in the catholic faith, through which he enters the Church, that he may be expiated through the help of so great a high priest.
06_interl148: he will make him groan, namely, for sins through fear of hell
06_interl149: that he may sigh, namely, with desire of eternal life
06_marg124: Our advocate with the Father. Or because he will make us pray, according to that: "The Spirit asketh for us with unspeakable groanings."
06_interl150: the mind rescued from carnal desire
06_interl151: that all may be holy and spotless
06_interl152: an innocent life for a criminal one, simplicity for craftiness
06_marg125: Let him presume nothing of his former conversation, but trust in the grace of God alone, by whose gift he receives pardon and everlasting rest.
06_marg126: When the just man shall turn himself away from his justice and do iniquity, all his justices shall be forgotten.
06_marg127: THIS IS THE LAW etc. After the lawgiver has instructed the Nazarite how he is to be cleansed if his consecration is defiled by the dead, he adds how, after the vow is completed, he should present himself to the Lord with an oblation to give thanks; mystically hinting that the life of the continent, with the oblation of work and cleanness of heart, will please the Lord in a good end.
06_marg128: He offers this who puts all his hope in his immolation, of whom it is said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sins of the world. He offers him for a holocaust when for his love, by mortifying the flesh, he consecrates to the Lord his whole life kindled with the ardour of charity.
06_marg129: Another reading: And he shall offer his gift to the Lord, a lamb of a year without blemish for holocausts, and one ewe lamb of a year without blemish "into sin". This some would not translate, as though avoiding an unusual expression, and said "for sin", not "into sin", although the sense in that expression is not to be disturbed. For "into sin" was said because what was offered for sin was called sin. Whence: Him that knew no sin, for us he hath made sin, that is, a sacrifice for sin. As therefore the lamb "into holocaust", so also the ewe lamb "into sin", so that the animal itself was sin, that is, a sacrifice for sin; as of the ram, which follows, he says "into saving", which he makes plain afterward by repeating. For he also says "for sin" what he had said before "into sin"; and "this sacrifice of saving" what he had said before "into saving".
06_marg130: Tropologically. He offers a lamb for a holocaust who shows God simplicity of heart with the devotion of charity; a ewe, who shows an example of innocence; and a ram as a peace victim, when he rules himself well in the way of God and subjects the rebellious flesh to the command of the soul.
06_marg131: He offers a ewe for sin who faithfully believes that Christ, the innocent, was offered for the sin of the human race.
06_marg132: This is done when he trusts that he is the one who by the dispensation of the flesh made peace between things heavenly and earthly, emptying every principality and power: whom "God hath exalted, and hath given him a name which is above every name" etc.
06_interl157: of gladness, the grace of the Holy Ghost
06_marg133: The old law, dictated by the Holy Ghost and tempered for human profit.
06_marg134: Without leaven: because spiritual grace lies open in the law and in the Gospel to those who understand rightly.
06_marg135: Presenting the merit and labour of each, his meditation and observance of the law, in the sight of God by rewarding it, at the entrance of the heavenly life, the contest of good work being finished.
06_marg136: BUT THE RAM etc. Showing him, namely, worthy of the reward of everlasting rest, as the prince and best leader of himself or of others, who has ruled and led himself well in the path of God's commandments, according to the doctrine of the Scriptures and the grace of the spiritual gifts.
06_interl160: the mind, namely, of one abstaining from superfluous thoughts
06_marg137: What is it that the Nazarites grow their hair, except that through a life of great continence the thoughts of presumption grow? But what is it that, the devotion being completed, the Nazarite is commanded to shave his head and put the hair in the fire of the sacrifice, except that we then reach the height of perfection when we so conquer outward vices that we also cut off superfluous thoughts from the mind? To burn these in the fire of the sacrifice is to kindle them with the flame of divine love, so that the whole heart burns in the love of God, and, burning up superfluous thoughts, consumes as it were the hair of the Nazarite by the perfection of devotion.
06_interl163: by revealing the obscure mysteries of the Scriptures
06_marg138: The strength, namely, of work, boiled and proved in the fire of tribulation, the high priest makes his holy one offer to God the Father.
06_marg139: AND ONE WAFER: helping him, namely, by the gift of the Holy Ghost to complete in work the knowledge of the law.
06_interl165: that is: when he has stripped him of the corruption of the flesh and freed him from the burden of cares.
06_marg140: HE SHALL ELEVATE: he will present to the Father, namely, the good things which the continent man has wrought, and will have them rewarded with everlasting reward.
06_marg141: SHALL BELONG TO THE PRIEST: because whatever the Nazarite has willed well and completed in deed pertains to his glory. For he it is who worketh in us both to will and to accomplish.
06_interl167: because our wisdom is his own gift
06_marg142: That is: after right intention, discreet promise, perfection of work, retribution of reward.
06_marg143: DRINK WINE: to drink in the spiritual gift fully and freely; whence: "Thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure."
06_interl172: which, namely, he will do of his own accord
06_marg144: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. Moses signifies the law, Aaron the priesthood, and his sons the order of the Church. The Lord therefore teaches through the law the order of priests how they should build up the people by preaching and strengthen them by frequent prayer and blessing.
06_marg145: Moses has a manifold signification.
