But we, if we slander, shall remain leprous until the end of the world's week, that is, until the resurrection, unless while it is the time for penance we are corrected, turned to Jesus, and supplicating him through penance.
06_marg260: RABANUS. Note that Pharan is not the special name of a station, but of a wilderness containing several stations, as is shown in the catalogue of the stations, when it is said: The children of Israel departing from Haseroth camped in Rethma, then in Remmonphares; so that all the stations in order, as far as Asiongaber and as far as the thirty-second station, are comprised under the name of the wilderness of Pharan. From Rethma, therefore, which was fifteenth in order, to the thirty-second, these are contained.
06_marg261: PHARAN is interpreted "visible mouth", in which can be understood that the Word was made flesh, and the invisible was made visible; and this is signified, that after the end and perfection of all things that were to be done toward that people had come, then it passed over and came to him whom, the Word made flesh, it did not believe before.
06_marg262: SEND MEN, etc. RABANUS. Twelve spies are sent to the holy land. The cluster is carried on wood, where the passion of Christ too is briefly shown. The people of the Jews murmurs, dreading the onset of the giants. There is fighting against Amalec and the Chanaanite, and, God willing it, it is overcome. It hears what sacrifices it ought to perform in the holy land. Dathan and Abiron and the sons of Core rise up against Moses and Aaron, and are swallowed by a chasm of the earth. Between the dead and the living the high priest goes in, armed with the censer, and the running wrath of God is stopped by the voice of the priest. The rod of Aaron brings forth both flower and leaves, and the dryness grown green is consecrated for an everlasting memorial. Not yet was there a temple or keepers of the temple, not yet had priests and Levites offered sacrifices, and the mystic word describes their portions. A red heifer is burned for a holocaust, and its ash is a sprinkling of expiation.
06_interl261: the land, namely, to be contemplated
06_marg263: AUGUSTINE. Another text: And he said to them: Go up from this wilderness, and you shall see the land, what it is, and the people that dwells upon it, whether it is strong or weak, whether they are few or many. He is understood to have explained what he had said, whether it is powerful or weak, that is, whether they are few or many. For how could they, looking out from a mountain, perceive the strength of human forces? There can also be another sense, much more fitting to the truth. When he says: You shall go up into the mountain, he spoke of the very land which they wished to explore. For they could not easily be understood as spies unless they searched out everything as travellers. For if we suppose that they viewed and explored the land from the top of a mountain, how could they inquire into all the things that Moses commanded? How could they enter the cities which they are read to have entered, and take the cluster from that valley, on account of which it is called the valley of the Cluster? The land, therefore, is explored in itself, because it was itself what was to be explored, and there was there a certain lower place, from which valley the cluster was taken.
06_interl262: of Christ, who hung from the wood of the cross
06_marg264: WHICH THEY CARRIED, etc. ISIDORE. Two bring the cluster on wood from the land of promise, because Christ hanging on the wood of the cross, promised to the Gentiles, was born according to the flesh of the land of his mother Mary. The two bearers who walked under the burden of the cluster are the two peoples: of whom the first, the Jewish, is blind and turned away, ignorant of the grace of him who hangs, and weighed down by the burden of him who is hung, to whom as judge it shall be subjected. Whence: "Let their eyes be darkened that they see not: and bow down their back always." But he who came behind bore, that is signified, the people of the Gentiles, which, believing and having Christ before its eyes, always sees him whom it carries, and follows as a servant his lord and a disciple his master. According to that: If any man will come after me, let him take up his cross and follow me. This is the cluster which, by the crushing of the cross, poured out the wine of his blood shed for our salvation, and gave the Church to drink of the pressed cup of his passion. Whom, in the pomegranate, mother Church followed with the companion grace of the gift; having within herself by the number of the seeds the multitude of peoples, by the redness, that is, the seal of the blood of Christ shining; having also the divers charisms of the Holy Ghost. Judging themselves unworthy of these, the unbelieving did not merit to receive the land of the flesh of Christ, flowing with milk and honey, which his servants, that is, the Christians, obtained through faith. Of whose doctrine it is said: "How sweet are thy words to my palate" etc. They brought the fig with the cluster from the land of promise, that is, the image of the law with the figure of Christ. For of him it is said: My beloved is as a cluster of Cyprus; because neither can Christ be without the law, nor the law without Christ.
06_interl264: by which the Church is figured, which signifies Christ
06_marg265: Which signify the law, because neither is Christ without the law, nor the law without Christ.
06_marg266: ISIDORE. The spies, who, sent to a fruitful land, frightened the people so that they did not believe they could possess the promised land, signify the scribes and Pharisees. For as those were sent by Moses carefully to consider the fertility of the soil, so these were sent by the law and the prophets, that by searching the Scriptures they might watch for the Lord's coming, in which was the land, that is, the holy flesh, in which they could obtain the kingdom of God, and the abundance of spiritual fruits, and eternal life. But as those frightened the people by despair so that they did not believe, though God promised, so these persuaded the people of the Jews not to believe in Christ, longing to return to the Egypt of this world, rejecting the manna of faith, and seeking the black pots of sins, and the rejected onions of blasphemies, and the melons of vices and lusts withering in corruption.
06_marg267: RABANUS. The wilderness of Pharan contains eighteen stations. At the last of these the spies returned to Moses and reported what they had seen, carrying the cluster with pomegranates and figs. And in what follows it is written: Departing from Asiongaber they camped in the desert of Sin. This is Cades, which is interpreted not "holy", as many think, but "changed" or "transferred" etc. At this station Mary dies and is buried, and because of the waters of contradiction Moses and Aaron offended the Lord and are forbidden to cross the Jordan.
06_interl265: of the doctrine of Christ it is said: "How sweet are thy words to my palate! more than honey to my mouth."
06_interl266: who was of the tribe of Juda
06_marg268: ORIGEN. What is this land, holy indeed and good, but inhabited by the wicked? Who are the enemies who dwell in the land of the saints? How are they to be cast out, that these may succeed and dwell there? The Gospels promise the saints the kingdom of heaven. And the Apostle says: "But our conversation is in heaven." In heaven, therefore, is the inheritance promised to the saints. Do you think, then, that there is now no inhabitant there who must be expelled? From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, etc. Unless there were some to be expelled from it, it would never be said that the kingdom of heaven is to be seized by violence. And unless we had a battle with some, the Apostle would not say: "Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood" etc. Of these too it is said: My sword hath been inebriated in heaven. It is necessary, therefore, that you conquer the spiritual wickednesses which are said to be in the heavenly places, who are the true Chanaanites, and expel them from the heavenly places, that you may dwell in their stead. Know, however, that there are giants. Everyone who resists God is called a giant, which those principally do. Whence: Who shall take the spoils from the giant? And elsewhere: No man can enter into the house of a strong man and rifle his goods, unless he first bind the strong man. By comparison, therefore, of human nature and demonic nature, we are locusts. Especially if our faith is doubtful and unbelief terrifies us, they will truly be giants and we locusts. But if we follow Jesus and believe his words, they will be as nothing in our sight. For he exhorts us, and says: If God loves us, he will bring us into this land, because it is good and its fruit wonderful. The figure therefore went before in the fathers; it is fulfilled in us. They cast out the giants and obtained their land, all the land of Judea, and the city of Jerusalem, and mount Sion. But to us it is said: For you are not come to the things that are visible, but to the invisible. For you are come to the mount of the living God, and to the heavenly city Jerusalem, and to the multitude of angels. And elsewhere: That Jerusalem which is above is free, which is our mother. We believe, therefore, that there is a heavenly Jerusalem, and that this earthly one is after its type; and the things written of this earthly one we refer spiritually to that heavenly one. And as they cast out of the earthly Jerusalem the Chanaanites and Pherezites and the other nations, so we too, who are come to the mount of God and to the heavenly kingdoms, must expel from them the opposing powers and the spiritual wickednesses in the heavenly places. And as they cast the Jebusite out of Jerusalem, and what was called Jebus was afterwards called Jerusalem, so we must expel the Jebusite from Jerusalem, and so obtain its inheritance. They conquered with visible and bodily arms, we with invisible and spiritual ones. Whence: Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, etc. Put on the breastplate of charity and the helmet of salvation, and take up the shield of faith and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God. With such arms, following Jesus as leader, as the fathers trod on the necks of the nations, you too shall tread on the necks of the demons. For he says to those who follow him: "Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions." Jesus therefore wills always to do wonderful things; he wills to conquer giants by means of locusts, and by those who are on earth to overcome the heavenly wickednesses. This is perhaps what is said: That he who believes in him shall not only do the things that he himself did, but greater. For it seems to me greater if a man set in the flesh, frail and perishable, yet armed with the faith of Christ and his word, overcomes legions of demons; although it is he himself who conquers in us, yet he says it is more that he conquers through us. Only let us always be ready and armed with these arms, and let our conversation be in heaven, every movement of ours, act, thought and speech be heavenly. For the more ardently we ascend there, the more headlong they will descend. And the higher we are, the lower they. If our life is holy and according to God, it brings death to them. If slothful and luxurious, it makes them mighty against us, as giants. And the more we are spread out on earth, the wider spaces we yield to them in heaven. Let us increase, therefore, that they may be diminished; that as we enter, they may be driven out, and as we ascend, they may fall.
06_marg269: AUGUSTINE. Caleb and Jesus Nave, speaking to the people that they should not fear to enter the land of promise, said: But fear ye not the people of the land, for they are food for us. For their time is departed from them, but the Lord is among us; fear them not. Since it is said: they are food for us, that is: we shall consume them. But in what is added: For their time is departed from them, but the Lord is among us, they carefully did not say: The Lord is departed from them. For they were wicked. But since even to the wicked, by a hidden dispensation, a time of flourishing and reigning is given, the time departed from them. But the Lord is among us: they did not say: Time is departed from them and ours has succeeded; but: the Lord is among us, not time. For they had time; these had the Lord, the creator of times and dispenser of all things.
06_interl267: The majesty of the Lord covered them in the clouds of heaven.
06_marg270: ORIGEN. This threat is not wrathful but prophetic. For the people of the nations was to be taken up, but not through Moses; therefore Moses excused himself. For he knew that the nation which is promised was to be called not through him but through Jesus, and was to be named not the Mosaic but the Christian people. Therefore he entreats with many words for his own people.
06_marg271: I WILL STRIKE THEM THEREFORE. This threat is made by the Lord, not to show the divine nature passible and subject to anger, but that the charity which Moses had toward the people, and the goodness of God, which is above every mind, might appear. For God is written to be angry and to threaten, that man may know that he has so much place with God, and so much confidence, that if there is even some indignation in God, it may be softened by human observances; that man can obtain so much from God that he changes his own decrees. For the goodness which follows the anger both shows the confidence of Moses with God and teaches that the divine nature is foreign to the vice of anger. And the word contains a mystery to be fulfilled in the future, by which God promises that, this people being cast off, he will raise up another.
06_interl268: others: as thou hast sworn, saying: The Lord is patient
06_interl269: He dispenses the manner of correction with balanced moderation.
06_marg272: ORIGEN. But their children who are here with me, whoever know not good or evil, etc. Our fathers were that former people; we are their children. Because they sinned, they were cast off and fell; but we their children have risen up in their place and been raised, we who knew not good or evil. For we are of the Gentiles, and we knew neither the goods that come from God nor the evils that are begotten of sin. Whence: See then the severity and the goodness of God: towards them indeed that are fallen, the severity; but towards thee, the goodness, if thou abide in goodness, etc.
06_interl271: that is, the punishment of fornication
06_interl272: he expounds the mystery of the number
06_marg273: ORIGEN. As a year for a day you shall receive your sins for forty years. I fear to discuss this mystery. For I see that in it is comprised the reckoning of sins and punishments. For if to each sinner a year of punishment is assigned for the sin of one day, and according to the reckoning of the days on which one sins so many years are spent in torments, I fear lest perhaps for us, who sin daily, not even the ages themselves, or even the ages of ages, can suffice to pay the penalties. In this, that that people for the offence of forty days is tormented forty years in the desert, and is not permitted to enter the holy land, there seems to be shown a likeness of the future judgment, where the reckoning of sins is to be examined; where there will perhaps be some compensation of good works, or of those things which each received in his life, as is said of Lazarus. But no one knows this wholly save him to whom the Father has given all judgment.
06_marg274: Someone perhaps may deny that it befits the goodness of God to repay a year of torments for a day's sin; indeed he may say that even if he repaid a day for a day, though it were just, it would not seem kind. But if a wound is inflicted on the body, or a bone broken, or the joining of the sinews loosened, these wounds are wont to befall bodies within the space of one hour, and afterwards, many torments and pains having been gone through, to be healed with difficulty in a long time. For how many swellings in the place, how many torments are produced? But if it happens that in the same wound or the same fracture someone is wounded again and broken more often, with how many pains and how many torments can he be cured? And in how long a time, if indeed he can be, is he brought to health? And scarcely will he ever be so cured as to escape either weakness of body or the ugliness of the scar. Pass from the example of the body to the wounds of the soul, which as often as it sins is so often wounded, by sins as by darts. Whence: Take the shield of faith, wherewith you may be able to extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one. And it suffers not only the wounds of darts, but also fractures of the feet, when snares are prepared for its feet and its steps are supplanted. How long do you think such wounds as these can take to be healed? O that we could see how the soul is wounded by each sin! An evil word inflicts a wound, though not on the tongue; the soul is wounded also by evil thoughts and desires. And it is broken and crushed by the works of sin. If we saw all these and felt the scars of the wounded soul, we would resist sin even unto death. But as the possessed or the mad do not feel if they are wounded (because they lack the natural senses), so we, made mad by the desires of the world or drunk with vices, do not feel how great wounds, how great bruisings of the soul we acquire by sinning. And therefore it is a fitting reckoning that the time of punishment, that is, of cure and medicine, be extended, and that for each wound the spaces of healing be prolonged according to the quality of the blow. So therefore let both the equity and the kindness of God become evident in the very torments of the soul, so that he who has sinned, hearing these things, may come to his senses and sin no more. For conversion in the present life and fruitful penance bestow a swift medicine, which not only heals the past wound but does not allow the soul to be wounded by sin any further.
06_marg275: I will add another thing: if I am a sinner, will the punishment be the same for me if I have sinned once as if twice and thrice, and if more often? No; for according to the manner and number and measure of the sin, the quantity of the punishment also is to be measured. Whence: He will give us for our drink tears in measure. And the measure will be that which each has sought for himself in this life by sinning either less or more. The cup in the hand of the Lord, of pure wine, is said to be full of mixture. For it is mixed for each one, and judgment is made not only from the evils he has done but also from the goods. Yet though both are mingled, its dregs (which I think are called the portions of evils) shall not be wholly emptied out. But these things are in the hand of God; ours rather is quickly to amend and repent, to bewail the past, to beware of the future. For when thou shalt be converted and lament, thou shalt be saved. For we have an advocate, who intercedes for us, far more excellent than Moses, who yet was heard for that people. And perhaps Moses is written to have obtained pardon for the former people for this reason, that we may trust much more that our advocate Jesus will obtain pardon for us from the Father.
06_marg276: RABANUS. O wonderful insolence of the human mind and dreadful folly of a blinded heart! God commands them to believe his promises and trust in his power, and so to enter the land. Human folly distrusts and spurns the wholesome warnings. Contrariwise, he denies his help to them when they will to invade the land against the will of God. Like these are those who do not believe the promises of God and do what is forbidden. But the spiritual Amalecites and Chanaanites, who dwell in the mountains of pride, smiting them pursue them as far as Horma. Amalecite means the people "licking blood"; Chanaanites, "traffickers" or "moved". Horma is interpreted "anathema". The wickednesses of the air, therefore, which thirst for our blood and wish to entangle us in earthly business, if we persevere in sins and climb the mountain of pride, cut us down with fiery darts and pursue us as far as perpetual anathema. Let us not therefore presume upon ourselves, but, considering our weakness, follow the command of God in all things. For so shall we overcome all enemies; so shall we receive the joys of the heavenly fatherland which are promised to us.
06_interl280: spiritual knowledge in meditation on the law
06_interl282: spiritual grace, or the communion of Christ's passion
06_marg277: A SACRIFICE OF FINE FLOUR, etc. The faith of Christ's incarnation, which is most fully commended in the law, or the keeping of the Decalogue.
06_marg278: JOSEPHUS. The law commands that in private and public sacrifices most pure flour also be added: with a lamb one measure of an assaron, with a ram two, with a bull three, and mixed with oil upon the altar. For those who sacrifice also offer oil: with an ox half a hin, with a ram a third part of this measure, and a fourth with a lamb. Now the hin is an ancient measure of the Hebrews, holding about two ancient choes, according to which they offered oil. And the ephi (as is read in Ruth) is a measure of three bushels. And the hin (as those wish who have written of weights and measures) holds the measure of a sextarius; which is so named because it is the sixth part of a congius.
06_marg279: Allegorically. A sacrifice is commanded to be added for each kind of animal that is offered. Because we, who shall enter the land of the Church by the grace of the Lord, ought to add spiritual knowledge in meditation on the divine law for each kind of good works. The measure of the ephi, therefore, which has three measures, signifies the faith of the holy Trinity, of which we ought to offer the tenth, that is, the faith of Christ's incarnation, which is most fully commended in the law, or the keeping of the Decalogue. We are commanded, therefore, to offer oil, that is, charity and mercy, and wine for a libation, that is, spiritual grace and the communion of Christ's passion. And these according to the portion of the measure of the hin, that is, according to the distribution of perfect devotion. For the number six, because it is perfect, signifies the perfection of each thing. What else therefore is it, in the offering of a lamb, to offer the tenth part of an ephi of fine flour tempered with oil according to the fourth part of a hin, and wine of the same measure to pour out in libations, but to show simplicity of manners with the knowledge of the law and evangelical prudence? For simplicity does not please without prudence, nor prudence without simplicity. Whence: "Be ye wise as serpents and simple as doves." For folly as well as cunning is abominable to God.
06_marg280: AUGUSTINE. In the offering of a ram two tenths of fine flour are offered, and of oil and wine the third part of a hin. Because the ram signifies the order of rulers, it is well offered with two tenths, when anyone holding the Decalogue of the law in understanding and in deed is appointed to the office of ruler. And the third part of a hin of oil and wine is shown forth when charity and mercy and the grace of spiritual doctrine are spent by him on those subject to him.
06_interl286: the knowledge of the law, practice and doctrine
06_marg281: RABANUS. In the offering of an ox, three tenths of fine flour and half a hin of oil and wine. The ox signifies the order of preachers, who till the Lord's field, and with the gospel ploughshare root out the thorns of vices and multiply the harvest of virtues. These are offered with three tenths of fine flour, because, holding the Decalogue of the law in knowledge, doctrine and work, they are true asserters of the faith of the holy Trinity. These ought to have charity, and to give an example by counselling their neighbours through mercy, that is, to profit them by divine grace as far as mortals can, that they may come to perfection and holiness of life, according to that: Be ye holy, because I am holy. But what is lacking in this life, let them hope to have perfected in them in heavenly beatitude by the grace of the Lord.
06_interl294: coming from the Gentiles or the Jews
06_interl297: the domestic disciplines which each one exercises in himself
06_interl298: the beginnings of loving labour toward others
06_marg282: WHEN YOU ARE COME INTO THE LAND, ETC. RABANUS. When anyone enters the present Church through faith, he must diligently work the land of his flesh, that is, his bodily life, in the fear of God, and bring forth the fruit of virtues for eternal refreshment. We are commanded, therefore, to consecrate to God firstfruits not only of the barnfloors but also of the dough; that is, not only of the office of preaching but also of the domestic disciplines which each one skilfully exercises in himself, to dedicate to the Lord the beginning of good will. For whether someone strives after virtues in himself, or spends loving labour on others, let him impute it not to himself but to divine grace, so that to him may be consecrated the beginning of every good from whom the completion of perfection is hoped for.
06_marg283: AUGUSTINE. Since it is commanded how sins are to be expiated which are committed not willingly, it is rightly asked what are these sins of the unwilling: whether those committed by the ignorant, or those which they are compelled to do? For these too are commonly said to be done against the will. But one wills that which he does for the sake of something, when he wills to live, if someone threatens death unless he does it: he wills therefore to do it because he wills to live. And therefore not seeking for its own sake to swear falsely, but to live by swearing falsely. If it is so, I do not know whether such things can be called sins of the unwilling, such as are here said to need expiation. For if it is carefully considered, perhaps no one wills sinning itself, but it is done for the sake of something else which he who sins wills. For all men who knowingly do what is not lawful would wish it were lawful; so far does no one seek sinning for its own sake, but for the sake of that which follows from it. If these things are so, there are no sins of the unwilling except of the ignorant, which are distinguished from the sins of the willing.
06_interl301: of the stock of the patriarchs
06_interl302: bread and wine in memory of Christ's passion
06_interl303: Christ in the likeness of sinful flesh
06_marg284: RABANUS. The children of Israel offer a calf of the herd for a holocaust when the faithful peoples believe and confess with full faith the body of Christ immolated on the altar of the cross for the salvation of the human race. They offer its sacrifice and libations as the ceremonies require when in the sacrament they offer bread and wine in memory of his passion, and, partaking, trust that they have truly received his body and blood. And the buck goat for sin, when they believe that he took humanity and the likeness of sinful flesh, and offered himself for sins. The priest himself prays the Father for the sins of the people, and they are forgiven it, because in the days of his flesh, offering prayers and supplications to God, he was heard for his reverence.
06_interl307: doing penance, namely, earnestly, and withdrawing wholly from sin
06_marg285: Christ, who "by his own blood entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption".
06_interl310: despising the command of the Lord
06_interl311: from the number, namely, of those who belong to God
06_marg286: AUGUSTINE. Another text: Whatever soul shall sin with a high hand of pride, of the natives or of the proselytes, provokes God; that soul shall be exterminated from his people, because he has despised the word of the Lord and scattered his commandments: that soul shall be crushed with crushing, its sin is in it. What the sins are that are done with a high hand of pride he explained, saying: Because he has despised the word of the Lord. It is one thing, therefore, to despise the precepts of God, another to esteem them highly but to act against them either in ignorance or unwillingly; which two perhaps pertain to the sins done by the unwilling, of which he advised above how they should be expiated, God being propitiated. Then he added the sin of pride, when anyone does wrong by being proud, that is, by despising the command; which kind of sin he did not say ought to be purged by any kind of sacrifice, as judging it incurable by that cure which was carried out through those sacrifices, such as are here commanded to be done. Which, if they are regarded in themselves, can heal no sin. But if the things of which these are sacraments are inquired into, the purging of sins can be found in them. What is written, therefore: The wicked man, when he is come into the depth of sins, contemneth, signifies him whom Scripture here says to offend with a high hand of pride. This, therefore, cannot be abolished without the punishment of him who commits it, and therefore cannot be unpunished, even if it is healed by repenting. For the very affliction of the penitent is the punishment of sin, though medicinal and wholesome. For the sin is rightly judged great when pride despises the command. But on the contrary, that it may be healed, God does not despise a contrite and humbled heart; but because it is not done without punishment, such things are here said: For he here, he says, provokes God, because God resists the proud. And: that soul shall be exterminated from his people, because such a one is not at all in the number of those who belong to God. Because he has despised the word of the Lord and made his precepts void. He shall be crushed with crushing. And he adds why he is crushed, saying: His sin is in him; and therefore if he applies by repenting the contrition due to such a sin, God will not despise a contrite heart. Although in the Greek it is not said in this place, he shall be crushed with crushing, because it could be taken as though he were extinguished by being crushed in every way, or worn away, so that he should not be. But the soul is immortal; and if that which is worn away were wholly made not to be, it would not be said of wisdom: Let thy foot wear the steps of her doors. But that distinction is to be considered, whether no one sins except either in ignorance, or overcome, or in contempt; of which it is long to dispute now.
06_interl312: by the sentences of the spiritual
06_marg287: AND WHEN THEY HAD BROUGHT HIM OUT etc. ISIDORE. The wicked cavil that by the command of God he was so cruelly slaughtered by the whole people because he gathered sticks on the sabbath. But all things happened to them in figure. And they are written for our correction. For he who dared to violate the sabbath day by gathering sticks, and was therefore punished, signified him who today, sealed in Christ, is found doing carnal work, that is, gathering together wood, hay, stubble for food of the eternal fire. Who, if he is caught, is stoned and slain, because he is judged by the spiritual.
06_marg288: The children of Israel are commanded to make fringes of blue at the four corners of their cloaks, so that as circumcision in their bodies is the sign of the Jewish nation, so their garment too may have some difference; and that those who by the command of God differ from the other nations in dress may be warned to differ also in religion. We too are instructed that the commandments which seem to be least in the dress of the law, if they are done for the sake of the heavenly life (which the blue riband signifies), profit much. For he who despises the least things falls away little by little. Whether therefore we eat or drink, or whatsoever else we do, let us do all to the glory of God.
06_marg289: AUGUSTINE. What is it that Dathan and Abiron, called by Moses in the sedition, answered proudly and insultingly: Is this a small thing, that thou hast brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, because thou art over us, thou art prince? And thou hast brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, and given us a lot of field and vineyards? After this they added: Thou wouldst have cut out the eyes of those men: we do not go up. Whose eyes did they mean? Whether of the people of Israel, as if: if thou hadst so provided, thou wouldst have cut out their eyes, that is, they would so love thee that they would pluck out their eyes and give them to thee, according to that of the Apostle: "If it could be done, you would have plucked out your own eyes, and would have given them to me." And then they added full contumacy: We do not go up, that is: We do not come, because he had called them. Or rather the eyes of those men, that is, of the enemies, who were reported as exceedingly fierce and terrible, as if: Even if thou hadst done this, we would not obey thee; except that one mood of the verb is put for another, so that they said not: We will go up, but: We do not go up, by a certain kind of idiom?
06_marg290: AUGUSTINE. Another text: Go up from the midst of this congregation, etc. It is to be noted that the Lord commands a bodily separation to be made then, when vengeance already threatens the wicked. So Noe with his house is separated from the rest who were to perish by the flood; so Lot with his own is separated from the Sodomites who were to be consumed by fire from heaven; so the people itself from the Egyptians who were to be overwhelmed by the waves of the sea; so these now from the congregation of Core, Dathan and Abiron, who before had willed to break themselves off by sedition: with whom, however, the saints, living and conversing before, and with the others whom God reproves, could in no way be defiled by them. Nor were they commanded to separate themselves when the Lord delayed vengeance, or applied such a one by which the innocent could not be endangered, as by the bites of serpents, or the slaughter of the dying, by which God struck whom he willed, as he willed, the other being untouched; not as by the water of the flood, or the rain of fire, or the water of the sea, or the gaping of the earth, by which he could consume them alike when mixed together (not because God could not preserve his own there; but what need was there of the trial of a miracle where a separation could be made), so that water, or fire, or the gaping of the earth might carry off those it found. And so at the end the wheat shall be separated from the cockle, that, the flames burning the wicked, the just may shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
06_interl315: into the lower parts of the earth
06_marg291: ISIDORE. By Dathan and Abiron and Core are signified heretics and schismatics, who, drawing many with them, deceive them; despising the priests of Christ and separating themselves from the fellowship of the clergy and the people, they dare to build churches, and make another altar and another prayer with unlawful words, profaning the truth of the Lord's victim by false sacrifices. And because they strive against the will and ordinance of God, for the audacity of their rashness they are swallowed alive, the joints of the earth being broken; and not only the leaders, but all their accomplices and abettors shall perish in eternal fire, the vengeance prepared.
06_interl316: into the lower parts of the earth
06_marg292: AUGUSTINE. Another text: And they went down, themselves and all things whatsoever were theirs, alive to the lower regions. It is to be noted that the lower regions are so called according to an earthly place, that is, in the lower parts of the earth; for the name of the lower regions is put in various senses, and it is commonly taken especially of the dead. But since these are said to have gone down alive to the lower regions, and from the narrative itself it appears what was done, it is manifest that here the lower parts of the earth are named by the word for the lower regions, in comparison with this upper earth on whose face we live. Just as, in comparison with the upper heaven, where the dwelling of the holy angels is, Scripture says that the sinning angels, thrust down into the darkness of this air, are reserved to be punished as in the prisons of hell.
06_interl318: because through those who sinned an example was given to the rest, that they might fear
06_interl319: as though it is rather to be regarded before whom they were offered than by whom
06_marg293: AUGUSTINE. Another text: And the Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest: Take the brazen censers out of the midst of the burnt, and sow this strange fire there; because they have sanctified the censers of these sinners in their souls; and thou shalt make them beaten plates, a covering round about for the altar, because they were offered before the Lord and are sanctified, and are made for a sign to the children of Israel. Why did the Lord speak not to Moses and Aaron, as above, but to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron? This reason occurs to me meanwhile: because the question was about the lineage of the priests, that is, of what stock they ought to be; whence those of another stock, because they dared to usurp the priesthood to themselves, perished by a wonderful punishment. God willed to speak not to Aaron, who was already high priest, but to Eleazar, who was to succeed him and already held the second priesthood, so as thus to commend the line of descent that was to be in the successions of the priests. Whence in what follows he adds: And Eleazar the son of Aaron took the brazen censers, as many as those who were burnt had offered, and added them as a covering round about the altar, a memorial to the children of Israel, that no stranger who is not of the seed of Aaron may approach to put incense before the Lord; and he shall not be as Core and as his conspiracy, etc. In this way therefore God willed to commend not the priesthood, which was already in Aaron, but the lineage of the succession. And when he says: Sow the strange fire, it is to be understood: scatter it there. And what he added: Because they have sanctified the censers of these sinners in their souls, is a sentence expressed by an unusual idiom. But it is to be noted that they are said in a new manner to be sanctified in the punishment of those by whom this sin had been committed, because through them an example was given to the rest of what they should fear.
06_marg294: ORIGEN. Core bears the figure of those who rise up against the faith of the Church and the doctrine of truth. He with his company offered incense of strange fire in brazen censers. The fire, therefore, is commanded by the Lord to be scattered, and beaten plates to be made of the censers, because they are sanctified, and the altar to be surrounded with them, because they were offered before the Lord and sanctified. This seems to me to be figured: that the brazen censers hold the figure of divine Scripture, upon which the heretics, putting strange fire, that is, an understanding foreign to God and contrary to the truth, offer to God an incense not sweet but execrable. And therefore a pattern is given to our priests, that (if anything of the kind arises) the things that are foreign to the truth be wholly shut out of the Church of God. But if any things are found in the very words of the heretics from the meanings of divine Scripture, let them not be rejected; for they are sanctified, and offered to the Lord.
06_marg295: What is commanded of the censers of the sinners, that they be joined to the altar, can also be understood in another way. They are called brazen, because where there is true faith and the whole preaching of the word of God, they are called either silver or gold; so that the gleam of gold declares the purity of faith, and silver tried by fire signifies the words of the Lord examined by fire. But these brazen censers, that is, the voices of the heretics, if we bring them to the altar of God, where the divine fire is, where the true preaching of faith is, the truth itself will shine the better from comparison with false things. For if I refute the sayings of Marcion or Basilides or any heretic with the words of truth and the testimonies of the Scriptures, as with the fire of the divine altar, their impiety will appear more evident in me from the very comparison. For if the doctrine of the Church were simple, and were not split from without by any assertions of heretical dogmas, our faith would not seem so clear and so tried. Therefore those who contradict assail the catholic doctrine, that our faith may not grow torpid with idleness but be polished by exercises. Whence: There must be heresies, that they who are approved may be made manifest; as if: The altar must be surrounded by the censers of the heretics, that the difference of the faithful and the unfaithful may be made manifest to all. For when the faith of the Church has begun to shine like gold, and its preaching has gleamed like silver tried by fire, the voices of the heretics will be the more basely sordid with the cheapness of dark brass. For good things are known more by comparison with worse. Who would know that light is good, unless we felt darkness? Who would know the sweetness of honey, unless he had tasted bitterness? Finally, if you take away the devil himself and the opposing powers, will not the virtues of the soul be unable to shine forth without an adversary? So too the glory of faithful priests cannot shine forth unless the reprobation and punishment of the unfaithful commend it. Each of the just also seems to be held more glorious with God by comparison with the rest. Of Noe it is written that he was a just and perfect man in his generation; in which it is shown that he was not perfect wholly, but in his generation, that is, in comparison with the rest. Likewise Lot: the worse the Sodomites became daily, the more just he appeared. And when those who had viewed the land had returned, and ten with lying words had struck the people with despair, and two, that is, Caleb and Jesus, had reported good things and exhorted them to remain in their purpose, it was not so much their own confession that brought them immortal merit as the fear of their companions. For the virtue of their soul would not have shone so splendidly in them, had not the cowardly fear of the rest been laid open.
06_marg296: AUGUSTINE. And why he willed a covering round about the altar to be made of them, he added, saying that they were offered for a sign to the children of Israel. He did not wish, therefore, to reprove in them that they were offered by such men, but rather that this should be thought on and regarded: before whom they were offered, that is, that it was before the Lord; so that the name of the Lord before whom they were offered might avail more in them than the most evil desert of those by whom they were offered. And this Scripture already mentioned in Exodus also, when it tells of the altar being made. Whence it is understood that the kinds of things done are distributed through the books, not the order of times woven together. For of the rod of Aaron too, how the thing was done, that flowering and budding it should divinely show the choice of his priesthood, is read in this book; and yet in Exodus it is said, that it should be put in the holy of holies with the manna in the ark, when the command is given about making the tabernacle; which was commanded long before the tabernacle itself was made and finished and stood. And it stood in the first month of the second year after they went out of Egypt, and this book begins from the second month of the same second year, on the first day of the same month. Whence it is clear that these things (if we consider the order of the books) are related by recapitulation, that is, by a recalling of past things; which those who attend less carefully think were done in the same order in which they are told.
06_marg297: ORIGEN. With God nothing is idle, but things thought fit to be thrown away have some necessary work. The Scripture relates, therefore, that by the command of God Eleazar took the brazen censers which those who were burnt had offered, and they made of them rings and set them about the altar for a memorial to the children of Israel, that no stranger may approach to put incense before the Lord. For divine counsels are not as human counsels: if this cause were judged among men, and were held before the princes of the churches concerning those (for example) who, teaching things different from the churches, have borne the punishment of divine sentence or vengeance, would it not be judged that what they spoke, what they taught, what they wrote, should all perish together with the ashes of them all?
06_marg298: ORIGEN. An example is given to posterity also, that no one by the presumption of a proud spirit should seize the office of high priest not given him by God. But let it fall to him whom no human ambition, no corrupt favour, no damnable largess has taken up.
06_marg299: ORIGEN. In Sodom indeed at least ten were required, by whom those who dwelt in the Pentapolis might scarcely be saved. But now if two are found such as Moses and Aaron were, they suffice for the whole nation of the Israelites to be saved. What then is more in these two? What so great virtue, what merit, that six hundred thousand and more should be delivered? I think that in Moses the law is signified, which teaches man knowledge and the love of God; but in Aaron the form of supplicating and beseeching God. If ever, therefore, God is indignant with us or with the whole people, and vengeance is already going forth, and the law of God returning into our heart warns and teaches us to be converted to penance and to make satisfaction for our offences, at once the wrath will cease and the Lord will be appeased, as though Moses and Aaron were interceding for us and supplicating for the whole people. But if our hearts are hardened, and we neither turn nor are humbled in the sight of the Lord, so as to soften his wrath in the confession of supplications, but say on the contrary: God has no care for the life of mortals, nor do these things pertain to God; he left us long ago, nor does he know these things; then Moses and Aaron are not in us, namely the knowledge of the law and the fruit of penance, by which we can escape destruction.
06_interl321: in tribulation, namely; for the glory of the Lord cannot appear to one sleeping and idle.
06_marg300: ORIGEN. For we do not read before that the cloud covered the tabernacle, and the majesty of the Lord appeared, and received Moses and Aaron within the cloud, except when the people rose up against them and wished to stone them. Let us learn from this how great a benefit there is for Christians in persecution, how God protects them and the Holy Ghost is poured in. For then the glory of the Lord is most present when the cruelty of men is stirred up; and then we have peace with God when we are assailed by men for justice' sake; for where sin abounded, grace did more abound. The cloud therefore covered the tabernacle, and the congregation rushed upon Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared. Though they are of great merit and strong in virtues, the glory of God does not appear to them except in tribulation and danger, and almost in death itself. The Apostle too merited to obtain the glory of the Lord in these things; whence he reckons that he was in tribulations above the rest, was thrice stoned, and suffered shipwrecks, and perils of the sea and of rivers.
06_interl322: seeing in spirit what was being done
06_interl323: The law, which teaches man knowledge and the love of God.
06_interl325: the soul, namely, with which Christ was born
06_interl327: lest, namely, the destruction should go further
06_marg301: ORIGEN. Moses and Aaron, therefore, are commanded to go out of the midst of the congregation, that it may perish. But let us see what they do. They are holy and perfect, and disciples of the Gospel rather than of the Law; therefore they love even their enemies and pray for their persecutors. For as those rush upon them, these fall upon their face, and Moses says to Aaron: Take the censer, and put fire upon it, put in incense, etc. Let those see, therefore, who accuse God and the law alike, how Moses and Aaron did first what the Gospel afterwards taught. Moses loves his enemies and prays for his persecutors. The virtue of the Gospel, therefore, is found in the law, and the Gospel rests on the foundation of the law. Nor do I call the law the Old Testament, if I understand it spiritually. The law is the Old Testament only for those who understand it carnally. For them it is old and has grown old, because it cannot keep its strength. But for us, who expound it spiritually, it is always new, and both are to us a New Testament, not by the age of time but by the newness of understanding. Whence John says: Little children, "a new commandment I give unto you, that you love one another", though he knew that the commandment of love had been given in the law. But because charity never falleth away, and the commandment of truth does not grow old, he declares it always new. For it always makes those who keep it new in spirit; but to the sinner, and to one who does not keep the covenants of charity, even the Gospels grow old. Nor can there be a New Testament for him who does not put off the old man and put on the new, created according to God. Moses exhorts the high priest to offer incense in the camp and pray for the people. For the people had already begun to be destroyed. Moses saw in spirit what was being done. Understand the people of Israel in the camp, arranged in order of tribes and families, and a certain power sent from God, not at random, but having begun to destroy the people from the first part, and proceeding in order, a slaughter of death. Consider after this the high priest, clad in the pontifical vesture, carrying the censer and fire with incense, hastening to the place to which death had come through the destroying angel, and standing where death had made an end of the first and threatened the last. Behold the high priest standing and by a kind of interposing separating the living from the dead, and the destroying angel put to shame by the power of his propitiation and the mystery of the incense, and in this death ended and life restored. But having considered the history, go up to the loftier heights of this word, and see how the true high priest Jesus, taking the censer of the flesh, and fire of the altar set upon it, namely a magnificent soul, and incense also added, which is the immaculate spirit, stood between the living and the dead and checked death, destroying him who had the empire of death, so that he who believes in him may not die but live for ever. This mystery, then, that was to come afterwards, he who was destroying the people already then dreaded; he recognized the figure of the censer, the fire, the incense, and foresaw what manner of victim was to be offered to God by him who had stood between the living and the dead. The image saved them; to us the truth of salvation has come. For that angel would not have been put to shame by the vestments of the high priest of purple and wool woven with fine linen; but he understood the vestments of the great high priest to come, to which the whole creation is inferior, and yielded. And I think this pattern was fulfilled not only at the first coming of the Lord, but will be fulfilled at the second also: the Son of man will come again, and will find some dead and some living. And we can understand that some will be found in this state of life, when many have gone before dead. Or let us understand the bodies as the dead and the souls as the living; and then perhaps Christ will stand between the living and the dead, when he shall set the sheep on his right hand and the goats on his left, and shall say to those on the right: "Come, ye blessed of my Father" etc. But to those on the left: Depart, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, etc. For those are dead who are sent into everlasting fire, and those living who are sent to the kingdom.
06_interl329: the form of supplicating and beseeching
06_interl332: through the excess of their crimes
06_marg302: GREGORY. Aaron, to appease the wrath of God, took the censer and stood between the living and the dead, because it is the business of the priest to pour out prayer to God, both for the just that they may not fall and for sinners that they may rise again. Whence: Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight.
06_marg303: Aaron, taking the censer, ran to meet the shattering, and standing between the living and the dead, shut out the deadly plague by putting himself in its way, like a kind of wall. This priest is Christ, who, beholding the ruin of death in the world, ran to meet it from the highest heaven, and came to meet it as a giant to run the way. And he stood between the living and the dead, because he was born and died; and so, taking the censer of the passion and holding it forth for an odour of sweetness, he stayed the destruction of eternal fire and bore hostile death.
06_interl336: SEPTUAGINT: the destruction; or, as is contained in other copies: the breaking.
06_marg304: ORIGEN. Another text: And the destruction ceased, or the breaking, which is more fitting. For breaking happens in earthen vessels, which are sinners. Whence: The sons of Sion, who are more honourable and exalted in gold, how are they esteemed as earthen vessels, etc.? And in a great house there are vessels of wood and of earth, and some unto honour, some unto dishonour, which can be broken. Whence the Apostle of earthen vessels: If any man therefore shall cleanse himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified and profitable to the Lord, prepared unto every good work. In which he shows that the vessel which is made and he by whom it is made are one and the same man. Understand, therefore, that a man's purpose is that which works; the rest of the man is the vessel itself, which is made unto honour or unto dishonour. When therefore our mind has chosen the things that are good and draws us to good conversation, it makes us a profitable vessel. But when it has neglected, and our purpose has fallen away from good things, we are made a vessel unto dishonour. If our understanding is of clay, and thinks always of clay and earthly things, we are made an earthen vessel, the work of the potter's hands. Whence: Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it: Why hast thou made me thus? For a clayey and earthly mind does not grasp the mysteries.
06_marg305: Our body too is called an earthen vessel, or the letter of the law, in that the Apostle says: Having this treasure in earthen vessels. Because the Lord bestows the treasure of grace through the Holy Ghost on those set in the body. And in the words of the law, which are despised because they seem set forth with no grammatical art, is hidden the treasure of the wisdom and knowledge of God.
06_marg306: OF ALL THE PRINCES, etc. Every prince has a rod, because without it he cannot rule the people. Whence Paul, because he was a prince of the people, said: "What will you? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in charity?"
06_marg307: All the princes of the tribes must have rods. There is one only high priest, Aaron, whose rod budded; this is Christ, whose rod of the cross not only budded but also flowered and brought fruit to believers: nuts, it says, a fruit which in its first covering is bitter, in the second is fortified, in the third feeds. Such, therefore, in the hearing of Christ, is the doctrine of the law and the prophets. The first face of the letter is bitter, which commands circumcision of the flesh, and sacrifices, and the rest; all which cast away like the bitter rind of the nut. Secondly you will come to the defence of the shell, in which is signified either moral doctrine or the reckoning of continence; which are necessary for the guarding of the things that are kept within. Yet they are at some time to be broken and loosed; for abstinence from food and chastisement of the body are necessary to a corruptible body. But when it has been broken and dissolved, and at the time of the resurrection made incorruptible and spiritual, no corruption of the body will any longer have dominion, not now by the labour of affliction nor by the chastisement of abstinence, but by its own quality. Now, therefore, abstinence is necessary, but afterwards it is not to be sought. In the third place you will find the hidden sense of the mysteries of the wisdom and knowledge of God, by which the souls of the saints are nourished even in the future. For this is the pontifical fruit, of which it is promised to those who hunger and thirst after justice that they shall be filled. So, therefore, through all the Scriptures runs the reckoning of a threefold sacrament; so Wisdom too admonishes that we describe her in our heart in three manners; so Isaac dug three wells, of which the third is named breadth or largeness. And because the rod of the nut is a priestly sacrament, I think Jeremias (who was one of the priests of Anathoth) saw a rod of the nut tree, and prophesied the things that are written of the rod of the nut tree and of the boiling caldron; as though he showed by these that in the rod of the nut tree is life, and in the kindled caldron is death. For life and death are set before our face. And life is Christ in the sacrament of the nut; but death is the devil in the figure of the caldron. If therefore you sin, your portion will be with the kindled caldron. If you do well, in the rod of the nut tree with the great high priest. In the Canticle of Canticles too the bride is said to go down into the garden of nuts, and with the nuts to have found an abundance of priestly fruits.
06_marg308: ORIGEN. God promised one fruit in the rod, and gave many, that we may observe the liberality of God to be larger than his promises. The man, he says, whom I shall choose, his rod shall bud. But when it comes to the thing, not only is this promise fulfilled, but many things are added. For it says: and it brought forth leaves, and put forth flowers, and budded nuts; whereas only a bud was promised. As in these God gave his promise fourfold, and bestowed many more and more precious things than he promised, so in all places of Scripture where some promise is contained, it will be prepared manifold in the future, and that will truly be fulfilled which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither hath it entered into the heart of man. Whether therefore you speak of earth or heaven, or this sun and the brightness of visible light, all these the eye has seen and the ear has heard. Pass beyond, therefore, all the things you see, that you hear, whatever even can be thought, and know that that is laid up for those who love God which cannot even ascend into the thought of your heart. Whence I think that nothing bodily is to be thought of in the promises. For the nature of bodily matter does not escape the sense of one who thinks; but they are things contained in the wisdom of God alone.
06_marg309: GREGORY. When Aaron, who was of the tribe of Levi, was despised for the priesthood, and another was believed worthy to offer holocausts, twelve rods according to the twelve tribes are commanded to be put in the tabernacle; and the rod of Levi grew green, and showed what virtue Aaron had in his office. In which it is hinted that all of us who lie in death until the end of the world remain in dryness, like the rest of the rods. But while all the rods remained in dryness, the rod of Levi returned to flower, because the body of the Lord, namely of the true priest, placed in the dryness of death, burst forth into the flower of the resurrection; by which flower Aaron is rightly shown to be priest, because by this glory of the resurrection the Redeemer, who sprang from the tribe of Juda and of Levi, is shown to be an intercessor for us. The rods of the twelve tribes remain in dryness, because the body of the Lord lives after death, but our bodies are still deferred from the glory of the resurrection until the end of the world.
06_marg310: The dry rod buds when the dead body comes to life again, to which four things will be granted: sown in corruption, it shall rise in incorruption; sown in weakness, it shall rise in power; sown in dishonour, it shall rise in glory; sown a natural body, it shall rise a spiritual body. These four things the rod of the dry body will bud forth in the resurrection.
06_marg311: GREGORY. The flesh of Christ, which, cut off from the root of Jesse and put to death, quickly lived again after the dryness of death. In the rod, the power of one reigning; in the flower, beauty. Whence: "I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys." Others think this rod which flowered without moisture is Mary, who without intercourse brought forth the Word of God. Whence: "There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root", namely Christ, who, bearing the type of the passion to come, made purple with the white light of faith and the blood of the passion; the flower of virgins, the crown of martyrs, the grace of the continent.
06_marg312: AND THE BUDS SWELLING, etc. ORIGEN. But by this reckoning, by which the good things of the promises are given greater than the promises, the punishments which are foretold to sinners are inflicted with multiplied torments. Unless someone should think that some third thing can be done, gathering some comfort from the things contained in the threat to David, where a destruction of death to come was foretold for three days, and the time of punishment was shortened to six hours. But these things can avail there where a time of penance and a place of satisfaction is granted. Yet it is written that God repays to the wicked their sins unto the third and fourth generation, but shows mercy to the good, not only unto the third and fourth, but according to Scripture unto a thousand generations.
06_marg313: We can also understand thus the differences of the things that budded on the rod. He who believes in Christ first dies, and afterwards is born again, and so the dry rod buds. The first bud is the first confession of a man in Christ. Secondly it puts forth leaves, when, reborn, he receives the gift of grace and the sanctification of the Spirit. Then it brings forth flowers, when he advances and is adorned with sweetness of manners, and pours out the fragrance of mercy and kindness. At length it brings forth fruits of justice, by which not only he himself may live, but he may give life to others, namely by bringing forth from himself the word of faith and of the knowledge of God, that he may gain others. So, therefore, each of the faithful buds from the rod of Aaron, which is Christ; and these four differences of theirs are marked in other places of Scripture as four ages. Whence John says: I have written to you, children; and I have written to you, young men; and I have written to you, youths; and I have written to you, fathers. In which he sets down differences not of bodily age but of the soul's progress, as we have observed in the bud of the priestly rod. But all these are had not so much in the rod of Aaron as in that which came forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root, upon whom the Spirit of God shall rest. Nor does it seem idle that the rod is said to come forth and the flower to rise up. For though Christ is one in substance, yet he becomes different to each, according as the one in whom he works has need. To him who is slothful he becomes a rod for discipline, and in the rod he is said not to rise up but to come forth. For he must come forth to one who is slothful, and pass over to another state, as a rod, that is, compelled by the severity of a more rigid doctrine. But in the just man, who flourishes like the palm tree, Christ is said to rise up. If anyone therefore needs stripes, he comes forth to him in the rod. But to him who advances to justice he rises up in the flower, until he brings forth the fruits of the Spirit, which are charity, joy, peace, patience and the other virtues.
06_interl338: SEPTUAGINT: You shall take the sins of the holy things; because, namely, by the things which the high priest offers for each one's sin, he purifies him.
06_interl339: the sacrifices offered for sins, which are due to the priests
06_marg314: AUGUSTINE. Another text: Thou and thy sons and thy father's house shall receive the sins of the holy things, and the sins of your priesthood. These are the sins of the holy things which are called sacrifices for sins. And sins of the holy things is said, not such as holy men commit, but from this, that they are holy things. It is said of the holy things because they are offered in the holy places, and the sacrifices for sins are called sins: therefore they are called sins of the holy things. And the sins of your priesthood, that is, the same things that are offered for sins: as he declares also in Leviticus, and says they belong to the priest.
06_marg315: Another text: Thou and thy sons and thy father's house with thee shall take the sins of the holy ones. Those who are better take up the faults of the lower. Whence: You that are stronger, bear the infirmities of the weak. If an Israelite sins, that is, a layman, he cannot himself take away his own sin, but seeks a Levite, or a priest, or a high priest, that he may receive remission of sins. But a priest or high priest, if he offends, can himself purge his own sin, provided he does not sin against God. For of sins of this kind we do not easily see remission of sins signified in the letter of the law.
06_marg316: Jesus our high priest, who has passed into the heavens with his sons, that is, the apostles and martyrs, takes the sins of the holy ones. For he came to take away the sins of the world by his death. Their sons too take away the sins of the holy ones. Whence Paul: I most gladly will spend myself for your souls. And elsewhere: For I am even now ready to be sacrificed. And a victim is sacrificed for this, that the sins of those for whom it is slain may be purged. And of the martyrs John writes in the Apocalypse that the souls of those who were slain for the name of Jesus stand by the altar. And he who stands by the altar is shown to perform the office of a priest, that is, to supplicate for the sin of the people. I fear therefore that perhaps, since there are no martyrs, and the victims of the saints are not offered for our sins, there may be no remission, and that may befall us which the Jews say of themselves. For having neither altar nor temple nor priesthood, and therefore not offering victims, our sins, they say, remain in us; therefore we do not obtain pardon. But we ought to say that because the victims of the martyrs are not offered for us, therefore our sins remain in us. For we do not merit to suffer persecution for Christ. For the devil, knowing that remission of sins comes about through the passion of martyrdom, does not wish to stir up against us a public persecution of the Gentiles, because he envies our glory; or perhaps God knows that we are not fit for martyrdom.
06_marg317: It is to be asked how some are called holy and yet it is written of their sins. For it is not (as some think) that as soon as a man has begun to be holy he cannot sin and is at once without sin. For it is said by Ezechiel: Begin ye at my sanctuary. For if the saints are without sin, how do they first succumb in the punishment of sinners? And elsewhere: The just is first accuser of himself. The Apostle too, who writes in the beginning: "To all that are at Rome, the beloved of God, called to be saints", afterwards says to the same: Destroy not the work of God for meat. And to the Corinthians: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the church of God that is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints. Afterwards he says to the same: For whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal, and walk according to man? And a little after: It is absolutely heard that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as the like is not among the heathens, and you are puffed up. In which he leaves no one free, while he ascribes fornication to some, to others being puffed up and the crime of pride, and he sets down many things of this kind and worse in what follows. But there are many differences among the holy. For those same are called holy and sinners who have vowed themselves to God and separated their life from the common crowd, that they may serve the Lord. A man of this kind, according to this, that he has given himself over to the Lord with his other acts cut off, is called holy. But perhaps in this, that he serves the Lord, he does not do all things as befits, but offends in some. For if he who separates himself from all acts in order to attain the discipline of medicine or philosophy is not at once so perfect that he does not err in anything, but rather scarcely reaches perfection by erring very often, and yet when he has given himself to such schools it is certain that he is numbered among physicians and philosophers; so he who is given over to the pursuits of holiness, according to what he has purposed, is called holy. But according to this, that he must offend in many things while by practice and diligence the habit of sinning is cut away, he is called a sinner.
06_marg318: I add further that unless someone has a holy purpose and carries on the pursuit of holiness, he does not know how to do penance for sin or seek a remedy. Those who are not holy die in their sins; those who are holy do penance for their sins, feel their wounds, understand their falls, seek the priest and purification through the high priest. Therefore it is carefully and significantly said that the high priests and priests take the sins not of anyone whatever, but of the holy. For he is holy who has his sin cured through the high priest.
06_marg319: etc. ORIGEN. Another text: But thou and thy sons with thee before the tabernacle of the testimony, keep your watches and those of the altar, of the tabernacle, etc. The things that are written should be diligently observed, and especially by those who glory in the priestly order. But who observes and does the things that are commanded to priests, and who uses the priestly order and speech but does not observe the works, he alone can know who searches the hearts and reins. And they are commanded to observe not only the things that are without, but especially those that are within the veil; as though the priests should have care both to fulfil the evident and manifest commands of the divine law and to behold the hidden mysteries with all clear-sightedness. But if you wish to refer the tabernacle of the testimony to man (for Paul calls the body of man a tabernacle), the inner part of the veil, where the inaccessible things are covered, we shall call the principal part of the heart, which alone can receive the mysteries of truth. And the two altars, that is, the inner and the outer (since the altar is a token of prayer), I think signify what the Apostle says: I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the understanding. For when I pray in the heart, I go in to the inner altar. Whence: But thou when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret. He who prays thus goes in to the altar of incense, which is within. But he who with a clear voice, and words uttered with sound, to edify the hearers, prays in spirit, offers a victim on the altar which is without, set up for the holocaust of the people. The priests therefore ought especially to care for the things that are covered within the inner veil, that nothing defiled be found there, namely the inner man and the secrets of the heart, that they may remain spotless there. The cherubim and the propitiatory are to be understood as the knowledge of the Trinity. For cherubim is interpreted multitude, that is, perfection of knowledge; and what other perfection of knowledge is there than to have known the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost? These things therefore are to be cared for by the priests, that they may be kept uncontaminated and unhurt. And the urn having the heavenly food of manna is the treasure of the divine word. The golden ark in which are the tables of the testament is our mind, in which we ought to have the law of God written: this ought to be golden, that is, pure and precious, in which the law of God may be "written, not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in the fleshly tables of the heart". Whence: "Who shew the work of the law written in their hearts." For God wrote with his finger in their hearts the natural law which the Lord gave to the human race, and wrote it in the minds of all. From which we take beginnings and certain seeds for searching out the truth, which, if we cultivate them well, will bring us the fruit of life.
06_marg320: Allegorically. The more perfect, namely, in the Church, and the holy doctors, whose office is to handle with their hands the divine sacraments and the holy vessels, that is, to winnow the mystic words of Scripture and bring them forth to understanding. But the rest of the crowd should diligently meditate on what it can grasp and what the discretion of the masters commands.
06_marg321: Not of the tribe of Levi. For Ozias, of the tribe of Juda, because he usurped the priesthood, was struck with leprosy.
06_marg322: AND THE LORD SAID, etc. ORIGEN. Another text: The Lord spoke to Aaron, saying: Behold I have given you the firstfruits for keeping. Others however say: for observing; but more truly: for keeping. And it is to be asked how, according to the law, the firstfruits are kept? For the priests receive them not to keep them but to consume them. This therefore is not applied to the law of the letter but to the law of the spirit. For spiritual firstfruits can be kept; literal ones cannot. Christ is truly the firstfruits which are given us for keeping. For it is blessed that the soul which has received Christ should always keep him and always have him. But the things that were offered in the law were consumed, and digested in the belly, into the privy; but not so these firstfruits. He who eats and tastes the bread which came down from heaven shall not die for ever. For this is the bread which, though it is always eaten, always remains, nay, is increased. For the more fully you take the word of God, the more it will abound.
06_marg323: Literal firstfruits are consumed; spiritual ones are kept. For the more fully you take the word of God, the more it will abound.
06_interl340: not by proselytes, not by Gentiles
06_marg324: ORIGEN. Another text: Of all things that are sanctified to me by the children of Israel, etc. God does not wish to receive firstfruits except from those sanctified of Israel. For works worthy of God are found among the Gentiles: some have cultivated the virtues of the soul, and prophecy has done something in a few. God wishes to receive good deeds from those whose mind sees God and who are holy through faith in God. But a Gentile, even if he has something honourable in his manners (because he ascribes it not to God but to himself), is not sanctified nor received among the firstfruits.
06_marg325: But according to the letter he seems to exclude the proselytes, and wishes only the sanctified of the children of Israel to offer firstfruits. And I think a proselyte is so called from this, that he is not permitted to enter the Church. For it is written: "Thou shalt not abhor the Edomite, because he is thy brother: nor the Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land. They that are born of them, in the third generation shall enter into the church of God." Until, therefore, the Egyptian or the Edomite bears fruit and makes sons of the first and second and third generation, he does not enter into the Church; but the begetting of sons makes him enter. And note that he does not say "if sons or daughters are born to them", but "if sons are born to them". Only sons are those who make the fathers enter into the Church.
06_marg326: Three times in the year every male is commanded to appear, not the female.
06_marg327: Not by the daughters. For not idly does he elsewhere name daughters too with sons, and elsewhere make no mention of daughters. Which, however, are to be referred especially not to sex but to the distinction of souls.
06_marg328: You will hardly find saints to whom God gives exceptional testimony having begotten daughters. Abraham and Isaac did not beget daughters. Jacob alone begot one daughter, and she was a reproach to her brothers and parents, and stirred up in her brothers the fury of vengeance.
06_interl342: because they are not holy of themselves
06_marg329: THESE THEREFORE SHALT THOU TAKE, etc. THE SAME. And let this be yours of the things that are sanctified of the holy things, of the sacrifices, etc. The Holy Ghost is so holy that he is not sanctified. For sanctification does not come to him from elsewhere, nor did he receive a beginning of holiness. The same is to be understood of the Father and the Son. For the Trinity alone is the substance which is holy not from without but by its own nature. For every creature, sanctified either by the condescension of the Holy Ghost or by reason of merits, is called holy. Whence: "Be ye holy, because I am holy" etc. For the same holiness is not to be set in God and in man. For of God it is said, that thou art holy; but to men, as to those who were not always so, it is commanded that they become holy. And where we have "be ye holy", in the Greek is had "become ye holy". But our interpreters put "be ye" indifferently for "become ye". Each one of us therefore, from the time he has given himself over to God with a true heart, is made holy. But truly and always holy is God alone. Whence: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one. And do not think that contrary which we read of Christ, whom the Father sanctified and sent into this world. For he who is sanctified according to the flesh is Christ, not according to the spirit. According to the spirit and the flesh alike he says: I sanctify myself for them; so that he who sanctifies is understood according to the spirit, he who is sanctified according to the flesh, yet one and the same Christ. From all the fruits, therefore, sanctified firstfruits are to be offered, but to the spiritual high priest. And the fruit of the spirit is charity, joy, peace, patience etc. And the firstfruits of charity are that one love God with the whole heart and with the whole soul and with the whole mind. From this fruit of charity I ought to have secondly that I love my neighbour as myself. Those firstfruits of charity, therefore, are offered to God through the high priest; those which are in the second place are left for my uses; and in the third place, from this fruit I ought to love even my enemies.
06_marg330: The law commands the firstfruits of all flocks to be offered to the priests, so that everyone who possesses a field, a vineyard and an olive yard, a garden, and whatever is worked on the land, and who rears herds of any cattle, should offer to God all that is first.
