For he says that what is given to the priests is offered to God; for this is taught from the law, that no one lawfully uses fruits or cattle unless firstfruits of each are offered to God in the priests. This law, therefore, I think must of necessity be observed according to the letter, like some others. For there are some commands that must of necessity be observed even in the New Testament. Yet there are those who say: If anything is observed according to the letter, why not all? But if they are to be understood spiritually, all are to be discussed spiritually. But we, tempering the extravagance of both assertions, will set forth by the authority of the Scriptures what is to be observed in these things. For it is written: "The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones"; "the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes"; "the fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever"; "the justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts"; "the judgments of the Lord are true" etc. Unless each of these were different, Scripture would not have given its own differences to each, so as to say one thing of the law of the Lord, another of the commandment, another of the justifications, another of the judgments. One thing therefore is the law, another the precept, another the testimony, another the judgment, another the justification. Whence elsewhere: "This is the law, and the commandments, and the justifications, and the precepts, and the testimonies, and the judgments, which the Lord commanded Moses." Let us attend more carefully, therefore, to the things recited in the law. For wherever a commandment is written to be, it is not at once to be taken as law. Justifications too are not at once to be thought law or commandment. For a testimony or justice is to be taken not confusedly as one with the rest, but distinctly. When therefore it is said that the law has a shadow of things to come, it is not therefore that the commandment or justice or judgments are shadows of things to come. For neither is it written "this is the commandment of the Pasch", but "this is the law of the Pasch". In the bodily sheep, therefore, I ought to understand that there is a shadow of the good to come, and that Christ our Pasch is sacrificed; likewise too you will find it written of the unleavened bread and of the other observances of feast days. Since therefore all these things are written in the law under the title of law, I ought to ask what is the unleavened bread of the good things to come? And I find the Apostle saying: "Not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness" etc. It is written also: "This is the law of circumcision." I ask therefore what shadow of the good things to come is contained in circumcision? Lest Paul say to me in the shadow of circumcision: If you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing. Each of these things, therefore, which the Apostle says are not to be observed according to the letter, "you will find marked with the title of law in Moses".
06_marg331: But where it says: "Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery" and the like, it did not set before them the title of law. For these are commandments, and therefore they are not emptied out among the disciples of the Gospel, but fulfilled. For not the commandment, but the law is said to have a shadow of the good things to come.
06_marg332: But note that law is said in two ways: for generally all these things, commandment, justifications, precepts, testimonies, judgments, are called law; but specially, some part of the things written in the law, as said above. And law is signified generally when it is said: "I am not come to destroy the law, but to fulfil." And elsewhere: "Love is the fulfilling of the law." For he named all the things written in the law the law.
06_marg333: Elsewhere too he says: Thou shalt follow justly after that which is just. And what need is there to seek allegory even in these, when the letter edifies?
06_marg334: I ask also whether some things which stand according to the letter must necessarily be understood allegorically too? For it is written in the law: "Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife" etc. That these contain allegorical mysteries Paul declares, saying: "This is a great sacrament" etc. But that it ought also to be kept according to the letter the Lord himself shows, saying: "It is written: For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they two shall be in one flesh." What therefore God hath joined together, let no man put asunder. And that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondwoman and the other by a free woman, who doubts that it stands according to the letter? But the Apostle added: Which things are said by an allegory.
06_marg335: EVERY OFFERING, etc. ORIGEN. It belongs to the wise scribe, learned in the kingdom of God, to know how to bring forth from these treasures new things and old; and how to cast away wholly the letter that killeth and seek the spirit that quickeneth, so as to confirm the useful and necessary doctrine of the letter, or, the history remaining, to bring in a mystic sense as well, as in the present place.
06_marg336: For it is useful to offer firstfruits to the priests of the Gospel, so that those who preach the Gospel may live by the Gospel. For it is impious that one who enters the Church of God, who knows that the priests and ministers stand by the altar and the word of God, or serve in the ministry of the Church, should not offer the priests firstfruits of the fruits of the earth which the Lord gave by bringing forth his sun and supplying the rains. For he who believes the fruits are given him by God knows how to honour God from his gifts by rewarding the priests. Whence: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because you tithe mint, and cummin, and anise, and have left the weightier things of the law: hypocrites, these things you ought to have done, and not to leave those undone." The Lord therefore wills these things not to be left undone according to the letter. To the disciples too he says: "Unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven." What therefore he wills from the Pharisees, much more from the disciples. But what he does not will to be done by the disciples, neither by the Pharisees. "Whence it was said to them of old: Thou shalt not kill"; this the Pharisees keep; but to the disciples it is said: "Whosoever is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment."
06_marg337: Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, not from the curse of the commandment or of the testimony or of the judgments; that is, that we should not be subject to circumcision of the flesh and the observance of sabbaths and the like, which are contained in the law, not in the commandments. Our justice therefore abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees. If they dare not taste of the fruits of the earth before they offer firstfruits to the priests and set apart tithes for the Levites, shall I, doing none of these things, so abuse the fruits of the earth that the priest and the Levite and the altar of God have no feeling of it?
06_marg338: Peter and Paul too offer through themselves the firstfruits of believers. Whence Paul says: "That from Jerusalem round about as far as unto Illyricum, I have replenished the gospel of Christ", where Christ was not named, lest they should build upon another man's foundation. All therefore whom he taught he offers as his fruits, and daily seeks new fields to cultivate and new country to sow. Whence he says: "I long to come unto you, that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles." From all these he marks out the choice ones, and chooses and offers the firstfruits of each church.
06_marg339: Every doctor too, because he teaches, preaches and instructs his hearers, seems to cultivate the field of his Church, that is, the hearts of believers. He has also the fruit of his cultivation, and in the fruit some choice and special one whom he may offer as firstfruits, and another for the firstborn, another for the tithes.
06_marg340: Someone perhaps has firstborn and lower ones whom he can offer neither for firstfruits nor for firstborn, but for tithes.
06_interl346: the true high priest, namely, that is, Christ
06_interl347: the apostles, the greater, namely, and the lesser powers
06_marg341: How can that be eternal which is visible? For the things which are seen are temporal. But the firstfruits which are offered to Aaron are visible; circumcision too and the unleavened bread and the Pasch are visible; necessarily they are not eternal but temporal. The invisible circumcision, therefore, which is in secret, is eternal, and the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. So too these things, for him who is a Jew not openly but in secret, who keeps the law in spirit, not in the letter, are called eternal ordinances according to the inner man.
06_marg342: ALL THE BEST, etc. ORIGEN. We have shown that the command concerning the firstfruits of crops or cattle ought to stand even according to the letter. Let us see how it is understood spiritually. For here he says: All the firstfruits of oil, wine and corn. The firstfruits of all these, which shall have been offered to the Lord, I have delivered them to thee. But if all firstfruits belong to the high priest, a high priest is to be sought to whom those firstfruits also ought to belong which we find in other places. And of Christ we read that he is the firstfruits of the dead; he is therefore in some part firstfruits. The Apostle also says of certain ones that they are the firstfruits of Asia, and others the firstfruits of Achaia. It follows that Cornelius, with those who received the Holy Ghost with him, is called the firstfruits of the Church of Caesarea, and perhaps of all the Gentiles, of whom he first believed and first merited the Holy Ghost. And the field is called the world. And the field is not of earth alone, but human hearts, which the angels have received to cultivate. The fruits of their cultivation, therefore, they themselves possess, namely those who live under stewards and authors and have not yet come to the full perfection of age. But the perfect, as chosen and special ones, they offer as firstfruits to the great high priest. We find that Cornelius himself, before he received the doctrine of the word or the grace of baptism from Peter, heard from an angel that his prayers and alms had ascended to God; whence through the angel he seems to have been offered to God as firstfruits.
06_marg343: Christ is the firstfruits of firstfruits. Cornelius the firstfruits of the Gentiles. Others the firstfruits of churches, as some the firstfruits of Asia, others of Achaia.
06_marg344: Each of the angels will be present at the consummation of the world in the judgment, bringing with him those over whom he presided, whom he helped, whom he instructed, for whom he always saw the face of the Father who is in heaven. And I think it will be inquired there whether the angel failed in the cultivation of men, or whether human sloth did not answer worthily to the angelic cultivation. There will therefore be a judgment of God in this also, whether by the negligence of the ministers who were sent to minister and help for the sake of those who receive the inheritance of salvation, or by our own idleness, so many falls befall us. There will therefore be a judgment of God both on men and on angels. And perhaps some who come from the multitude of believers will be judged with Paul and compared with his labours and fruits, and perhaps he will be found stronger than some angels. Whence: Know you not that we shall judge angels? Not that Paul judges angels, but the work of Paul will judge some. Hence perhaps Peter said: On whom the angels desire to look. Although the apostles too use the angels as helpers in completing the office of preaching. Whence in the Acts of the Apostles it was said that it was Peter's angel who knocked at the door. Likewise, therefore, it is understood that there is an angel of Paul and of any apostle, and of each in order or according to merits; who in the labours and doctrine either of the apostles or of the other doctors must have the first parts, and bring to the Lord's threshing floor the fruit of the souls which have profited through them, together with those through whom they worked. There will therefore be, in the gathering of fruits, that is, in the choosing of believers, he who was the special and outstanding firstfruits of that Church; and the higher of that Church, the firstborn offered by that archangel. All, therefore, that is foreshadowed in the law (since the law has a shadow of the good things to come) will be fulfilled in another manner through the ministries of angels in the truth of the good things to come, so that the things formed in Israel according to the flesh may be fulfilled in the true Israelites. For the name of Israel reaches to the angels, who are more truly called Israel, inasmuch as they are more truly the mind seeing God; for this is what Israel is interpreted. For as certain names of nations or princes are referred to evil angels, as Pharao king of Egypt, Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon or the Assyrian, so the things written of holy men and of a religious nation are referred also to the holy angels. Whence Isaias of Nabuchodonosor: "And I will bring the sword upon a great nation, and upon the prince of the Assyrians." And elsewhere, as of the prince of some nation: "How art thou fallen, O Lucifer, who didst rise in the morning?" And as to what we read in Genesis of God speaking to the angels: "Come, let us confound their tongue", it is to be thought that divers angels produced divers tongues and speeches in men. For example: one impressed on one man the Babylonian tongue, another the Egyptian, another Greek; and so perhaps they themselves were the princes of divers nations, who seemed to be the authors of the tongue and speech. But the tongue first given through Adam, that is, Hebrew, remained in that part of men which is the portion not of an angel or prince but of God.
06_marg345: The angels therefore offer firstfruits from among us, and each cultivates what he has zealously converted to God from the errors of the Gentiles, and each one is in the portion or care of this or that angel. And as from the beginning, when God divided the sons of Adam, he appointed the bounds of the nations according to the number of the sons or angels of God, and each nation was made subject to this or that angel, but Israel is the portion of the Lord and the lot of his inheritance; so I believe it will be at the end of this world and the beginning of the other age, that the Most High will again divide the sons of Adam; and those who cannot be so clean of heart as to see God himself and be the portion of the Lord will either see the holy angels and be according to the number of the angels of God. It is desirable therefore that each should so advance as to be chosen among the firstfruits or firstborn and offered to God as his portion. If less, let him at least merit to be the portion of the holy angels, provided he is not found among those of whom it is said: "They shall go into the lower parts of the earth: they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes", that is, of demons. For these are the foxes that destroy the vineyards; of whom was Herod, of whom it is said: "Go and tell that fox." Let us flee, therefore, earthly acts and earthly understanding, lest we go into the lower parts of the earth. For they go in who receive the law of God and the goods of the promises with an earthly understanding, and do not rouse the souls of the earthly to the expectation of heavenly things, that they may seek the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth.
06_marg346: The angels offer firstfruits, each one, I believe, of his own nation and of his own church; to whom John in the Apocalypse seems to write, namely to the angel of the Church of Ephesus, Smyrna, Laodicea etc. Each therefore offers the firstfruits of his nation or of his church, which was committed to him to dispense; or perhaps there are also other angels from without, who gather the faithful from all nations. And let us consider whether perhaps, as in some city where there are not yet Christians, if someone teaches and instructs, and afterwards becomes chief bishop there; so the holy angels, those whom they have gathered from divers nations, if they have made them advance, may become princes and rulers in the future? so that Christ may be called King of kings and Lord of lords. For these are the kings of those whom they rule and make to advance. They themselves therefore offer some to the high priest, some to the sons of the high priest, that is, to the higher powers and archangels, some to the Levites, that is, to those a little lower; if the angelic orders are distinguished as the Israelites were, since they are said to serve the shadow and example of heavenly things. Perhaps, therefore, in the future, when all the fruits shall be gathered to the threshing floor, some will be the portion of the true high priest, that is, Christ; others, of the Levites, set apart either for angels or for other heavenly powers; some also the portion of men who in this life were prudent dispensers of God. Whence to him to whom the Lord had entrusted five pounds and who had made ten he says: "Have thou power over ten cities" etc. For what is understood here by power over cities but the government of souls? Whence it seems to me that among the angels some hold principality and power over others, others are subject and obey the power. So neither does he to whom the power of ten cities or of five is given come to this power undeservedly. All things therefore are done with God by reason and judgment, and not by favour but for merit is one set as prince of many, another subject to principality.
06_marg347: The fields of the angels are our hearts; each of them offers firstfruits to the Lord from the field which he cultivates.
06_marg348: As Christ is King of kings, so he is the firstfruits of firstfruits which are offered not to the high priest but to God; because he offered himself a victim to God, and rising from the dead sits at the right hand of God. And he is called the firstfruits and firstborn of every creature. Whether this ought to be understood so through each creature, as among men he is called and understood the firstfruits of them that sleep, or with a loftier and more divine understanding, it is not for the present time to pursue.
06_marg349: But even if I merited to offer a great sense and worthy of the supreme high priest, so that something excellent out of what we say and teach might please the supreme high priest, the angel who presides over the Church could choose something from all our sayings and offer it to the Lord in place of the firstborn or firstfruits from the little field of our heart. But would that we might not merit to be condemned for the things we say; this grace would suffice us.
06_marg350: ALL THE FIRSTRIPE OF THE FRUITS, etc. AUGUSTINE. All the firstborn things whatsoever shall be in their land, however much they shall offer to the Lord, shall be thine. Here he calls firstborn not the first or firstling young of cattle. For these in Greek are named prototoka or prototosa; but these, protogennemata. But in Latin two names have not been found for these two things, and therefore some have translated these protogennemata as firstfruits. But firstfruits are plainly so called and are something else. These three, therefore, are distinguished thus: that prototoka or prototosa are the firstling young of animals and of men; protogennemata, the first fruits taken from the land or from the tree or from the vine; but firstfruits, from the fruits indeed, but those already brought in from the field, as from the lump, from the vat, from the jar, from the cask, which were taken for firstfruits.
06_interl350: The firstborn are those who are not defiled with women, or the martyrs.
06_marg351: ORIGEN. Perhaps those can be called firstborn who are not defiled with women, or even the martyrs. The virgins too can be called the firstfruits of the Church, and the tithes those who are continent after marriage.
06_interl353: archangels, angels, apostles, and any doctors of the Church
06_marg352: ALL THE FIRSTFRUITS, etc. RABANUS. In both testaments oblations and tithes are assigned to the ministers of the altar for their necessities, lest they should dare to dwell in earthly possessions or seek gain from the ministry. Whence: "Freely have you received, freely give. Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money." But mystically the tithes signify the observance of the law, or the sincerity of the integrity of faith, or the perfection of good work, which those ought most to have who give themselves to the divine ministry. For in the number ten is comprised the knowledge of the creature and of the Creator; because seven looks to human nature, namely three showing the power of the soul. Whence: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole strength." And the body consists of four elements. And if you join seven to the number three, which expresses faith and the confession of the Trinity, you will complete ten.
06_marg353: RABANUS. He names as a covenant of salt the whole of the oblations which pertain to the ministry or the right of the priests. Whence in Leviticus: "Whatsoever sacrifice thou offerest, thou shalt season it with salt" etc. Mystically it is shown that wisdom befits the priests and preachers of the divine law; not worldly but apostolic, of which Paul says: "We speak wisdom among the perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world" etc. Of which it is said to the apostles: "You are the salt of the earth." For as all food is seasoned with salt, so all speech with apostolic wisdom. To Aaron therefore and his sons there is an everlasting covenant of salt, because wisdom is necessary not only to bishops, but also to priests, deacons and all orders; and this before God, that is, that it may please God pure and simple, without cunning and malice. For the wisdom of this world is an enemy to God.
06_interl357: "The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup" etc.
06_marg354: AND THE LORD SPOKE, etc. AUGUSTINE. And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: This is the distinction of the law, whatsoever the Lord has appointed, etc. There is no distinction except between two or more. For singleness does not admit distinction; nor did he mention the distinction of just any thing, but added: of the law; and not of just any law. For it is constantly read in Scripture of each thing of which something is lawfully commanded: This is the law of this or that; not the universal law which contains all things that are lawfully commanded. But here, when he had said: this "is the distinction of the law", he added: "whatsoever the Lord has appointed", namely by commanding, not by creating. For some translated: whatsoever the Lord commanded. If therefore this is the distinction of the law, whatsoever the Lord commands, great is this distinction, and it is rightly understood to understand or distinguish the two testaments. For the same things are in the Old and in the New Testament: there overshadowed, here revealed. For not only are the sacraments different, but also the promises there seem to be set forth as temporal, by which a spiritual reward is secretly signified; but here spiritual and eternal things are manifestly promised. And what more certain distinction is there between temporal and carnal goods and spiritual and eternal ones than the passion of Christ? In whose death it shone out that transitory happiness is not to be hoped for and desired as a great gift, since God, by the only-begotten Son (whom he willed to suffer such things), declared by an open distinction that something far other is to be sought from him and awaited. This passion, therefore, as the distinction of the two testaments, is fittingly enough figured by what is said of the slaying of the red heifer. The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: "This is the distinction of the law, whatsoever the Lord has appointed"; then he begins to command, adding these things, saying: "Speak to the children of Israel." It can also be punctuated thus: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: "This is the distinction of the law, whatsoever the Lord has appointed, saying"; not whatsoever the Lord has appointed in creating, as heaven and earth and sea and all things that are in them, but whatsoever the Lord has appointed in saying, in two, namely, testaments; so that there then follows: Speak to the children of Israel, and let them take to thee a red heifer without blemish. The red heifer signifies the flesh of Christ. The female sex, fleshly weakness; red, bloodied by the passion. And when he says, let them take to thee, he shows in Moses himself the figure of the law; because according to the law they seemed to themselves to kill Christ, because he broke the sabbath and profaned the observances of the law.
06_interl360: because all his working is perfect
06_marg355: By the male strength is signified, by the female weakness. By the cow is figured the weakness of the Lord's incarnation, taken up for sacrifice. For he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God.
06_marg356: A RED COW, red, namely, with the blood of the passion. Whence: "My beloved is white and ruddy." White, namely, from the divinity; ruddy from the blood; white also through justice of life.
06_marg357: Morally. We slay the red cow when we extinguish the flesh from the wantonness of pleasure; which we offer with hyssop, cedar wood and scarlet, because with the mortification of the body we burn the sacrifice of faith, hope and charity.
06_interl361: "Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth."
06_marg358: AUGUSTINE. Without blemish. For the other victims signified this flesh, where likewise cattle without blemish were commanded to be immolated. For he was in the likeness of sinful flesh, but not sinful flesh. But here, where God willed more evidently to commend the distinction of the law, it was too little to say without blemish, unless it were said: which has no blemish in itself. And if it was said for the sake of repetition, perhaps it is not in vain that the repetition itself commended the thing more firmly; although it would not stray from the truth if it is understood to have been added, which has no blemish in itself, when it had already been said, a heifer without blemish, because the flesh of Christ had no blemish in itself, but had it in others, who are his members. For what flesh in this life is without sin save that one alone which had no blemish in itself?
06_marg359: Everyone who sins is the servant of sin; because therefore Christ never sinned, he did not carry the yoke.
06_marg360: And there is no yoke laid upon her, etc. For she was not subjugated to iniquity; finding those subjugated to it, he freed them and broke their bonds. Whence: "Thou hast broken my bonds: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise" etc. For upon his flesh no yoke was laid who had power to lay down his life and to take it up again.
06_marg361: The cow is delivered to the priest to be immolated, because the Lord incarnate made himself a sacrifice for our redemption, given into the hands of the Jewish people.
06_marg362: "And thou shalt give her to Eleazar the priest" etc. Why not to Aaron? Perhaps it was prefigured that the passion of the Lord would come not in the time that then was, but in the posterity of this priesthood.
06_marg363: Morally. No one will be able to immolate the red cow (whose ash is the expiation of the people) save one who has not done earthly works, and has not drawn the yoke of offence, and has not been bound with the chains of sins.
06_marg364: WHO SHALL BRING HER FORTH, etc. AUGUSTINE. Because Christ suffered without the gate, that he might lead us out of the conversation of the present life as out of a city.
06_marg365: And they shall cast her out of the camp. So the Lord, about to suffer, was cast out of the city.
06_marg366: Into a clean place, because he had no evil cause. And they shall slay her in his sight; so the flesh of Christ was slain in the sight of those who were to be the priests of the Lord in the New Testament.
06_marg367: GREGORY. Because Christ was as it were extinguished in the sight of all. He was immolated in the sight of the Father, because what before the eyes of men was punishment, this before the eyes of the Father was sacrifice.
06_marg368: AND DIPPING HIS FINGER, etc. AUGUSTINE. Another text: And Eleazar shall take of her blood and shall sprinkle of her blood seven times over against the face of the testimony. Because Christ according to the Scriptures shed his blood for the remission of sins, therefore over against the face of the tabernacle of the testimony, because it was not made known otherwise than it had been foretold by the divine testimony. And therefore seven times, because that number pertains to spiritual cleansing.
06_marg369: GREGORY. In the finger the discernment of working is signified. To dip the finger in the blood of the cow is to consecrate our works in the passion of the Lord, that we may imitate his passion which we know. For he suffered, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps.
06_marg370: Eleazar the priest immolates and dips his finger in the blood, because the Jewish people, on the part of the reprobate, persecuted the humility of the Lord even to the passion; but in the elect it imitated the working of his humility. And he shall sprinkle over against the door of the tabernacle etc. The tabernacle signifies the synagogue. He therefore who has dipped his finger should sprinkle over against the door of the tabernacle; that is, whoever imitates the ways of his passion should give to the synagogue, which does not believe and resists, a sign of living well by good examples and right preaching.
06_marg371: GREGORY. The same will show to the resisting people, by right preaching and works, the examples of Christ's passion.
06_marg372: Because of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, which through the blood of Christ are distributed over the peoples of the Church, in which they are purged from every offence.
06_marg373: Seven times, etc. In the number seven perfection is signified or understood. Whence also all time is completed in seven days, and the Holy Ghost is called sevenfold. To dip the finger in the blood seven times, therefore, is to imitate the mystery of the passion by perfect working. And to sprinkle seven times over against the synagogue is to announce the passion to unbelievers by perfect preaching.
06_marg374: SHALL BURN HER IN THE SIGHT OF ALL, etc. GREGORY. By the skin and flesh and blood and dung are signified the sacrifices held in the Old Testament which announced the weakness of the Lord. Because all of them, understood afterwards spiritually by the fathers, are called dung according to the outward mystery. Whence Paul: "I count all things as dung"; which are delivered to the flame. For though at first they were shown forth carnally, afterwards through the Holy Ghost they were consumed by the fire of understanding.
06_marg375: And they shall burn her in his sight. I think that the burning pertains to the sign of the resurrection. For it is the nature of fire to move upward, and that which is burned is turned into it. For the very word cremare is a word brought from Greek into Latin, from hanging up. And what is added, in his sight, that is, in the sight of the priest, seems to signify that the resurrection of Christ appeared to those who were to be of the royal priesthood.
06_marg376: HER SKIN, etc. AUGUSTINE. And what follows, her skin and flesh and her blood with the dung shall be burned, sets forth how she shall be burned; and it is signified that not only the substance of the mortal body of Christ, which is intimated by the mention of skin and flesh and blood, but also the contumely and abjection of the people, which is signified in the dung, will be turned into glory, which the flame of the burning signifies.
06_marg377: By the skin and flesh the outward working of Christ is signified. By the blood, the subtle and inner power quickening the outward deeds. By the dung, weariness, thirst, hunger and the fear of death, and whatever he willed to suffer from humanity. For whatever he had from the defect of mortality was as dung in him, to be cast away; all which are to be burned with fire, that is, to be understood according to the truth of the Holy Ghost, so that the things he did bodily may be perceived as ordered by the incorporeal spirit of the Godhead.
06_marg378: The cedar is a tall and incorruptible wood. Hyssop is a very lowly herb, which yet warns against the swelling of the lung. By the cedar, therefore, lofty persevering contemplation is signified; by hyssop, the humility of a meek heart. For he who is raised by contemplation to heavenly things ought to condescend to the lower by the compassion of humility; nor should he lift himself up because of what he has, but should gladly spend it in preaching on those who have it not.
06_marg379: And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet and cast them into the midst of the burning of the heifer etc. The cedar wood is hope, which dwells firmly in heavenly things. Hyssop is faith, which is a lowly herb clinging with its roots to the rock. Scarlet is charity, which bears witness to the fervour of the spirit by its fiery colour. These three we ought to cast into the resurrection of Christ, as into the midst of that burning, that our life may be hidden with him.
06_marg380: By the cedar can be understood hope, which seeks lofty things. By hyssop (which by its smell also purges the uncleanness of the stomach), faith, which bears adverse things with very even mind and cleanses whatever had been contracted from former sins. And by the scarlet, charity. Let each of us, therefore, cast into the flame which devours the cow the cedar, the hyssop and the scarlet twice dyed; that is, let him show forth faith, hope and charity in the sacrifice of the Lord's passion, lest he hear of the passion of his Redeemer to no purpose. Hence Paul: "And now there remain faith, hope, and charity: but the greater of these is charity." Whence here too the scarlet is put last, because when faith and hope are completed and we have come to the eternal fatherland, charity alone will be multiplied in us at the last.
06_marg381: Let the cedar be cast into the flame which devours the cow; that is, let the perseverance and loftiness of our contemplation be burned with the fire of the Lord's passion. Let the hyssop be cast in; that is, let the humility of our heart draw the truth of meekness from mingling with the Lord's passion. Let the scarlet twice dyed be cast in; that is, let the charity which rouses us to love God and our neighbour compel us to contemplate the Lord's passion continually, that in it it may learn the right works it is to do.
06_marg382: ISIDORE. Baptism, because they were sprinkled with hyssop dipped in the blood of the lamb.
06_marg383: ISIDORE. The scarlet twice dyed is the blood of Christ, by which we are washed in mind and body. These three purge: the cedar, that is, the faith of the cross; hyssop, baptism or martyrdom; scarlet, the sacrament of the Lord's blood.
06_marg384: In the scarlet twice dyed the virtue of charity is expressed, which, kindled by the flame of holy love, is commanded to be shown forth by two precepts, namely the love of God and of neighbour. The scarlet therefore is twice dyed when charity is formed by the twofold precept, so that God is loved in such a way that the neighbour is not forsaken, and the neighbour in such a way that God is not despised.
06_marg385: GREGORY. All of us who believe in Christ are priests. Whence: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc. The lofty things, therefore, which we reach by contemplation, and what we do from the meekness of humility, and what we show forth through the fire of charity, we ought to dip in the blood of Christ's passion, so that all that is in us may imitate him from whom it is; because outside the imitation of the passion it is not so much virtue as vice.
06_marg386: This priest who burns the cow's flesh, skin, blood and dung can signify the order of the Jewish priesthood, with the people under it, consenting to the death of the Lord. Whence it follows: And then after washing his garments and his body.
06_marg387: AND THEN AFTER, etc. THE SAME. It can be understood that this priest is both washed in his garments and yet unclean until the evening, because the Jewish people, on the part of those who believed, is clean; on the part of those who did not believe, remains unclean until the evening. He washes his garments and body, therefore, because by believing he cleanses his outward works and inner mind from wicked actions; and he returns fully to the camp then, when he is called back perfectly at the end. But because, while Judea partly persists in unbelief, the Gentile world enters into faith and understands the mysteries of the divine incarnation, he rightly adds: And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the cow etc.
06_marg388: The priest shall wash his garments and wash his body with water, and afterwards shall enter the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the evening. The washing of the garments and the body is the cleansing of the outward and inward things; this is the priest. Then follows: He who burns her shall wash his garments and wash his body with water, and shall be unclean until the evening. In him who burns her I think those are figured who buried the flesh of Christ, committing it to the resurrection as to a burning.
06_interl364: cleansed, namely, by the water of baptism and by penance
06_interl367: the end of the world: then indeed the remnant shall be saved.
06_marg389: AUGUSTINE. At evening the priest enters, because the unbelieving people, which until the evening, that is, the end of the world, is set outside the commandments of life as outside the camp, defiled with wicked works, washed by the water of baptism and by penance, returns to knowledge at the end of the world as into the camp.
06_interl368: Those who offer the heifer are unclean, and those who laid hold of Christ.
06_interl373: The Gentile, clean by faith; whence: "Purifying their hearts by faith."
06_marg390: AND SHALL GATHER UP. AUGUSTINE. And a clean man shall gather the ashes of the heifer, the remains, namely, of the slaying and of the burning, that is, the fame which followed the passion and resurrection of Christ; because there are remains for the peaceable man. Christ was ashes, because he was condemned by the unbelieving as dead; and yet he cleansed, because he was believed to have risen by the unbelieving. And because this fame shone out most among the other nations, which were not of the fellowship of the Jews, it is said: a clean man shall gather the ashes of the heifer; clean, namely, from the slaying of Christ, which made the Jews guilty. And he shall lay them up in a clean place, that is, shall handle them honourably; yet without the camp, because the gospel word shone out outside the celebration of the Jewish custom.
06_marg391: The priest burns the cow, a clean man gathers the ashes; because the Jew slew the weakness of the Lord, the Gentile understands his subtle mysteries.
06_marg392: They are clean who preach the passion of Christ to the Gentiles.
06_interl374: the most subtle sacraments of the incarnation
06_marg393: Because the Gentile does not cease to preach the sacraments which he has come to know, but makes them manifest to those who know them not.
06_marg394: The clean man pours out the ashes of the cow in a most pure place when any learned man taken from among the Gentiles seeks out the hearts of the Gentiles made clean through humility and does not cease to hand on to them the mysteries of the Redeemer. And when this is done the faith of the Gentiles is multiplied, the divine power is known, the discipline of the precepts is held. Whence he adds: that they may be reserved for the multitude of the children of Israel. For Israel is interpreted a man seeing God, and the Gentile world well converted is called Israel, which now contemplates God by faith.
06_marg395: Because all the Gentile world is outside the law, outside the sacrifice, outside the synagogue.
06_marg396: Because the secrets of the Lord's incarnation are not to be handed on to wicked and polluted minds, but to those who, coming to the faith, have cleansed their heart.
06_marg397: AUGUSTINE. Another text: And it shall be to the congregation of the children of Israel for keeping. The water of aspersion is purification. Afterwards he declares more fully how the water of aspersion was made from this ash, by which they were cleansed from contact with the dead, that is, from the iniquity of this dying or deathly life. But what follows is strange. And he who gathers, it says, the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until the evening. How shall he be made unclean by this, who came to it clean? Unless that those also who seem to themselves clean in the Christian faith acknowledge that all have sinned and need the glory of God, being justified freely by his blood. Yet he said that this man washes his garments, not his body also. I believe that by the gathering of that ash and laying it up in a clean place (if these things are understood spiritually) he wishes him to be understood as already cleansed within. As Cornelius, hearing and believing what Peter preached, was so cleansed that before visible baptism he received, with his own who were present, the gift of the Holy Ghost also. But neither could the visible sacrament be despised, so that being washed outwardly too he should in a manner wash his garments.
06_marg398: Because the more subtle sacraments, handed on to the clean hearts of the Gentiles, are turned into a fortification of the mind. Because while we attend by imitation to the secret and subtle things of his working, we provide cleanness for ourselves by this.
06_marg399: On account of working, the ashes are for our keeping; but on account of baptism, for a water of aspersion.
06_marg400: Then we providently keep the ashes for our keeping when we carefully consider our Redeemer, who suffered for our iniquities. For we weigh what he will render to the good, who willed to die for the wicked; what we, brought to the justice of faith, owe to his grace, who, set in iniquity, received the intercession of his death.
06_interl376: some stain of this life being contracted, even after full remission of sins
06_marg401: AUGUSTINE. And it shall be to the children of Israel and to the proselytes who are added an everlasting ordinance, etc. What else does it show but the baptism of Christ, which the water of aspersion signified, to be of profit to both Jews and Gentiles, that is, to the children of Israel and to the proselytes, as to the natural branches and to the wild olive grafted into the fatness of the root? But whom does it not move that after the washing it is said of each one: and he shall be unclean until the evening? Not here only, but in all or nearly all such cleansings; where I do not know what is to be understood, except that every man, after the fullest remission of sins, by remaining in this life contracts something whereby he is unclean until the end of life, where this day is in a manner closed, which the evening signifies.
06_interl378: as grafted into the fatness of the root
06_marg402: AUGUSTINE. He that toucheth the dead body, etc. He begins to say how men made unclean are purified by that water of aspersion. He that toucheth, it says, a dead man, every soul of a man, shall be unclean seven days. This one shall be purified on the third and on the seventh day, and shall be clean. And here I understand nothing else than that the touching of a dead man is iniquity. And I think the uncleanness of seven days is said on account of soul and body: the soul in the number three, the body in the number four; according to which I think it is said by the prophet: For three crimes and for four I will not turn.
06_interl379: that Christ may be believed to have risen from the dead on the third day
06_interl380: in the kingdom, namely, of the saints, the Lord coming
06_marg403: IF ON THE THIRD DAY, etc. AUGUSTINE. But if he is not purified on the third day and the seventh day, he shall not be clean; everyone who has touched a dead man, of any soul of a body, and has died having touched the dead before he is or has been purified, defiles the tabernacle of the Lord; that soul shall be cut off from Israel. It is to be noted that it is very hard to find in these books anything written more evidently of the life of the soul after death. Here, then, when he says that if he has died before purification, the uncleanness remains on him and that soul is cut off from Israel, that is, from the fellowship of the people of God, what else does he wish to be understood than that punishment remains for the soul even after death, if while it lives it has not been cleansed by this sacrament by which the baptism of Christ is figured? Because the water of aspersion, it says, has not been sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him. Still, that is, even after death.
06_interl381: fortified, namely, by faith in this grace
06_interl382: from the kingdom of the saints
06_marg404: As far as in him lies; according to that: Extinguish not the spirit, though that cannot be extinguished. For if he wished the tabernacle to be understood as made unclean by this, he would command it to be cleansed.
06_marg405: GREGORY. The covering of the lid or the binding is the censure of discipline; whoever is not held down by it is rejected as an unclean and polluted vessel. For he is defiled as a vessel without lid or binding who, lying open through the pursuit of display, is covered by no veil of silence.
06_marg406: AUGUSTINE. Another text: Everyone who touches upon the face of the field one wounded, or dead, or the bone of a slain man, or a tomb, etc. It is asked what he understands by wounded, or dead? For if he meant one thing by wounded and another by dead, care must be taken lest he who touches a living wounded man be thought unclean too; which is surely absurd. But because the dead also can be wounded, he is understood to have distinguished the dead themselves, so that we understand either a wounded dead man, that is, one killed by a wound, or one dead without a wound.
06_interl387: a minister of Christ, that is, one who bears his person
06_marg407: HE SHALL WASH BOTH HIMSELF, etc. And he shall wash his garments, and shall be washed with water, and shall be unclean until the evening. The water of aspersion is one thing, and that with which he washed his garments another. And he shall be washed with water, which I think is to be understood as spiritual, by signification, not by its proper nature. For without doubt it was visible, like all the shadows of things to come. But he who is rightly washed by the sacrament of baptism (which that water of aspersion figured) is cleansed spiritually, so that he is clean in body and spirit. And as to his saying that the water of aspersion is sprinkled with hyssop, which herb we have said signifies faith, what else occurs but what is written: "Purifying their hearts by faith"? For baptism does not profit if faith is lacking. And he said these things are done by a clean man, where the ministers are signified who bear the person of the Lord, who is truly the clean man. For of these ministers he will say in what follows: And whoever sprinkles the water of aspersion shall wash his garments, that is, shall keep them, and in body. And he who touches the water of aspersion shall be unclean until the evening; and whatever the unclean man touches shall be unclean, and the soul that touches it shall be unclean until the evening.
06_marg408: AND THE CHILDREN CAME, etc. ISIDORE. The thirty-third station is in the desert of Sin; this is Cades. And Sin is interpreted "holy", by antiphrasis, as a grove is called lucus when it is least lucid, or war bellum when it is horrid. At this station Mary dies and is buried, who signifies prophecy dead; as Moses and Aaron signify the end of the law and of the priesthood, which cannot come to the land of promise nor lead the people out of the wilderness of this world; which Christ alone does, that is, the Saviour, the Son of God.
06_interl390: the Jew placed under the law of Moses
06_interl391: fastening him to the wood of the cross
06_marg409: AUGUSTINE. That water was brought out of the rock the Apostle explained, saying: "And all drank the same spiritual drink: and they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them; and the rock was Christ." Signified, therefore, is the spiritual grace flowing from Christ, by which the inner thirst is watered. But that the rock is struck with the rod figures the cross of Christ; for when the wood came to the rock grace flowed; and that it is struck twice signifies the cross more evidently. For the cross is two pieces of wood.
06_interl392: because of the two pieces of wood of the same cross
06_marg410: ISIDORE. Here Moses offends the Lord and is forbidden to cross the Jordan; for, troubled by the murmuring of the people, he struck the rock with the rod doubtingly, as though God could not bring water out of the rock, which he had done before. Here Moses signifies the Jewish people placed under the law. For as Moses, striking the rock with the rod, doubted of the power of God, so that people, placed under the law given through Moses, fastened Christ to the wood of the cross, but did not believe him to be the power of God. But as from the stricken rock water flowed for the thirsty, so the wound of the Lord's passion was made life for believers. This carnal doubting of the divinity of God, therefore, God commands to die in the height of Christ himself, when he orders the death of Moses' flesh to take place on the mountain. For as Christ is the rock, so also the mountain: Christ the rock, lowly strength; the mountain, eminent greatness. For the prudence of the flesh lives when the humility of Christ in the cross is despised, as a rock that is struck; for Christ crucified is unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness. The prudence of the flesh dies when Christ is acknowledged exalted, as the eminence of a mountain. For unto them that are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
06_marg411: THIS IS THE WATER, etc. AUGUSTINE. What is said of that water which flowed from the rock: This is the water of contradiction, because the children of Israel railed before the Lord, and he was sanctified in them. First they railed when they spoke against the benefit of God by which they had been brought out of Egypt; and afterwards he was sanctified in them, when his holiness was declared in the miracle. Or perhaps he showed two kinds of men, those who contradict the grace of Christ and those who receive it, so that to the former it is the water of contradiction. For of him it is said: "for a sign which shall be contradicted".
06_interl395: freely, namely; but: we will pay the price; which he declares in what follows.
06_marg412: The thirty-fourth station is at mount Hor, in the furthest borders of Edom, into which Aaron went up according to the command of the Lord. And he died in the fortieth year of the going out of Israel from Egypt, namely when the new people was about to enter the land of promise. And although on the mountain he left the priesthood to his son Eleazar, and the law brings those who have fulfilled it to the summit, yet that very loftiness is not beyond the Jordan, but in the furthest borders of earthly works. And the people mourns him thirty days. Aaron is mourned; but Jesus is not mourned. In the law is the descent to hell; in the Gospel, the ascent to Paradise.
06_marg413: AND WHEN HE HAD HEARD. The Chanaanite heard that Israel had come to the place of the spies, where once the people had offended; he joined battle and led Israel captive. And again in the same place there is fighting; by a vow the victor is vanquished, the vanquished overcome. In which it is understood that when enemies have attacked us, destitute of the help of God, and taken us captive, we should not despair; for it may come about that we conquer where we were conquered.
06_marg414: AUGUSTINE. And he anathematized him and his cities, and the name of that place was called Anathema; so that the victor should carry off nothing thence for his own uses, but vow the whole to punishment. For to anathematize is what is commonly called to devote. And the origin of this word is in the Greek tongue, from those things which, vowed and paid, that is, promised and rendered, were set up aloft in the temples: apotoianathome, that is, to set up aloft, either by fixing or by hanging.
06_marg415: THEY MARCHED, etc. The thirty-fifth station is in Salmona. The thirty-sixth station is in Phinon. These two are not found in the order of the history. In these, Aaron being dead, Israel murmurs against God and Moses, loathes the manna, is wounded by serpents. And beautifully is Salmona interpreted "little image", because there the image of Christ was expressed by the brazen serpent which hung on the wood. And Phinon is interpreted "mouth", because when we know his passion, what we believe with the heart we pronounce with the mouth. For with the heart we believe unto justice, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
06_marg416: MAKE A BRAZEN SERPENT, etc. ISIDORE. The bites of the serpents were healed when the brazen serpent was lifted up and looked upon, because Christ triumphed over the ancient serpent on the gibbet and shut out his poisons, so that he who truly and expressly looks upon the image of the Son of God and his passion may be healed. Whence: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert" etc. The brazen serpent is hung on the wood because brass is more durable than the other metals; and Christ, dead through his humanity in the serpent, lives through his divinity, as being of brass.
06_marg417: AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SETTING FORWARDS CAMPED, etc. The thirty-seventh station is in Oboth, which is rendered "magicians" or "pythons". Because after the image of God, which is shown in the reason of the heart, and the confession of faith, which is uttered with the mouth, serpents and evil arts rise up. But let us, keeping our heart with all watchfulness, stop our ears, that we may not hear the voices of enchanters and the songs of the sirens.
06_marg418: AND DEPARTING THENCE, etc. JEROME. In Jeabarim, a heap, namely of stones passing over. These are the saints who hasten to pass through this world to other stations. For there are holy stones which roll over the earth, light and polished, and by their roundness like the wheels of chariots. There are others to be taken out of the way, lest they strike the feet of those who walk. Whence Isaias: "Lift up the stones from the head of the streets."
06_marg419: And as to its being said, in the borders of Moab, and written above, in the wilderness of Moab, which faces Moab toward the rising of the sun, it shows according to the letter that up to this point they were in the borders of the Edomites, and now come to the boundary of Moab, from one province, namely, to another. For not always is one virtue to be striven after; but one must go from virtue to virtue and pass from one to another. For they cleave to one another and are so joined that he who lacks one lacks all. And this belongs properly to those who consider the rising of the sun of justice.
06_marg420: THEY CAME TO THE TORRENT ZARED, etc. The thirty-ninth station was in Dibongad, as is written in the series of the stations, which is interpreted "temptation strongly understood". But in place of this, in the order of the history, it is said that from Jeabarim they came to the torrent Zared. Then they camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness of the borders of the Amorrhite, on the boundaries of the Moabites and the Amorrhites. And afterwards they came to the well where they sang this song: "Spring up, O well, which the princes dug" etc. And from the wilderness to Mathana, then to the torrents of God, and after to the high places, and from the high places to the valley which is in the country of Moab. Some, interpreting these places in the borders of the Amorrhites, think they are not stations but crossings, and that an extraordinary exposition ought not to prejudge the catalogue of the stations. Others, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, will not have regions signified, but by the names of the places the progress of virtues: that after the magicians and the gatherings of stones we often come to the torrent Zared, which is interpreted "a strange descent", and placed in the descent pass over to the Arnon, that is, the curse, which is set in the borders of the Amorrhites, who are bitter enemies, or speak much. And if we pass the boundaries of Moab (who was born or begotten of incest and departed from the true father), there meets us the well which no common or ignoble man dug, but princes and leaders, who prophesy singing where they are to pass over in the desert, namely to Mathana, that is, the house of Juda; to Nahaliel, that is, the torrents of God; then to Bamoth, which is interpreted "high places" or "death coming", when we are made conformable to the death of Christ. Afterwards there meets us the valley of humility, which yet is set on the top of mount Phasga, which is interpreted "hewn", namely having nothing shapeless or rough, which looks toward the wilderness, which in Hebrew is called Sinen; because, set on the summit of the virtues, we look upon the ruins of the whole world and the desolation of all sins. Dibongad is interpreted "temptation strongly understood". After Dibongad there is fighting against Sehon king of the Amorrhites and Og king of Basan. And when we have come to the summit and have drunk from the fountain of the princes, going up the mountains of Phasga, let us not be proud, but fear the wilderness set before us.
06_marg421: AUGUSTINE. He did not say in what book it is written, or of what prophet or patriarch; nor is it to be denied that there were already books, either of the Chaldeans, whence Abraham came out, or of the Egyptians, where Moses had learned all their wisdom, or of any other nation, in some one of which books this could have been written. Yet it is not therefore to be taken into those scriptures to which divine authority is committed. For it was lawful for divine authority to take a true testimony whence it would; but it does not therefore confirm that all things written there are to be received. But why this is mentioned in this place does not plainly appear, unless perhaps, since a war was waged so that boundaries should be set there between two nations, the men of that place said because of its greatness that it was a war of the Lord, so that it was written in some book of theirs: the war of the Lord.
06_marg422: WHEN THEY WENT FROM THAT PLACE, THE WELL APPEARED WHEREOF THE LORD SAID, etc. ORIGEN. What is it that the Lord earnestly commands Moses to gather the people, that he may give them waters from the well to drink? As though they would not come together of their own accord to drink. The Spirit says through Solomon in the Proverbs: "Drink water out of thy own cistern, and the streams of thy own well; and let not the waters overflow thee outside thy fountain." Although in other copies we have read: "and let thy waters be poured out outside thy well." Each one therefore has within himself a well, nay many wells and many vessels of water. Whence he says: "Out of thy own vessels and out of the fountain of thy wells." Abraham had wells, and Isaac. In the Gospel the Saviour sat upon a well, resting after his labour and saying: "That if anyone drinks of the waters which the earthly well contained, he will thirst again. But whoever drinks of those which Jesus gives, there will become in him a fountain of living water, springing up into life everlasting." And elsewhere it is said: "He that believeth in him, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water." He therefore who believes in him will have in himself not a well but wells, not only fountains but rivers; not such as are wont to bestow mortal life, but such as bestow eternal. According to these things, therefore, which we read in the Proverbs, "where wells with a fountain are numbered or named, the word of God is to be understood": a well, if it covers a deep mystery; a fountain, if it flows out to the peoples. And it is to be asked how Wisdom in the Proverbs speaks of wells in the plural and of a fountain in the singular: "Drink waters from the fountain of thy wells?" Let us see, therefore, of what wells he called one the fountain. I think that the knowledge of the unbegotten Father can be understood as one well, and the knowledge of the only-begotten Son as another; for the Son is other than the Father, nor the same as the Father. Whence: "It is another that beareth witness of me, the Father." The third well is the knowledge of the Holy Ghost; for the Spirit is other than the Father and the Son. Whence: "The Father will send you another Paraclete, the Spirit of truth." There is therefore this distinction of three persons in the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost, which is brought back to the plural number of wells; of which there is one fountain, because there is one substance and nature of the Trinity.
06_marg423: Those wells also can be seen of whose knowledge he speaks who was filled with the Wisdom of God: For he hath given me the true knowledge of the things that are, that I should know the knowledge of the world, and the virtues of the elements, the beginning and ending and midst of the times, the alterations of their courses and the changes of seasons, the revolutions of the year and the dispositions of the stars, the natures of living creatures and the rage of wild beasts etc. You see how many wells there are in the knowledge of things. There is a well, the knowledge of plants; and perhaps the nature of each plant has its own well. Again there is a well, the knowledge of animals; and perhaps each species of animals has its own well; and each of these (since they have a deep knowledge) are rightly said to be wells. And while the mystery of Christ was hidden from ages and generations, the knowledge of these things is rightly called wells. But when God has made them manifest to believers through the Holy Ghost, all these become fountains and rivers, so that the knowledge of them is no longer held in secret, but waters believers and satisfies them. Therefore, I believe, the Saviour said that he who believes in him and drinks the water of his doctrine, in him there will be no longer a well nor a fountain, but rivers of living water. For as one well, that is, the word of God, becomes wells and fountains and rivers, so the soul of man, which is to the image of God, can have in itself and bring forth wells and fountains and rivers. But the wells which are in our soul need one to dig them, that they may be cleansed and what is earthy be taken away, so that those veins of rational senses which God has set in them may bring forth pure and sincere streams. For while earth covers them, the pure wave of water cannot flow forth. Therefore it is written that the servants of Abraham dug wells, but the Philistines covered them with earth. Isaac too, who had received his father's inheritance, dug his father's wells and removed the earth which the Philistines had thrown in. And note that while Abraham lived the Philistines dared not fill up the wells or throw earth in; but when he was dead they grew strong and laid snares for his wells; but they are restored by Isaac. The servant of Abraham too found Rebecca at the wells, who is interpreted "patience". She becomes the wife of Isaac, but at the wells. Likewise Jacob, when he came to Mesopotamia having his father's command not to take a foreign wife, found Rachel at the wells, and Moses Sephora. If therefore you have understood what and of what kind are the wives of the saints, if you wish to lead or take patience in marriage, or wisdom and the other virtues of the soul, and to say what is said of wisdom: Her have I sought to take for my bride, be constantly about these wells, and there you will find a spouse of this kind; because it is certain that the virtues dwell by the streams of the living word. There are therefore many wells within the soul, and very many others in each of the words and senses of the scriptures. This one, then, is the more eminent, which not any men whatever dug, but princes, and those higher than these whom he called kings. Therefore hymns are sung to God at this well; and it is written that this is the well whereof the Lord said to Moses: Gather the people, and I will give them water from the well.
06_marg424: Allegorically. The law calls you to the well, Christ, namely the Son of God, subsisting indeed in his own substance, yet named with the Father and the Spirit by the one fountain of the Godhead. To this well, therefore, that is, to the faith of Christ, the law calls you together. Whence he himself says that Moses wrote of me. And it calls us that we may drink the waters and sing a song to him; that is, believe with the heart unto justice and confess with the mouth unto salvation.
06_interl399: SEPTUAGINT: Begin to him the well; that is: confess the well to be at the beginning of all things.
06_marg425: ORIGEN. Begin to him the well; that is, set the well as the beginning of all things, because he himself is the beginning and the firstborn of every creature.
06_marg426: Or thus: so that the words are directed from the person of Moses to the people. Give a beginning to your heart, that you may begin to understand what the well is from which the spiritual waters are to be drawn and the people of believers refreshed. Begin, therefore, to him, that is, to Israel, this well, so that if anyone sees God with the heart he may draw the mystic sense from the depths. To this well Moses, that is, the law, gathers; to which someone seems to come, but unless he is gathered by Moses he is not accepted by God. Marcion seems to himself to have come, and Basilides and Valentinus; but because they did not come through Moses, nor received the law and the prophets, they cannot praise God from the fountains of Israel. Such, therefore, do not come to the well which the princes dug and the kings hewed out. And there is a salt valley in which there are wells of bitumen. And every heresy and every sin is in the valley, and in the salt valley. For sin does not go up on high, but always descends to the depths and to the lower things. Every heretical sense, therefore, and every act of sin is set in the valley, salt and bitter. For what sweet, what pleasant thing can sin have? But if you have come to a heretical opinion and the bitterness of sin, you have come to the wells of bitumen, which is the food and nourishment of fire. If you taste the water of these wells, if you receive a heretical sense and the bitterness of sin, you will prepare in yourself the fuel of fire and the burnings of gehenna. To such it is said: "Walk in the light of your fire" etc. The princes dug it and the kings hewed it out. The princes therefore dug, the kings hewed out; which is said from hewing out, not from cutting down. For that is said to be hewn out which is cut or shaped in stone. The princes, as being lower, dug, that is, sank a certain depth as into the softness of earth. But these whom he calls kings, as stronger, penetrate not only the depth of the earth but the hardness of the rock, that they may reach the deeper waters and search out the very veins of the abyss, knowing that the judgments of God are a great deep. These are the apostles, one of whom says: "But to us God hath revealed them by his Spirit." For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. Those, therefore, who through the Holy Ghost can search the deep things and penetrate the profound mysteries of the well are said to be kings, who hewed out the well in the rock, because they penetrated the hard and difficult secrets of knowledge. The princes therefore dug this well and the kings of the nations hewed it out, that is, the apostles, who gathered the nations to obedience of faith and opened to all the knowledge of Christ, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. For they fulfilled the command of God, teaching all nations and baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. And by this they hewed out, that is, laid open, the knowledge of the well. These things too which we have in hand are a well for us, and all the scripture of the law and the prophets, the gospel too and the apostolic, together are one well, which none can dig or hew out but kings and princes, who namely can take away the earth and remove the surface of the letter, and from the lower rock, where Christ is, bring forth spiritual senses as living water. They are called kings because they have expelled the kingdom of sin and set the kingdom of justice in their members. For it befits him to teach the rest who has first done what he teaches. Whence: "He that shall do and teach, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven." And to be great in the kingdom is to be a king.
06_marg427: The same can be called princes and kings; or we understand the prophets as princes. For they set the sense and prophecy of Christ, buried, in the depth of the letter. Therefore it is said of them: "But if you will not hear in secret, your soul shall weep." And elsewhere: "O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!" The kings are the apostles, who search the deep things of God and rule the churches. Whence Christ too is called King of kings.
06_marg428: ORIGEN. The kings of the nations, it says, hewed it out in their kingdom, while they ruled over them. For they cannot dig this well, nor open the hidden veins of living water, unless they are first lords of the barbarous nations. Whatever was wild in them in their acts, whatever barbarous in their manners, they tamed and subjected to the royal sense, that they might act not in the manner of the Gentiles but lawfully. These truly are kings, probing the depths of the well and searching out the secrets of the word of God.
06_marg429: ORIGEN. Setting out from the well they came to Mathana, which is interpreted "their gifts". For God asks faith and affection from man. Whence: "And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but that thou fear the Lord, and walk in his ways, and love him" etc. These gifts must be given by us to the Lord after we have drunk the knowledge of his goodness from the depth of the well. And note that the prophet says "require of thee", that those may blush who deny that it is in the choice of man to be saved. For how would God require of man, unless man had in his power what he ought to offer to him who requires it? There are therefore things that are given by God and things given by man. It was in man to make five pounds of one; from God, that man should have the pound from which he could make ten pounds. And when he had offered from himself, he received from God no longer money but power and the kingdom of ten cities. God asked Abraham to offer him his son. He offered him fearlessly, laid him on the altar, drew the knife to slay him; but at once he is stopped, and a ram is given instead of his son for the victim. You see, therefore, that the things we offer to God remain to us; but they are required of us that our affection and faith may be proved.
06_marg430: He who drinks from this well advances to this, that he has gifts to offer to God, of which it is said in the law: "My gifts, my presents." From the things, therefore, which God has given, there is offering to God. And he gave the knowledge of himself, and man offers him his faith and affection.
06_marg431: When we have offered the things that are from God, we obtain the things that are from God. For when we have offered our faith and affection, then he bestows the divers gifts of the Holy Ghost, of which it is said: "But all things are of God."
06_marg432: Bamoth, the coming of death; by which, namely, we die with him that we may live with him, and mortify our members which are upon the earth. For we are buried together with him by baptism into death. For he who keeps the order of the saving way ought to make his journey through each of these and after many to come to this place.
06_marg433: ORIGEN. The same, and from Bamoth, it says, into the grove which is in the plain of Moab, from the top of the mount of Cesi, which looks toward the desert. If we walk by this journey, which consists not so much in the names of places as in the progress of the soul, after all things we come into the grove, or according to others into Ranan, which is interpreted "ascent" or "top of the mountain". Through these things, therefore, one comes to that famous grove of paradise and the pleasant delights of the ancient dwelling, or to the summit of perfection and beatitude, so that we may say that he has raised us up together with him and made us sit in the heavenly places with Christ. You see how far one comes from the well; by what stations, nay progresses, the journey of the soul to heaven is prepared.
06_marg434: THE SAME. Israel sends ambassadors to the king of the Amorrhites, namely the proud king, who said: "By the strength of my own hand I have done it, and by my own wisdom I have understood, and have removed the bounds of the people" etc. And: "I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars" etc. That proud and lifted-up one too is as it were his only-begotten, of whom it is written: "Who is lifted up above all that is called God, or that is worshipped" etc. Every one, therefore, who is lifted up is a son of this lifted-up one, or his disciple and imitator. Whence: "Lest being puffed up he fall into the judgment of the devil." In which it is shown that every one lifted up will be condemned like the devil. We therefore, who wish to pass through this world that we may come to the holy land promised to the saints, send with peaceable words to Sehon, promising that we will not dwell in his land nor tarry with him, but only pass through, going by the king's way, or the royal way, turning aside nowhere, neither into field nor into vineyard, nor drinking of his vat. For when we come to the water of baptism and receive the seals of the first faith, we renounce the devil and his pomps and all his works and all his services and pleasures; which is foreshadowed when it is said: "That Israel turn not aside into his field nor into his vineyard, nor drink of his vat." For the faithful no longer drinks of diabolical discipline, not of astrological, not of magical, or of that doctrine which is against the piety of God. For he has his own fountains, and will drink of the fountains of Israel, of the fountains of the Saviour, not of the vat of Sehon. Nor, leaving the fountain of living water, does he gather to himself broken or crushed cisterns.
06_interl404: that is, of the unbelieving, namely who lead God into bitterness
06_marg435: Sehon, who is interpreted "unfruitful tree" or "lifted up". This is the king of the Amorrhites, who are interpreted "leading into bitterness" or "speaking". This is the devil, lifted up and unfruitful, of whom it is said: "The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing." And elsewhere: "Now shall the prince of this world be cast out"; not because he created the world, but because sinners are in the world. And he himself is the prince of sin, according to what is said: "That the whole world is seated in wickedness", and he himself is the prince of the world.
06_interl405: diabolical discipline, or that contrary to piety
06_marg436: THE KING'S HIGHWAY, etc. Who says: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life." Of whom it is said: "Give to the king thy judgment, O God." By this one must walk and turn aside nowhere, neither into field nor into vineyard; that is, neither to diabolical works nor to diabolical senses; we wish to pass peaceably through the world. But this rather stirs up the prince of the world, that we say we do not wish to remain with him or tarry or touch anything of his. Thence he is angry and moves persecutions and threatens perils of torment. Thence he says: "Sehon gathered his people" etc.
06_marg437: With princes, namely, and judges of the world, and all the ministers of wickedness, who always assail the people of God.
06_marg438: In Jasa or Isaar, which is interpreted "fulfilment of the commandment". For if we come to the fulfilment of the commandments, we overcome the proud and lifted-up one. For to fulfil the commandment is to overcome the devil and his army. For nothing will be able to harm us if we come into Isaar, that is, if we keep the precepts of our Lord Jesus Christ.
06_marg439: "For the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two edged sword" etc. Of which the Apostle says: "And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God." By the edge of this falls Sehon, that is, the devil.
06_marg440: Every earthly region is called the land of Sehon. But Christ and his Church have dominion in all the land of Sehon.
06_marg441: Jeboc is a city and the end of the kingdom of Sehon, as the Arnon is its beginning. And Arnon is interpreted "their curses"; Jeboc, "wrestling". For he who wishes to go out of the kingdom of the devil must wrestle with his ministers. But if he has conquered, Jeboc will no longer be the city of Sehon but of Israel. Hence Jacob, when he had come to a certain place, a contest was prepared for him, and having wrestled there all night, when he had prevailed his name was called Israel.
06_marg442: SO ISRAEL TOOK, etc. AUGUSTINE. Here Israel possessed the cities of the Amorrhites which it overcame in war, because it did not anathematize them. For if it had anathematized them, it could not possess them, nor take anything thence for its own uses. And note how just wars were waged: for an inoffensive passage was refused, which was owed by the right of human society; but now, that God might fulfil his commands or promises, he helped the Israelites here, to whom the land of the Amorrhites was to be given. For when Edom likewise refused passage, the Israelites did not fight with that nation, that is, the sons of Jacob with the sons of Esau, because he had not promised that land to the Israelites; but they turned aside from them.
06_marg443: He who is Israel in Christ, not in the flesh, but seeing openly, dwells in all the cities of the Amorrhites, when the churches of Christ are spread through the whole world. But each of us too was formerly a city of king Sehon, who is interpreted "lifted up". For folly, pride, impiety and all things that are on the side of the devil reigned in us.
