But when the strong man was overcome and his goods plundered, we were made cities of Israel and the inheritance of the saints; if only the power that before had dominion, and the unfruitful tree, and the lifted-up king, is wholly cut down in us, and we are under him who says: "Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart." In Hesebon and its villages etc. He enumerates one by one the cities of the proud and unfruitful king, and names Hesebon, the chief city of his kingdom, which is interpreted "thoughts". Rightly, therefore, the greatest part of the devil's kingdom and the most of his power reigns in the thoughts, because from the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries and the like, which defile a man. Necessarily, therefore, this city is burned up with the fire which the Saviour came to send upon the earth, and wills that it be kindled.
06_marg444: In the thirty-ninth station war is waged against Sehon king of the Amorrhites and Og king of Basan. Sehon is interpreted "temptation of the eyes". This is the devil, who transforms himself as into an angel of light, and through heresies and schisms lies with things like the truth, that he may deceive the unwary. Him the Amorrhites, that is, the embittering, have as king. For unless a certain pretence of truth went before, there would be no embittering heresies nor schisms in the Church. This king each one slays when he condemns pretence and loves truth. Og is interpreted "shutting in"; and Basan, "confusion". For the devil acts to shut the way to God by setting idols in the way, lest Christ be believed in. Shutting in goes before as king; confusion follows as the people. For those who are now shut in so as not to believe in Christ will be confounded when Christ appears. Therefore this station, that is, Dibongad, is interpreted "temptation strongly understood". Because if the pretence which embitters the Church through schism or heresy is overcome, and the shutting in which closes the way of faith through sacrilege, the temptation is understood, and being understood is strongly overcome.
06_interl408: from the father, or paternal water
06_marg445: Sehon, that is, of one speaking; for those who act under the devil know how to speak, but they speak vain things, as astrologers and some natural philosophers. But the kingdom of the faithful, which is from God, is not in speech but in the power of God.
06_marg446: RABANUS. Moab, who is interpreted "from the father" or "paternal water", conceived of incest and drunkenness, the father as it were absent and unknowing, signifies worldly knowledge, which has its own sense as author. And because it is begotten by the making of God, it seems to be born of the father. But because it is adulterous and an adversary of the people of God, it is begotten of incest, and in a cave, and by night. Whence according to Isaias: "In the night it perished", that is, in everlasting error. Ar too, the city of the Moabites, which is interpreted "adversary", signifies that this wisdom, hostile to God, is consumed by the fire of truth, the word of the Church fighting against it; by which also the inhabitants of the high places of the Arnon are devoured. For Arnon is interpreted "curse" or "their enlightening". Because those who trust in eloquence or human wisdom, which seems bright to the children of darkness, fall and are consumed.
06_marg447: ORIGEN. Another text: For this, it says, the speakers in riddles shall say: Come into Hesebon, that the city of Sehon may be built and set up; for a fire went out from Hesebon and a flame from the city of Sehon, and devoured as far as Moab, etc. Sehon was king, whose city was Hesebon. This is therefore the order of the words, as if the speakers in riddles said: Come, that Hesebon may be built and set up, which was the city of king Sehon. A riddle is called figurative speech; speakers in riddles, those who speak figuratively. These are the law and the prophets. Whence: "I will open my mouth in parables: I will utter propositions from the beginning." And Isaias: "The words of this book, he says, shall be as the words of a book that is sealed." The book is sealed because it is entangled with figures and wrapped in riddles. Come into Hesebon that it may be built: the first fell, overthrown and burned; another is to be rebuilt. If you see a Gentile in comeliness of life and in error of religion, say that this is Hesebon, the city in the kingdom of king Sehon. For the unfruitful and lifted-up king reigns in his thoughts. If Israel approaches him, that is, a son of the Church, applying the darts of the word of God, drawing the sword of the spirit against him, and destroys in him all the fortifications of Gentile dogmas and burns up all the arguments of the lifted-up with the fire of truth, say that Hesebon, the city of king Sehon, is overthrown. Yet it is not left deserted. For when all the children of Israel have overturned evil thoughts and impious senses in men, they build up good thoughts and pious senses; they put in the doctrine of truth, the rite of religion, the order of living and honesty of manners. And then truly these speakers in riddles say to one another: Come, let us build Hesebon, which was the city of Sehon. For the children of the Church, because they understand the riddles of the law spiritually, are called speakers in riddles. Whence: "Lo, I have set thee this day over the nations and over kingdoms, to root up and to pull down, to build and to plant." For he overthrows Hesebon, roots up impure thoughts; but he rebuilds and replants chaste thoughts, so that Hesebon is made not of the Amorrhites but of the children of Israel.
06_marg448: WOE TO THEE, MOAB, etc. Chamos is interpreted "gathering" or as it were "handling". Dibon, "understanding temptation abundantly" or "their flowing". Iophe, "blowing" or "breathing". Medaba, "from the forest". Woe therefore to those who, trusting in the spiritual Moab, gather to themselves the treasures of worldly wisdom and lift themselves up against the power of God. Whose boldness shall not prevail, but shall flee and be delivered into captivity to the king of the spiritual Amorrhites. For their yoke shall perish from Hesebon unto Dibon; that is, from the root of thought to the depth of understanding their knowledge shall flow away; and weary, blowing out vanities of words and breathing the fetid odour of putrid sense, they shall come into the forest, where there are no fruitful trees but beasts; against which it is said: "Deliver not up to beasts the soul that confesseth to thee."
06_interl411: understanding temptation abundantly, namely, or their flowing
06_marg449: That is, their strength: namely the strongest dogmas of the heretics, built up by the art of dialectic.
06_marg450: By converting them from error and teaching the precepts of the Lord, that from their correction and progress they might acquire for themselves the heavenly fatherland.
06_marg451: ORIGEN. To Og king of Basan they neither deign to send ambassadors nor ask of him to pass through his land, but at once fight with him and overcome him and his people. Basan is interpreted "foulness". Rightly, therefore, neither are ambassadors sent to this nation nor is passage asked through its land. For there ought to be no passage or approach of ours to foulness, but it is to be fought from the beginning at once and wholly avoided. And Og is interpreted "shutting in". He holds the figure of all carnal and material things, held by the desire of which the soul is shut out from God; against which war is commanded to be waged so that nothing living be left in him. None, therefore, ought to be left living by the children of Israel in the kingdom of foulness and disgrace. It befits Israelite virtue to cut away impious things, and to build up pious and honourable things. But of the kingdom of Sehon it is not written that none be left alive, nor of the kingdom of Moab. For perhaps we need some of those things for the exercises and struggles of this life; otherwise we ought to have gone out of this world. But of Basan, that is, foulness, we need nothing at all; all the works of foulness are to be shaken off. For in nothing can that be honourable which is foul.
06_marg452: AUGUSTINE. In what Scripture says, that after Israel had conquered the Amorrhites and possessed all their cities, Balac king of the Moabites sent ambassadors to hire Balaam to curse the people of Israel, it is sufficiently shown that not all the Moabites had come under the dominion of Sehon king of the Amorrhites when he overcame them in war. Since the nation of the Moabites remained until that time, when Balac reigned as king of Moab. And as to what Moab said to the elders of Madian, that is, the Moabites to the elders of the Madianites: Now this congregation will lick up all who are round about us; they were not one nation, but neighbours said to neighbours that it was to be guarded against alike; but two neighbouring nations.
06_marg453: HE SENT THEREFORE, etc. ORIGEN. War threatens you, king Balac; you ought to prepare arms and an army, and go to meet them equipped with arms. But you send many gifts to Balaam the diviner and promise greater, saying: "Come, curse the people which came out of Egypt." And Balaam refers this to God and is forbidden to come; the king sends ambassadors again and puts all his hope in Balaam, that he may hurl curses at the people in place of darts; if perchance by words the people might be overcome whom the king's army could not overcome. What consequence or counsel does this history have? What king ever, with battle threatening him, laid aside arms and fled for refuge to the words of a diviner and soothsayer? First, then, it must be confessed that in some things words avail more than bodies. For what an army cannot accomplish is accomplished by words; and I do not say holy words or words of God, but certain words which are current among men. How to name them I do not know. Yet they are composed by a useless art, whose name may be whatever pleases each one. There were enchanters and magicians in Egypt. What man can by strength of body change a rod into a serpent, or water into blood? Which they did; for Moses had done it first. But because the king of Egypt knew that these things were done by a certain art of words that is current among men, he thought Moses had done this not by the power of God but by magic art, and had pretended it was done by the power of God. At once he calls together the enchanters and magicians of the Egyptians, and makes a contest between him who worked by the power of God and those who invoked demons. The contrary power does the like; but the serpent made by the power of God swallowed up the others. For demonic power could not restore to good the evil it had made from good. It could make a serpent from a rod, but not return a rod from a serpent. Therefore they are all consumed by that which had been turned into a serpent by the power of God, and by divine power it is returned to its own nature, that nature might confess God. The enchanters of the Egyptians turned water into blood, but could not turn blood into water. But the power of God turned not water but the whole river into blood, and at the prayer of Moses returned it to its own nature. The magicians brought forth sciniphs, but could not drive them away; but Moses brought them forth and removed them. For the contrary power can do something evil, but cannot restore to wholeness. And there are differences among magicians: some avail more, others less. Balaam was famous in magic art and mighty in incantations. For he had not the power or art of words for blessing, but for cursing. For demons are invited for cursing, not for blessing. As one experienced in such things, then, he was most renowned in the east. For otherwise the king would not have presumed that this could be done by words which could scarcely be accomplished by iron and battle line. Certain, therefore, and having often made trial, laying aside the instruments of war he sends to the diviner, saying: "Behold a people is come out of Egypt and hath covered the face of the earth" etc. The king also seems to have heard that the children of Israel are wont to conquer enemies by prayer, not by arms; not so much by iron as by prayers. For Israel moved no arms against Pharao, but it was said to him: "The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace." Against the Amalecites too, not so much the force of arms as the prayer of Moses availed. These things the king of Moab had heard. For it is written: "Nations rose up and were angry; sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim. Then were the princes of Edom troubled, and the princes of the Moabites" etc. He thought therefore within himself, saying: "Because no arms can be matched with the prayers of this people, I must therefore seek prayers that can overcome their prayers." It is written therefore: "And Moab said to the elders of Madian: Now this congregation will lick up all who are round about us, as the calf licks up the grass of the field." Because as the calf tears off the grass of the field with its mouth, and with its tongue as with a sickle cuts whatever it finds, so the people fights with mouth and lips, and has its arms in words. Balac therefore sends to Balaam, that he may oppose words to words and prayers to prayers. And do not wonder whether there is such a thing in magic art. For Scripture marks out this art in order to forbid it, as it signifies that demons exist but forbids them to be worshipped; because the masters of magicians are evil spirits. For none of the holy spirits obeys them; one cannot invoke the great Michael or Raphael or Gabriel; much less, then, can one invoke the Father or the Son or the Holy Ghost. We alone have received this power. But he who has been made partaker of the Holy Ghost ought not to invoke unclean spirits, lest the Holy Ghost flee from him. Magicians are those who invoke Beelzebub. This the people knew, who, lying against the Lord, said: "By Beelzebub the prince of devils he casteth out devils." But the Saviour, knowing that it is true that Beelzebub is the prince of devils, did not reprove them for a lie in this, but answered: "If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out?" It is clear, therefore, that there are certain evil demons who, invoked by magicians, are present with them for evil, not for good. For they are ready to do evil, but know not how to do good. These, therefore, by a certain art and composition of words, took Balaam into friendship; from whose friendship great fruit was seen among men. The king therefore sends to him, saying: "Come hither and curse me the people" etc.
06_marg454: He seems not to trust wholly in Balaam, terrified by the fame of the mighty works which were done among the people of God.
06_marg455: ORIGEN. I do not believe he knew that whomsoever Balaam blessed would be blessed; but he said these things for the sake of flattery, so that by extolling his art he might make him readier for himself. For the magic art does not know how to bless, nor do demons. Isaac and Jacob and all the saints know how to bless. None of the wicked knows how to bless.
06_interl420: SEPTUAGINT: divinations, namely the price of divination
06_marg456: Others: divining instruments, in the arts which human curiosity has composed. There are certain things which Scripture has named divining instruments. And Gentile custom calls them tripods or cauldrons or by words of this kind, which, as though consecrated to this, are wont to be moved and handled by them. But divine Scripture in the prophets names the Ephod in the native tongue, which they report to be the garment of those prophesying. Yet prophecy is one thing in divine Scripture, divination another. For it says: There is no soothsaying in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. Divination therefore is wholly renounced; for it is fulfilled by the work and ministry of demons. Balaam therefore, having received the divining instruments, when the demons were wont to come to him, sees them put to flight and God present; whom he therefore says he consults, because he does not see those accustomed to obey him. God therefore comes to Balaam, not because he is worthy, but that those who were wont to be present for cursing and doing evil might be put to flight. For hence God was providing for his people.
06_marg457: GOD CAME, etc. It is not said whether this was done in sleep, although it is clear that it was done by night. For afterwards Scripture says: "Balaam rising up" etc.
06_marg458: Let no one glory if God speaks to him. For he knows how to speak with such, since he speaks even with the reprobate. And when he speaks through angels, he himself speaks.
06_marg459: God came and said to him, etc. It can be objected: Let Balaam invoke demons, let him curse the people; let the demons invoked do what they can. Can God not defend the people from the demons and check their force? What need was there that he should come to Balaam and forbid the demons even to attempt to harm the people? Though not all things that may occur are to be brought forward, we shall say however that he does not will to condemn them before the time. For they too know that their time comprises this present age. Whence: "Art thou come hither to torment us before the time?" Therefore he did not remove the devil from the principality of this age, because his works are necessary for the perfecting of those who are to be crowned. So too he does not will to draw the other demons away by force from the intent of their purpose before the time. Therefore he does not permit them to be invoked through Balaam, lest perhaps, invoked, they should be destroyed before the time, and perish with God defending the people. For it is one thing if a demon awaits from God someone to be tempted, as Job, and receives power by a certain limit, and it is said to him: I give thee all that he hath in thy power, but touch not himself. It is another if, at a magician's demand, extorting by certain adjurations, the demons rage without any restraint. In which, if their freedom of choice is kept, they will destroy the people of God; if it is taken away, this will be for God to have condemned a rational creature, and brought judgment before the time, and hindered all who, striving against them, could be crowned. For if freedom of choice is taken from the demons, none will assail the athletes of Christ, and there will be no contest; no reward, no victory. So therefore God acts, that the people still raw, and lately begun to be drawn away from the worship of demons, may not be delivered to demons; and that the demons invoked may not bring answers to the magician, and the race of demons not be stripped of the power of choice. Therefore God comes first and forbids Balaam to invoke demons, if only he had ceased from covetousness. But because he persists in the desire of money, God, indulging the power of choice, permits him to go; yet he put his word into his mouth, forbidding the curse to be made through demons, so as to give place to blessings; and in place of curses he makes him bring forth blessings and prophecies which edify the other nations too. For if his prophecies were written by Moses, how much more by those who dwelt with him in Mesopotamia, among whom he was held in great esteem as among the disciples of this art. From him the race and institution of the magi is said to flourish in the parts of the east. They, having in writing all the things that Balaam had prophesied, had this among the rest: That a star shall rise out of Jacob and a man shall spring up out of Israel. Therefore the magi, when the Lord was born, recognized the star and understood that the prophecy was fulfilled, more than the Jews, who despised the oracles of the holy prophets. They therefore, recognizing that the time was at hand, came and adored. And it was a proof of great faith that they venerated a little child as a great king.
06_marg460: Balac means "shutting out" or "devouring". In which is signified some contrary power of this world, which desires to shut out and devour the spiritual Israel, and uses no ministers but the high priests and scribes and Pharisees. It invites these, it promises reward; and they, like Balaam, feign to refer all things to the Lord and to act from zeal for God. For they say: Search the scriptures, and see that out of Galilee a prophet riseth not. "We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God."
06_interl421: a vain people; this signifies the scribes and Pharisees of the Jews
06_marg461: IF BALAC WOULD GIVE ME, etc. AUGUSTINE. In that Balaam said, when more honourable messengers had been sent to him a second time: If Balac would give me his house full of gold and silver, I cannot transgress the word, etc., he has no sin at all; but what follows is a grave sin. For he ought now to have been constant, since the Lord had said: "Thou shalt not go with them" etc., and not to give them hope that the Lord, as though like Balaam bent by gifts and honours, could change his sentence against the people whom he had called blessed. But he showed himself overcome by covetousness, when he wished the Lord to speak to him again about this matter, of which he already knew his will. For what need was there to add: "And now stay here this night" etc.? But the Lord, seeing his covetousness overcome by gifts, permitted him to go, that he might restrain his avarice by the beast on which he rode; confounding his madness by this very thing, that the ass did not dare to transgress the Lord's prohibition made through the angel, which he by covetousness was trying to transgress, although fear held down his covetousness. For God came to Balaam by night and said to him: If the men have come to call thee, arise, follow them, etc. Why after this permission of the Lord did he not consult him again, as after that prohibition, unless because his covetousness was apparent, though it was held down by fear? Then the Scripture says: "And the Lord was angry", because he went; and the angel of the Lord rose up, and the rest that follows until the ass spoke. Nothing here seems more wonderful than that he was not terrified when the ass spoke, but even answered her (as one accustomed to such ministers) with his anger continuing. Afterwards the angel speaks to him, reproving his way; and when he saw him he was terrified and adored. Then he was permitted to go, that prophecy might be brought forth through him. For he was not permitted at all to say what he wished, but what the Spirit compelled. But he himself remained reprobate. Whence: "Having followed the way of Balaam of Bosor, who loved the wages of iniquity."
06_interl422: God yields to covetousness; he lets him go in the desire of his heart.
06_marg462: GOD THEREFORE CAME, etc. Balaam is troublesome to God, and almost extorts permission to go to curse the children of Israel and invoke demons; to whom God had already come.
06_marg463: It is difficult in the explanation of the history how, when it is said "God came to Balaam by night" the first time and asked who the men were who had come to him, and he had answered that they were sent by Balac, saying: Come and curse me the people, the Lord answered: "Thou shalt not go with them" etc. The second time he is said to have come by night and said: "that he should go with them" etc., but that he should speak the word which God would give in his mouth. And the third time the angel of God met him as he went, etc. To whom yet his way seems untimely, so that he would even have killed him had the ass not turned aside; and yet, blamed because he willed to go, he is permitted by him to go, only that he should bring forth the word alone which God would give in his mouth. But before we come to the matter it is to be said that in the letters of the Hebrews the name of God, this God or Lord, is said to be written differently. For any god whatever is written one way, and another way the God of whom it is said: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord thy God is one God." This God of Israel, then, the one God and creator of all, is written with a certain sign of letters, which among them is called the tetragrammaton. When it is written under this sign, there is no doubt that it is said of the true God. But when in common letters, it is uncertain whether it is said of the true God or of any of the others. Those therefore who read Hebrew letters say that God is not here set under the sign of the tetragrammaton; let him who can inquire into it. And that God said, as though asking: Who are these men? it is asked why he seems not to know. And again that he says: "Thou shalt not curse the people", for it is blessed; as though he had said: Thou shalt not curse my people. We meanwhile shall say that by the wisdom of God all things are so ordered that nothing is idle with God, whether good or evil. God did not make malice; yet though he could forbid it when found out by others, he does not forbid it, but uses it with them for necessary causes; for through those in whom it is he proves those who strive toward the glory of the virtues. For if malice were destroyed, there would be none to go against the virtues; and virtue, if it had no contrary, would not shine forth nor be tried; and not proved nor tried, neither would it be virtue. Take away the malice and envy of the brothers of Joseph, and at the same time you will destroy the dispensation of God and the things done in Egypt for the salvation of all nations. If Joseph is not sold, the dream of Pharao will not be expounded; no one will understand what God revealed to him. No one will gather corn in Egypt; Egypt and the bordering regions will perish, and Israel himself and his seed seeking bread. For he will not enter Egypt, nor will the wonders of God be done; there will be no plagues upon the Egyptians, nor the mighty works which God did through Moses and Aaron. No one will cross the Red Sea dryshod; manna will not be given, nor water from the rock, nor the law on mount Sinai; the things related in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy for the knowledge of the human race; they will not come to the land of promise, none will enter it. Take away the malice of king Balac, by which he desires Israel to be cursed, and the cunning by which he invites Balaam to devote the people, and you will take away the dispensation of God and the favour of his providence; nowhere will there be the prophecies of Balaam. Take away the malice of Judas and the betrayal, you will take away likewise the cross of Christ and the passion; nor are the principalities and powers despoiled, nor triumphed over in the wood of the cross. If there had not been the death of Christ, there would have been neither his resurrection, nor any firstborn from the dead, nor hope of resurrection for us. Let us suppose the devil had not sinned, or after sinning had lost the will of malice: the contest against the wiles of the devil will be taken from you, nor will there be the crown of justice and victory for him who strives lawfully. If there are no opponents there will be no contests, nor will rewards be set for the victors. Not only, therefore, does God use the good for good work, but also the wicked. There are vessels unto honour, there are vessels unto dishonour; yet both are necessary. And they are rational and of free choice, and no one is made a vessel of honour by chance or fortuitously. But he who lives most wickedly will become a vessel of dishonour, not by the maker but by himself, having given causes for dishonour. The maker therefore did not make them to be such, but disposes their minds according to their purpose by the justice of his providence and by a certain ineffable reason. As in great cities men of the foulest life are condemned to do the lowest and laborious works, which yet are necessary: either they serve the furnaces of the bath to kindle the fires, that you may enjoy comfort or delights, or they clean the sewers, or do things of this kind, so that you may have a pleasant dwelling in the city. So God indeed did not make malice; yet, found out by the intent of the purpose of those who turned aside from the right way, he did not will to take it away wholly; foreseeing that, though it would be useless to him who used it, he would yet make it useful to those against whom it was exercised. Therefore we ought to flee wholly, lest malice ever be found in us. But in others we must strive to overcome it, not destroy it, because those in whom it is contribute something of necessary work to the whole. For nothing is idle, nothing empty with God; for if the purpose of a man is good, he uses it for good things; if evil, for necessary things. But you will be more blessed if from the virtue that is in you the whole of this life obtains some good, according to that: "That you may shine as lights in the world, holding forth the word of life unto glory." Lights therefore are necessary to this world; and what is so delightful and so magnificent as the work of the sun and moon, by which the world is enlightened? For the world needs also angels who are over the beasts and preside over the birth of animals, the planting of plants and shrubs and the growth of the rest; and who preside over holy works, who teach the understanding of eternal light and the knowledge of the hidden things of God and the science of divine things. See therefore that you are not found among the angels who preside over beasts, if you have led a beastly life, or among those who preside over earthly works, if you have loved bodily and earthly things. But take pains how you may be taken up into the fellowship of Michael, who always offers the prayers of the saints to God. And you will be taken up into this number, or into this office, if you are instant always in prayer and watch in it. Or into the office and fellowship of Raphael, who presides over medicine: when you see one wounded, namely by sins and by the arrows of the devil, apply the cure of words and the medicine of the word of God, that you may heal the wounds of sin through patience. He who does such things in this world offers himself to be formed by the maker in the future a vessel of election, profitable to the Lord, prepared unto every work. He who does the contrary has offered himself a vessel unto dishonour of the divine dispensation. Therefore I think that in the divine volumes are written the deeds of the good and of the wicked, and the scriptures are woven of left-handed and right-handed acts, that we may understand that with God neither the works of the wicked nor of the good are idle.
06_marg464: IF TO CALL, etc. Balaam was a diviner, namely by the ministry of demons and magic art sometimes foreknowing future things. He is asked by Balac to curse Israel. The ambassadors come; they carry divining instruments in their hands; the nations stand astonished and earnestly awaiting what Balaam will answer, whom they believed worthy of divine converse. See how the wisdom of God made a vessel prepared for dishonour profit not one nation but almost the whole world. And to this man, to whom demons were wont to appear, God appears, forbidding the journey of evil work. Balaam is stupefied and wonders at the authority of the one forbidding. For evil was not wont to displease the demons. He sends back the ambassadors, saying that he can do nothing but the word which God shall give in his mouth. The ambassadors return; he inquires again; again he is troublesome, again he desires to hear. For the covetous does not easily go without reward. What then does he hear the second time? If these men have come to call thee: "Arise and go with them." In which God yields to the will of his covetousness, according to that: "So I let them go according to the desires of their heart" etc. But the counsel of the divine dispensation is fulfilled; for it is said to him: Whatever word I shall put in thy mouth, that shalt thou speak. If he had not been unworthy, the Lord would have put his word not in his mouth but in his heart. But because in his heart was the desire of reward and the covetousness of money, the word of the Lord is put not in the heart but in the mouth. For it was being brought about by a wonderful dispensation that the words of the prophets, which were contained within the Israelite court, should reach the Gentiles through Balaam, since all the nations believed him; and that he should bring forth to the nations the secret mysteries of Christ and a great treasure, not so much with heart and sense as with mouth and speech.
06_interl423: The counsel of the divine dispensation is fulfilled.
06_marg465: BALAAM AROSE, etc. ORIGEN. Allegorically. If you see a contrary power assailing the people of God, you will understand who it is that sits upon the ass. And if you see how men are driven headlong by demons, you will understand what the ass is. For you understand Jesus sending his disciples to the ass that was tied, and to the colt, that they might loose them and bring them, that he himself might sit upon her. Perhaps this ass, that is, the Church, formerly carried blasphemy, but, loosed by the disciples, carries Christ, that with her he may enter the heavenly Jerusalem. Whence: "Behold thy king cometh to thee, meek, and sitting upon a beast of burden": the believers, namely, from the Jews; "and a young colt": namely the believers from the Gentiles.
06_marg466: Who was present, namely with the children of Israel; of whom it is written: "My angel shall go before thee."
06_interl425: who was outside the walls of the vineyards
06_marg467: The magician sees demons, the ass sees the angel; not because she is worthy to see, as neither to speak, but that Balaam may be confuted. Whence: "The dumb beast rebuked the folly of the prophet."
06_marg468: Balaam strives to reach his purpose, but the animal over which he presides hinders his wish; because the ass saw the angel whom the human mind does not see. Often the flesh, made slow by troubles, by its own scourge points out to the mind the God whom the mind, presiding over the flesh, did not see; so that it hinders those who, in anxiety of spirit, desire to advance in this world and strive swiftly, until it makes known the invisible one who meets it. Whence it is well said by Peter: He had a check of his madness, the dumb beast used to the yoke, which, speaking with man's voice, forbade the folly of the prophet. For the insane man is rebuked by the dumb beast of burden when the lifted-up mind is reminded by the afflicted flesh of the good of humility which it ought to hold. But Balaam did not obtain the good of this correction, because, going on to curse, he changed his voice, not his mind.
06_marg469: That is, the wall of that vineyard in which the angel was not, since he was on the other side, in the furrows of the vineyards, according to the Septuagint.
06_marg470: No longer in the furrows of the vineyards, but between the walls themselves, that is, in the way, he withstood him, so that he could go neither to the right nor to the left.
06_marg471: Because, hurt, she did not go back nor turn aside in either direction, because she was not terrified from one side, but the angel was in the middle of the way in the narrow place.
06_marg472: That Balaam might be reproved by her and confuted by the voice of a dumb beast, who seemed a diviner and wise.
06_marg473: ISIDORE. Allegorically. The ass on which Balaam sits sees the angel and speaks. That is, the brutish Gentile world, which formerly Balaam, that is, the seducer to idolatry, as a brute animal resisting with no reason, subjected to what error he would; it saw the angel whom man could not see, and saw and bore it and spoke; that we might know that at the coming of the great angel that Gentile people, the nature of its hardness and stolidity being changed, would speak with tongues loosed to God.
06_marg474: Allegorically. The ass on which Balaam sat (because Scripture says: "Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord") can be understood as a part of the believers, which for its folly or innocence is compared to animals. Whence: Not many wise, not many mighty, not many noble; but the foolish things of the world hath God chosen, that he may confound the wise. These, therefore, were held subject and bound by most wicked masters, the scribes and Pharisees; but they are loosed by the Lord, not indeed by himself, but by his disciples. Whence: "Go ye into the village that is over against you, and you shall find an ass tied" etc. As therefore in the Gospel it is not the Lord himself but his disciples who loose the ass, so here the mouth of the ass is opened not by God himself but by the angel. And as in the Gospel those who do not see reprove those who speak; whence: "Father, I give thee thanks, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones." The scribes and Pharisees therefore sat upon the ass and held her bound. With them, therefore, the angel is angry; and unless by a certain foresight of things to come, he would have slain them and saved the ass, which saw and reverenced him who came to the vineyard and stands among the ruins. Yet she pressed the feet of him who sat upon her against the wall. Therefore perhaps that ancient rider cannot walk, nor will he come to him who says: "Come to me, all you that labour and are burdened." Yet the ass came, brought by the disciples; and on her, on whom Balaam, greedy of reward, then sat, Jesus now sits. Do not wonder if you see him whom we have said signifies the scribes and teachers of the people prophesying of Christ. For Caiphas said: "It is expedient for you that one man should die for the people." But, it says, because he was the high priest of that year, he prophesied. Let no one therefore be lifted up if he prophesies, if he merits foreknowledge; because prophecies shall be made void, tongues shall cease, knowledge shall be destroyed; but there remain faith, hope, charity, and the greater of these is charity, which alone never falleth away.
06_marg475: Truly he was carried away, so full of covetousness, that he was not terrified by the miracle of so great a portent, and answered as though speaking to a man; whereas God had not turned the soul of the ass into a rational nature, but had made to sound from her what pleased him, to restrain his madness. Perhaps prefiguring that the foolish things of the world God chose to confound the wise, for the spiritual and true Israel.
06_interl427: the faithful, namely, the foolish, the innocent
06_marg476: LO, HERE I AM: SHALL I SPEAK ANY OTHER, etc. ORIGEN. Balaam is set down in the scriptures now as blameworthy, now as praiseworthy. He is blameworthy when, forbidden by God to come to the king, he persists in coming, and, greedy of reward, consults God again until he is left to his covetous desires and goes in his own wills. He is culpable when he builds altars, lays victims on them for demons, and with magic apparatus demands divine counsels; when he gives the most wicked counsel by which the people may be deceived. He is shown praiseworthy when the word of God is put in his mouth, when the Spirit of God is upon him, when he prophesied of Christ, when he foretells to Jews and Gentiles the future mysteries of the coming of Christ, when instead of curses he blesses the people and extols the name of Israel above visible glory with mystic utterances. It is difficult, therefore, to define, to determine his person; to whom not only this diversity belongs, but also what he himself says of himself as though prophesying: Let my soul die among the souls of the just, and let my seed be like the seed of the just. Through Micheas also it is said: "O my people, remember what Balac the king of Moab purposed against thee", and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, from the cords to Galgal, that thou mightest know the justice of the Lord. He shows therefore that through these things the justice of the Lord would be known. Therefore Balaam the son of Beor answered all those things concerning king Balac which are related in writing. Who, think you, will be found who can show from these very answers of Balaam that the justice of God is made manifest in them? For if the word of God was put in his mouth, and the Spirit of God came upon him, and the justice of God is known from his answers, the things said by him are to be believed prophetic and divine; although it is hard to find that the Spirit of God came upon any of the prophets. But either the vision which he sees, or the taking up of the word of God, or the word of God came to him, and certain other things we read of the prophets; but that the Spirit of God came upon any of the prophets I do not remember to have read. Of David indeed it is written thus: "And the spirit of God appeared," or "shone forth," "upon David from that day forward"; yet the Spirit of God did not come upon David. But of Saul it is written thus: "The spirit of the Lord shall come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be changed into another man." Again of the same: "The spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him." Again: it came to pass, when the evil spirit was upon Saul, David took the harp and played, and it was well with him, and the evil spirit departed from him. That which is written may therefore seem a middle case: And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him. We shall try, therefore, to unfold Balaam in the person of the Pharisees and scribes and those like them. From Mesopotamia, he says, Balac king of Moab hath called me, from the mountains of the east, etc. He calls Mesopotamia the land which lay between the rivers of Babylon, of which it is said: "Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: when we remembered Sion." If anyone therefore is between the rivers of Babylon, if anyone is flooded with the streams of lust and washed round with the heats of luxury, he is said not to stand but to sit. Whence: Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, when we remembered Sion. But neither can they weep unless they have first remembered Sion. For the remembrance of good things makes the causes of evils lamentable. For unless one remembers Sion, unless he looks upon the law of God and the mountains of the scriptures, he does not begin to weep for his evils. From these rivers, therefore, Balaam is called, and from these mountains of the east he is invited. These mountains are not the holy mountains of which it is said: "The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains." And elsewhere: "Mountains are round about it: so the Lord is round about his people." But those of which it is said: Dark mountains, etc. And elsewhere: "O dark mountain", and again: "Behold I come against thee, O destroying mountain." These are the mountains in which is every height that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God. From these mountains Balaam is called. Such as the mountains are, such an east they have; for they have the rising of their own light. He who transforms himself as an angel of light has that light of which it is said: "The light of the wicked shall be put out." And as the light of the wicked, and of him who transforms himself as an angel of light, is contrary to that light which said: "I am the light of the world", so too this east is contrary to that of which it is said: "Behold a man, the Orient is his name." From the borders of that east, then, not of this, Balaam came, enlightened by that Lucifer of whom it is said: "How art thou fallen, O Lucifer, who didst rise in the morning?"
06_interl429: in which is every height exalting itself against the knowledge of God
06_marg477: SEPTUAGINT: From Mesopotamia, which is washed by the rivers of Babylon. Whence: "Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: when we remembered Sion."
06_interl430: of the devil, namely of Lucifer, who rose in the morning
06_marg478: COME, HE SAID, AND. ORIGEN. Come, he says, and curse me Jacob. In the Latin words the repetition seems almost superfluous; but in the Greek, with the name Israel, there is the addition of a preposition, namely: over-curse me Israel; so that he seemed to demand a curse with greater intensity against Israel than against Jacob. For while one is only Jacob, that is, placed in works, he is assailed with lower curses; but when he has advanced and sharpened the inner man to see God, he is assailed with over-curses, that is, with the more vehement darts of curses. And then indeed the mouth of Balaam was full of cursing and bitterness, and under his tongue labour and sorrow. He sat in ambush with the rich, he awaited reward from the king, that in secret places he might kill the innocent. But God, who alone does wonderful things, works salvation from enemies. For he put the word into his mouth, though his heart could not yet receive the word of God; for there was still in his heart the covetousness of reward. Whence after the word of God which he had in his mouth, he said to Balac: "Come, and I will give thee counsel" etc. For he had the word of God not in his heart but only in his mouth. And therefore he speaks the word of God.
06_marg479: ORIGEN. How shall I curse him whom the Lord does not curse? Or how shall I over-curse him whom God does not over-curse? The Lord does not curse Jacob nor Israel; but do you think he curses anyone? To the serpent he says: "Cursed art thou among all the beasts of the earth"; and to Adam: "Cursed is the earth in thy work"; and to Cain: "Cursed art thou upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive the blood of thy brother" etc. He will say also to those who shall be on his left: "Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire"; and when he says: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites", and the like, he seems to reprove with curses. What is it, then, that the Apostle says: "Bless, and curse not"? Does he himself, who sets an example of life for men, do what he does not wish done by men? It is not so. For God, when he curses, marks the desert of him who is cursed and brings forth sentence, as one whom neither the quality of the sin nor the disposition of the sinner deceives. But man, who cannot know these things nor recognize the purpose and mind of another, if he utters a curse in the manner of one speaking or bringing forth sentence, there cannot be a just cause of cursing where the disposition of the sinner is unknown; and especially he utters curses when he is provoked by reproaches and injuries. Which vice the Apostle cuts away, lest we provoke curses with curses and reproaches with reproaches, commanding that we bless and do not curse; not that the truth of judging, which is not hidden from men, and the authority of pronouncing, are destroyed.
06_marg480: Who yet marks the desert of him who is cursed and brings forth sentence, whom neither the quality of the sin nor the disposition of the sinner deceives. But man knows neither, and often curses when provoked by reproaches. Therefore the Apostle says: "Bless, and curse not", that the vice of reproaching may be cut away.
06_marg481: FROM THE TOPS, etc. As if it ought not to be cursed for this, that its life is lofty and heavenly. No one understands it unless he has ascended to eminent knowledge.
06_marg482: ORIGEN. From the tops of the mountains I shall behold him, and from the hills I shall understand him. As though because Israel is set on lofty hills and high mountains, that is, in a high and arduous life, to behold and understand which no one is fit unless he ascends to eminent knowledge. Therefore God does not curse him, because his life is most lofty, not lowly and cast down. Which seems to be said not of the carnal Israel, but of him whose conversation, while he walks on earth, is in heaven. Or if these things are referred also to that people, it is rightly said, I shall behold and I shall understand, so that the future time is signified in which all Israel, coming to the faith of Christ, shall be saved. And he shall be beheld from the mountains and from the hills, that is, those who, rising with Christ, have practised a lofty and heavenly life on earth.
06_marg483: The act of Jacob, that is, of the active, is seen; the contemplation of Israel, that is, of the contemplative, is only understood. Or in the future resurrection Jacob shall be seen, that is, the body; Israel understood, that is, the soul and spirit of those who rise.
06_marg484: Because it is not mingled with other men, nor reckoned among the other nations, ennobled by certain privileges, observances and ordinances of its own; as the tribe of Levi is not mingled with the others. This people shall dwell alone, etc. The spiritual Jacob and Israel truly dwells alone among the nations. For if we have come to mount Sion and to the city of the heavenly Jerusalem, and have come to the spiritual Judea, which is the portion of God, and, set on earth, have our conversation there, truly we are not reckoned among the other nations, nor are their borders mingled with ours. Even if Sodom and Egypt are restored to their former state, and whatever else of the kind is written in the prophets, yet when Jacob and the spiritual Israel have gone up with the Church of the firstborn, none shall be equalled or mingled with them. For unless one has been grafted among the branches as a wild olive and made partaker of the fatness of the root of the olive, how can he be associated with Jacob or Israel? Since without that root no one can be called either Jacob or Israel; neither can anyone of Jacob or Israel be called Jacob or Israel if he sins; nor will anyone from the Gentiles, if he has entered the Church of the Lord, be any longer reckoned among the Gentiles.
06_interl434: No one, namely, except him "who telleth the number of the stars", and brought forth all things in measure and weight and number.
06_marg485: THE SAME. Who has searched out the seed of Jacob? And who has numbered the people of Israel, etc.? This is like what the Lord said to Abraham: "Look up to heaven and number the stars of heaven, if thou canst"; and he said: "So shall thy seed be." And Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice. Abraham, then, or any man whatever, or even perhaps of the angels and higher powers, cannot number the stars nor the seed of Abraham, since it is said: "So shall thy seed be." But God ("who telleth the number of the stars, and calleth them all by their names", and who said: I have commanded all the stars) can search out the seed of Jacob and number the dust of Israel. For he alone knows who is truly Jacob and who truly Israel. For he does not regard the Jew openly, nor circumcision in the flesh, but him who is a Jew inwardly and circumcised in heart. He alone, therefore, can number and search out; who, according to incomprehensible wisdom, after that heavenly form which he alone can know, set also these numbers which we have in hand, in which he commanded that according to their kindreds and the houses of their families, by name, all the males should be numbered by their polls from twenty years old and upward, every one who goes forth in strength; and their number is gathered as sacred, sacred namely and pleasing to God then, when it is numbered at his command. But if anyone wishes to number contrary to the command of the Lord, though he be David, though a great prophet, he acts against the law and is reproved by a prophet, and suffers the things that are written in the second book of Kings.
06_marg486: ORIGEN. He seems to prophesy of himself; but according to the letter it was not done either in Balaam or in that Israel, nor could it be done; for he died not among them but by them.
06_marg487: Let my soul die among the just. This fits rather the person of those who at present, though they are held a vain people, because they are without the grace of the Holy Ghost, yet when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in, all this prophecy which is spoken of Israel will be fulfilled in the spiritual Israel, and his soul will die with the souls of the just. For they will receive into themselves the faith of Christ, that they may be baptized into his death, and buried together with him by baptism into death. And let my seed be as the seed of the just. For not they themselves, but their seed becomes as the seed of the just, who, believing from the Gentiles, are justified in Christ. Therefore neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith that worketh by charity.
06_marg488: Let my soul die the death of the just, and my last end be like to them, etc. Many within the Church have long prayers to God, but have not the life of those who pray; and they weep in prayer, but in the time of temptation, when they are assailed by pride, they swell with haughtiness. Likewise they succumb to the storm of avarice, of luxury, of anger, nor do they remember that they wept for desire of the eternal kingdom. Which Balaam showing of himself says: Let my soul die the death of the just, etc. But after his compunction he gave counsel against the life of those to whom he had asked to be made like even in dying; and by occasion of avarice he forgot what he had wished concerning innocence. For often the wicked are pricked to justice to no profit, as the good are tempted to fault without harm. For it comes about by divine dispensation that the former do something of good which does not profit them, whence they may trust amid the evils which they commit most fully; and the latter, who are tempted but do not consent, through weakness fix the steps of the heart more truly in justice through humility. The one is plain in Balaam; of the other Paul says: "I see another law in my members, fighting against the law of my mind" etc. The one, therefore, is pricked, yet does not draw near to justice. The other is tempted, and yet fault does not defile him; because neither do imperfect good things help the wicked, nor do unconsummated evils condemn the good. For prayer which perseverance does not hold has not the weight of virtue. Whence: "Their faces were no more changed in different ways."
06_marg489: This can be understood of the magi, who first came from the east to adore Christ, who were of the seed of Balaam by succession of race and by tradition of discipline. For it is clear that they recognized the star which Balaam had foretold would rise in Israel.
06_marg490: Balac, hearing against his hope blessings instead of curses, and bearing it no further, interrupted the words of the one prophesying.
06_marg491: Allegorically. The bitter king does not wish blessing, but seeks curses. For he is of the mind of him to whom it is said: "Cursed art thou among all the beasts of the earth."
06_interl437: in whose mouth God put the word
06_marg492: He thinks him terrified by the multitude of Israel and therefore not daring to curse, and that a change of place will profit him.
06_marg493: The madman thought the Israelite grace could be hidden by the obstacle of a place, not knowing that "a city seated on a mountain cannot be hid".
06_marg494: The thing was being done with profane sacrifices, and divination was sought by magic art. Yet God, willing grace to abound where offence abounded, deigned to be present, not at the sacrifices, but coming to meet him. And there he gives his word, and foretells mysteries and things to come, where the faith and working and wonder of the Gentiles most hung; so that those who will not believe our prophets may believe their own diviners.
06_marg495: He stood by the holocaust, set in his idolatry; therefore he fell the more. He therefore seems to stand who had fallen the more, when he seemed to stand in idolatry.
06_interl439: who is hindered by vices, so that what he speaks is not true
06_marg496: GOD IS NOT AS, etc. ORIGEN. God is not deceived as a man, nor terrified as a son of man. As though you think that God is deceived like a man in the things he speaks. "For men are hindered by many vices, so that what they speak is not true. For they speak when angry, or from fear, or covetousness, or for the sake of boasting; but God, in whom there is no passion, whatever he has said, says according to the deserts of the causes." And therefore he cannot be deceived, because whatever is brought forth by reason cannot lack reason. He therefore is not one who speaks in vain like a man, nor is he terrified, or does he terrify, as a son of man. In men terror changes the sentence; but God, who is above all things, can be terrified by none so as to change his sentence; nor does he terrify as a son of man. For men for boasting's sake raise false alarms and threats even against those whom they cannot harm. But God terrifies by reason, that he may correct man in the tribulation of hearing, that, terrified by the word of threatening, he may be amended, lest the vengeance of his evils come upon him.
06_interl440: changeable through the vice of human frailty
06_marg497: HATH HE SAID THEN, etc. ORIGEN. The same: when he has said, will he not do? will he speak and not abide? Though men do not do what they say, being changeable through the vice of human frailty, God is unchangeable. But someone says: When God spoke of Nineve, that it should be overthrown after three days, why did he not abide by his word? And in the things he spoke of David, to whom death had been promised for three days to waste the people, and within one day, even to the hour of the midday meal, it ceased? Perhaps the things that are said by way of question will be seen not to be defined, but to show something in between; and the disposition of an irrevocable sentence is not shown; so that this seems said more moderately: Hath he said, and will he not do? It is written in Jonas: "And Jonas preached and said: Yet three days", or forty according to the Hebrews, "and Nineve shall be destroyed." It is to be observed, therefore, that it is not found in the words of God, which he spoke to the prophet, "yet three days and Nineve shall be destroyed"; so that the word said and not done seems uttered rather by Jonas than by the Lord. In the second book of Kings too: the word of the Lord, it says, came to Gad the prophet, saying: "Thus saith the Lord: I give thee thy choice of three things, choose one of them which thou wilt, that I may do it to thee. And Gad came to David, saying: Either seven years of famine shall come to thee in thy land, or thou shalt flee three months before thy enemies, or for three days there shall be a pestilence in thy land." Observe therefore how, in these three threats too, God is not found to have spoken of death for three days. For it is set in the words of Gad, not in the commands of the Lord. And the things that are said through a prophet are not always to be received as said by God. God spoke many things through Moses; yet Moses commanded some things by his own authority. Whence: "Because of the hardness of your heart Moses wrote you this precept" etc., down to: "What therefore God hath joined together, let no man put asunder." You see therefore here that God neither commanded nor willed divorce to be made; but that Moses, because of the hardness of the Jews, wrote that a bill of divorce was to be given. Hence Paul says: "The Lord commandeth, not I." And elsewhere: "For I speak, not the Lord." And again: "I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give counsel." And again: "That which I speak, I speak not according to God." Likewise, therefore, in the other prophets: some things the Lord spoke and not the prophets, some the prophets and not the Lord. The objection therefore seems to be resolved, since the Lord revokes and changes for the better not so much his own words as the prophet's. But I think rather that the former solution fits the senses of the whole of Scripture; and especially those in which God says he is patient and of much mercy and repenting of the evil; or most of all in those which are pronounced generally by Jeremias, in which it is shown that for his many mercies and incomprehensible goodness God speaks and does not do, speaks and does not abide, thus: "I will suddenly speak, that is, I will speak definitely, against a nation and against a kingdom, to root up and to pull down and to destroy it. If that nation shall repent of their evil, I also will repent of the evil that I thought to do to them. And I will suddenly speak of a nation and of a kingdom, to build up and plant it. If it shall do evil in my sight, that it obey not my voice, I will repent of the good that I have spoken to do unto it." How then can we prefer to these things, which are said absolutely through Jeremias, those which are said in suspense through Balaam, unless because those are to be confirmed for the negligent and the despisers, but these are to be noted more secretly by the more perfect?
06_interl441: by God, who put the truth in my mouth
06_interl442: For he cannot, even if he would, turn the word of God with a human tongue.
06_marg498: Another translation: "There shall be no labour in Jacob, nor shall sorrow be seen in Israel"; in the world to come, namely.
06_marg499: There shall be no labour in Jacob, nor shall sorrow be seen in Israel, etc. The state of the life to come is announced. For this life is not passed without labour and sorrow. For Paul is beaten with rods thrice, stoned once, and suffers innumerable things; but in the future sorrow and sadness and groaning shall flee away. Which yet is referred not to all, but only to those who shall be of the merits of Jacob and Israel; as the poor Lazarus, who passed this life in labour and sorrow, whence where the rich man is tormented, he rests. He is in the true Israel and in the true Jacob, upon whom labour and sorrow do not come. But that rich man was Israel according to the flesh, of whose brothers he said: They have the law and the prophets; let them hear them.
06_interl444: a likeness of an existing thing
06_interl446: He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
06_interl447: who does not forsake his Israel
06_interl448: the preaching of the Gospel, by which the trophy of the cross is announced
06_marg500: THE LORD HIS GOD, etc. THE SAME. The Lord his God is with him, and the glorious things of the princes are with him, etc. God never forsakes his Israel. The glorious power of the princes is principality and true kingdom; since there are also some princes who are to be driven out of their principality, or perhaps have already been driven out, and these who are truly Israel are to be brought in. After all those glorious things which those princes had in heaven, who kept not their principality but forsook their everlasting dwellings, this Israel and Jacob, who wrestled and conquered, shall receive them.
06_marg501: The admonition of preaching, because in you the king, that is, Christ, triumphs over the devil.
06_marg502: THE SAME. God who brought him out of Egypt; as the glory of the unicorn to him, etc. That Israel was brought out of this earthly Egypt; but the spiritual Israel out of the Egypt of this world and out of the power of darkness. And his glory is as of the unicorn. The unicorn is said to be an animal formed according to its name, in whose strength and power Christ is understood. And horn is often put for kingdom. Whence: "The four horns are four kingdoms." Under the name of unicorn, therefore, it seems to be shown that all that is his is one horn, that is, one kingdom. For the Father has put all things under his feet, until the last enemy, death, is destroyed, and as the unicorn he holds one kingdom of all, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. There goes out, therefore, glory to the spiritual Israel as the glory of the unicorn. Whence: "Father, grant them that as I and thou are one, so these also may be one in us"; when, namely, he will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory.
06_marg503: Whose? Christ's, all of whose is one horn, that is, one kingdom; whose glory belongs to the spiritual Israel. For he himself says: "Father, grant them that as I and thou are one, so they may be one in us."
06_interl451: who wrestles against principalities and powers and the rulers of this world
06_marg504: ORIGEN. There is no soothsaying in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. It seems to me that the foreknowledge of future things, as far as regards the thing itself, is something in between, that is, neither properly good nor properly evil; since foreknowledge of future things can sometimes come to the knowledge of men even from the side of the devil. But when the time and opportunity and the will of God are there, foreknowledge is also given to men by God through the prophets. Therefore that cannot properly be called good which is sometimes from the evil one, nor properly evil which is sometimes from God. In the book of Kings it is written that the ark of God was taken by the foreigners and brought into Azotus, and they brought it into the house of Dagon. And Dagon was found fallen on his face to the ground before the ark; and the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the Azotians, and he struck them in the hinder parts. After this it went into Accaron, and the Accaronites said to their diviners and priests: Tell us how we shall send back the ark to its place. They answered: "If you send it back, send it not empty, but give it what you owe for sin, and then you shall be healed, and he will forgive you; otherwise his hand will not depart from you." And after a little: "Make a cart, and take two kine that have calved, on which there hath come no yoke, and yoke them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home; and put the ark upon the cart, and the vessels of gold which you have offered for sin, and all its holy things, and let it go. And look: if it go up by the way of its own coasts towards Bethsames, then he hath done us this great evil; but if not, we shall know that it is not his hand hath touched us, but it hath happened by chance." See therefore how, by judgments set before them, they consider whether the cause of the evils came from the hand of God and for the injury to the ark, or happened by chance. It follows: "When they had put the ark of the Lord upon the cart, the kine took the straight way that leadeth to Bethsames, and turned not aside neither to the right hand nor to the left." Who then, looking carefully at these things, would call the foreknowledge which was foretold of the oxen's going straight either fortuitous or composed by art, and not ministered by demons? Who feared the power of the ark, by which even the worship of demons was destroyed, their images and temples falling down. There is therefore a certain working of demons in the ministry of foreknowledge, which is gathered by certain arts by those who have given themselves over to demons; and it seems to be grasped and understood now through lots, as through auguries; now from the contemplation of entrails, which they call auspices, and by tricks of this kind. Which arts have deceived men away from God, so that Manasses, the son of the most just Ezechias, deceived by this error, built an altar to all the host of heaven in both courts of the house of the Lord; to the spiritual wickednesses, namely, set in the heavenly places. And such were the things he awaited, of which it could be said: That they were done in all power and lying signs and wonders, so that even the elect might be deceived. All these things, then, I do not doubt are done by the working of demons, who direct the movements of birds or beasts or entrails, or of lots, according to the signs which they themselves have taught to be observed by those to whom they handed down this art. From all which the man of God, who is numbered in the portion of God, ought to be wholly a stranger, which the demons secretly contrive; lest he be again joined to the demons and filled with their spirit and power, lest he be brought back to the worship of idols. It is better to be ignorant than to learn from demons. It is better not to learn even from a prophet than to inquire of diviners. For divination is not given divinely, but is so called by antiphrasis, as being done through men filled with demons. But the rite of the Gentiles believed everything divine which is uttered by any spirit whatever. Yet God commands us to learn nothing from these, lest we become their partners. Whence Christ, disdaining to receive testimony from demons, said: Hold thy peace, and go out of him. Paul too, when the woman having a spirit of divination cried out: These men are the servants of the most high God, etc., being grieved said: I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to go out from her; because he judged it unworthy that testimony should be given to his preaching by the spirit of divination. We ought therefore to grieve the more whenever we see souls deceived by those who believe a spirit of divination, or a ventriloquist, or demons of this kind, as a divine spirit. There shall be no soothsaying in Jacob, then, nor divination in Israel. It follows: In time it shall be told to Jacob and to Israel what God shall accomplish. That is, when it behoves, when it is expedient, future things are told by God through the prophets, by the Holy Ghost. If they are not told, it is not expedient to foreknow them. Those, therefore, who inquire into future things by divers arts and invocations of demons desire to learn what is not expedient. And for the utter destruction of divination or augury we shall add this also, that all these animals or birds are judged fit and worthy for the ministry of demons. For dragons and other serpents are said to minister to the pythons; and to the augurs and to those who take auspices from slain victims, wolves bring all things, or foxes, or hawks, or crows, or eagles, or the like; which Moses, I believe for these causes, marked as unclean.
06_interl452: in which it behoves and is expedient
06_marg505: Who sees God by purity of faith and cleanness of mind; nor would he receive Balaam himself, but he does not dare to reject the word which God put in his mouth. For unless the word had been from God, he would not have revealed it to his servant Moses, far away, when Balaam said these things.
06_interl454: "The kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away."
06_marg506: Others: Behold, as a lion's whelp he shall rise up, and as a lion he shall exult. For he is a whelp when rational infants lately born receive milk without guile; but an exulting lion when the perfect man puts away the things of a child.
06_marg507: THE SAME. Behold the people shall rise up as a lion's whelp, and shall exult as a lion. He seems to describe the confidence of the people believing in Christ, and the freedom which it has in faith, and the exultation which it bears in hope. For it is compared to a lion's whelp when it tends toward perfection, glad and swift; but to a lion when it already holds the things that are perfect. For as the lion and the lion's whelp fear no animal, but all things are subject to them, so the perfect Christian, who takes up his cross and follows Christ, saying: "The world is crucified to me, and I to the world", despises all things that are in the world, imitating him who is called the lion of the tribe of Juda and the lion's whelp. For as he himself is the light of the world and granted his disciples to be the light of the world, so, since he is the lion and the lion's whelp, he gave to those who believe in him the name of lion and of lion's whelp.
06_marg508: He says the people shall be lifted up in the future; for of the one he saw he would have said: it is lifted up.
06_marg509: ORIGEN. He shall not sleep until he eat the prey and drink the blood of the wounded. These things cannot stand according to the letter. For how should this people, so praiseworthy, so magnificent, drink the blood of the wounded, when even those called from the Gentiles are commanded to abstain from blood as from things sacrificed to idols? But except we eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, we shall not have life in us. For his flesh is meat indeed and his blood is drink indeed; in which is spirit and life; who was wounded for our sins. We drink his blood, not only in the rite of the sacraments, but also when we receive his words, in which is spirit and life. He himself, then, is the wounded one, whose blood, that is, the words of doctrine, we receive. And all those are wounded who have preached his word to us. For when we read their words, that is, of his apostles, and obtain life from them, we drink the blood of the wounded. Whence: they drank the purest blood of the grape; of that grape, namely, of which it is said: I am the true vine, the disciples the branches, the Father the husbandman. You therefore are the true Israel, because you know how to drink the blood both of that grape which is of the true vine and of its branches which the Father purges; whose fruit is rightly called the blood of the wounded, which we drink from their words. If only we are as lion's whelps rising up, and as an exulting lion.
06_interl455: Christ was slain for our offences
06_interl457: the words of Christ and of the apostles; whence: The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
06_interl459: Balac thinks the diviner lacks the advantage of place for cursing rather than the will.
06_marg510: ORIGEN. And Balac took Balaam himself to the top of mount Phogor, which stretches toward the desert. Those whom God calls he sets on the top of mount Sinai. Balac, contrary to God, on the top of mount Phegor, which is interpreted "delight". On the top of delight and lust, therefore, Balac sets men; for he is a lover of pleasure more than of God, and wishes to shut them out from God; for he is called, or is interpreted, "shutting out" and "devouring". Therefore Phegor stretches toward the wilderness, that is, toward the business which is a wilderness and deserted by God.
06_marg511: THE SAME. The things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. Yet because the law of God commanded sacrifices and handed down to Israel the rite of sacrificing, perhaps it is asked why these things, which seem dedicated to demons, are commanded to be offered to God? And the answer will be ready. Because as the giving of a bill of divorce was not of the will of God, who did not wish what he had joined to be separated, but Moses wrote it because of the hardness of the Jews, so it can be seen of this too. For God does not eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats, who says: I spoke not to thee of sacrifices and victims in the day that I brought thee out of the land of Egypt. But Moses, because of their hardness, to take away the Egyptian custom, commanded them these things, that those who could not abstain from sacrificing might sacrifice at least to God and not to demons. There is perhaps a more secret reason for sacrificing to God, for the destruction, namely, of the sacrifices which are offered to demons; so that, because souls are wounded through those, they might be healed through these; as those who have skill in medicine confirm. For they report that the poisons of serpents are driven out by medicines made from serpents. So, therefore, the poison of the sacrifices of demons is driven out by the sacrifices offered to God; so the death of Jesus does not allow the death of sin to have dominion over believers. But while the time allowed it, sacrifices were set against sacrifices; when the perfect victim came, which should take away the sin of the whole world, the sacrifices which were offered one by one to God seemed superfluous, since by one victim all the worship of demons was driven away. But Balaam, either according to the purpose of his heart, which he had not amended, or according to the figure by which he bore the person of the teachers and Pharisees of the unbelieving people, still sets up victims, in which men put their hope who do not receive the faith of Christ.
06_marg512: AND WHEN BALAAM SAW, etc. When he saw no demon, no contrary power standing by, heeding his victims, and the ministers of malice which he used for cursing shut out, he could understand thence also that it was good in the sight of the Lord to bless Israel. But that people which is now vain, and the teachers who, not believing in Christ, hold the people in vanity, will see in the last days, when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in and all Israel has begun to come to the faith of Christ: those who now have eyes and see not will then lift up their eyes to higher and spiritual senses, and will see and understand that it is good in the sight of the Lord to bless Israel, arranged in its parts and houses and families, each one in his own order to obtain the glory of the resurrection.
06_marg513: HE WENT NOT AS, etc. That is, he does not consider the will of God by foolish senses, as he was wont, in dumb animals and beasts. But he will recognize that God has no care for oxen, nor for sheep, nor for birds and other animals; namely, understand that the things written are written for the sake of men.
06_marg514: AUGUSTINE. And the Spirit of God came upon him, that is, upon Balaam. The Spirit of God was not made as though he were a thing made; but he came to be upon him, that is, it came about that he was upon him. As: He that cometh after me is preferred before me, that is, it came about that he was before me, that he was set above me, because he was before me. As: The Lord was made my helper; for the Lord is not a thing made, but it came about that he helped me. And: The Lord is become a refuge for the poor, that is, it came about that the poor fled to him. And: The hand of the Lord came upon me, that is, it came about that it was upon me; and many like things.
06_interl462: because: "A veil is upon their heart"; they neither see nor understand.
06_interl463: a vain people, or one casting them headlong
06_marg515: ORIGEN. Balaam the son of Beor hath said. The man who truly sees hath said, hearing the words of the strong one, who saw the vision of God in sleep; his eyes were opened. It is a wonder how Balaam is held so worthy that, taking up his parable, he should pronounce these things of himself. For how is he one who sees, who serves divination and auguries, who studies magic? Unless perhaps because the Spirit of God came to be in him and the word of God was put in his mouth, such great things are said of him. For neither Moses nor any of the prophets is easily found raised up with such praises. Whence these things seem rather to fit that people at the time when, turned to the Lord, it puts away the veil that was upon its heart. For God is a spirit; therefore he says his eyes were opened, as though those formerly shut are opened through the Spirit of God who came upon him, the veil being taken away. Now therefore is the time when he truly sees and truly hears the words of the strong one, and sees the vision of God in sleep; that is, he will see fulfilled the times which were marked out in sleep to the prophet Daniel, and the visions which were brought to him in sleep he will understand with opened eyes, so that he can say: "But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with open face" etc. Perhaps these are the eyes which elsewhere are called the eyes of earth, that is, the senses of the flesh, of which the serpent said to Eve: "For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened." And a little after: "Their eyes were opened." For some are the eyes which are opened through transgression; others those by which Adam and Eve saw before the transgression, by which the woman saw that the tree was good to eat.
