Christ therefore came into this world for judgment, that they who see not may see, and they who see may become blind; because in sinners the eyes which are better do not see, but those which are called the senses of the flesh and which were opened by the counsel of the serpent. It was the work of Christ, therefore, that those who do not see with the better eyes the things that are good, but with those opened by the counsel of the serpent the things that are evil, should become blind; and that those who were blind in those which the serpent opened should see the good things of the Lord in those which Jesus came to open. For unless the sight of evil things is first shut, the gaze on good things will not lie open. Hence too it is said: Who made the seeing and the blind? Seeing, namely, according to the Spirit of Christ; but blind according to the counsel of the serpent. It is apparent, therefore, that Balaam (because his eyes had been opened) speaks of himself: The man who truly sees hath said, and hearing the words of the strong one. And likewise the other ears are to be shut and opened. But if anyone wishes to take these things according to the history, he can say that in this, that Balaam saw that it is good in the sight of the Lord to bless Israel, his eyes were opened and he was made a man who truly sees. For he saw true things which were to come to Jacob or Israel. He heard the words of the strong one when God came to him and said to him in sleep: The word which I shall put in thy mouth, take heed that thou speak. And this will be the vision of God which he saw in sleep; and therefore he says his eyes were opened, because he could see what he saw.
06_interl464: of the one impelling, that is, the devil, who impels to sin
06_marg516: Because in sleep, his bodily eyes being shut, he saw these things by angelic ministry; but the eyes of the mind he has partly open, partly shut; who recognizes future mysteries, but does not correct his error. So the wicked do one thing in knowledge, another in manners; show one thing in the mouth, another in work.
06_interl465: who is perfect in act and work
06_interl466: of those, namely, who always walk and find no certain end of the journey
06_marg517: ORIGEN. How good are thy houses, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel, etc. He does not praise earthly houses, which they did not have beyond the other nations. But the people was divided by tribes, the tribes by peoples, the peoples by kindreds, the kindreds by houses of families; the houses were numbered by the number of men and by heads. That is, every male who was from twenty years old and upward, who could go forth to war; these things, foreseeing in spirit, he extolled. Nor is the sense to be regarded of the letter alone; for he speaks taking up a parable. For if you consider the divisions and orders of the peoples which will be in the true Israel in the resurrection, when each shall rise in his own order; if you can behold its tribes and kindreds, in which you will understand a kinship not so much of flesh and blood as of mind and spirit; then good are the houses of Jacob and the tabernacles of Israel. And a house is a thing founded and stable and enclosed by certain bounds; tabernacles are of those who are always on the way and walk and have not found the end of the journey. Jacob, therefore, is to be held in the persons of those who are perfect in acts; but Israel are those who study wisdom and knowledge. Because, therefore, the exercises of acts are closed by a certain end (for the perfection of works is not without end) when one has fulfilled all that he ought to do, the very perfection of works is called a good house. But of those who study wisdom and knowledge (because there is no end; for what end will there be of God, and what bound of wisdom? for the further one approaches, the deeper he will find it, for the wisdom of God is incomprehensible) he does not praise their houses, because they have not come to the end; but he wonders at the tabernacles in which they always walk and advance; and the more they advance, the more the way of advancing is increased and stretches out into the immeasurable. Therefore he names the tabernacle. And if anyone has begun some progress in knowledge, and knows something by experience, he knows that where he has come to some contemplation and knowledge of spiritual things, there the soul tarries as in a tabernacle. When therefore from these it searches out other things it has found, and advances to other understandings, as though the tabernacle were lifted, it tends to higher things and there sets the seat of the mind, fixed with stability of sense; then from these it finds others which the consequence of the former senses has laid open; and so, always stretching forth to the things before, it goes by tabernacles. For there is never a time when the soul, kindled by the spark of knowledge, can be idle and rest; but it is always called on from good things to better, and from better to higher. This journey of the wisdom of God, therefore, he has described with great and much comeliness, saying: "As shady groves, and as gardens beside the rivers" etc.
06_interl468: By these rivers the tabernacles of Israel are flooded, like those which the Lord pitched.
06_marg518: Others: Shady groves. To those who walk the journey of the wisdom of God, the groves are the whole assembly of the just and the choir of the prophets. For under the shade of the senses which they find written among them their souls are refreshed, and in their doctrine they delight as though walking through the shades of groves.
06_marg519: THE SAME. And as a garden beside the rivers. These find gardens beside the rivers like that in which is the tree of life. For the rivers are the evangelical or apostolic scriptures, or the helps of the heavenly powers toward such souls. For they are watered by them and flooded, and are nourished to all knowledge and acknowledgment of heavenly things. For although Christ is the river which makes glad the city of God, and the Holy Ghost is not only himself a river but is in those to whom it is given that "rivers flow from their belly", the Father too says: They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water; from which, namely, these rivers proceed. Flooded by these rivers, the tabernacles of Israel become as the tabernacles which the Lord pitched; he compares tabernacles, then, to tabernacles. For we can say that the houses of Jacob are the law and the tabernacles of Israel the prophets. For he praises not Jacob himself but his houses, nor Israel but his tabernacles, when his eyes have been opened. For as long as the veil is set upon the reading of the law and the prophets, neither the tabernacles seem good nor the houses praiseworthy; but when it is understood that the law and the prophets are spiritual, the letter that kills being removed, and the spirit that quickens perceived, the bodies and souls together of the believing people gathered from the Gentiles seem also to be praised. Let the house of Jacob be said of bodies, as is read in a certain little book, that Jacob is the house of Israel, that is, his body is called Jacob and his soul Israel. The body of Jacob, therefore, is praiseworthy in continence and chastity; but the tabernacles of Israel are perfect souls, to which the name of Israel belongs from seeing God. These tabernacles, therefore, are as the tabernacles which God pitched; those, namely, which he showed Moses when he was building the tabernacle, saying: See that thou make all things according to the pattern which was shown thee on the mount; that in imitation of these Israel, and each of us, might make tabernacles. Hence it seems to have come about that Peter and Andrew and the sons of Zebedee were found fishermen by trade, but Paul a maker of tents; and those are changed into fishers of men, and Paul, called an apostle through Christ, by a like transformation of his trade is transferred to setting up heavenly tabernacles. For he makes tabernacles by teaching the way of salvation and of the blessed mansions in heaven, and builds churches from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum. And he makes tabernacles after the likeness of those which God showed Moses on the mount. But each one who has gone out of Egypt and dwells in the desert ought to dwell in a tabernacle and keep the feast. For as the commemoration of the going out of Egypt is made by the Pasch and the unleavened bread, so the memory of the dwelling in the desert is made by tabernacles. For your fathers dwelt in tabernacles in the desert; these things must be done according to the words of the law and the prophets and the Psalms. For when the soul advances from the things that are written, and, forgetting the things that are behind, stretches forth to those that are before, and from the increase of virtues and the imitation of progress, it is rightly said to dwell in a tabernacle.
06_interl469: of which it is said: "That" "they may receive you into everlasting dwellings."
06_interl470: because they are not carried about with every wind of doctrine
06_marg520: Of God, namely, which hold up the branches of the vine transplanted out of Egypt, on which rests that fruit whose shadow covered the hills.
06_interl475: from the nation, or from the primitive Church
06_marg521: AND HIS SEED, etc. THE SAME. A man shall come forth from his seed and shall rule over many nations, and his kingdom shall be exalted above Gog. God brought him out of Egypt, "as the glory of the unicorn" etc. Christ came forth from the seed of Israel according to the flesh, who rules among the nations. Whence: Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, etc. Gog is interpreted "upon the roofs", and here it is not put for a nation, as is thought, but, as in many places, the Hebrew word itself has been left untranslated. For the sequence of the speech is such: and his kingdom shall be exalted upon the roofs, and his kingdom shall grow. To be exalted upon the roofs is said of the perfection of believers; to grow, of their multitude. In those, therefore, who are perfect, the kingdom of Christ is exalted upon the roofs, that is, over those who are in the heights. For perhaps there are some in heaven who advance more in some things, and those who are in the kingdom of Christ are exalted higher. Whence: "He that is on the housetop, let him not come down to take any thing out of his house"; for those who have come to lofty perfection ought not to come down to the lowly things of this world, which is called a house. And elsewhere: "That which you hear in the ear, preach ye upon the housetops." And his kingdom grows while the number of the Church is multiplied, until the Father puts all enemies under his feet and destroys the last enemy, death.
06_interl477: the king, namely, of the Amalecites, whom he spared
06_marg522: God brought him out of Egypt, after the death, namely, of Herod. Whence: "Out of Egypt have I called my son"; which seems taken from this place and inserted in the Gospel, or from the prophet Osee.
06_marg523: After the death of Herod; or the Father brought him out of the world to himself, that he might make a way for those who were to ascend from this world to God.
06_marg524: WHOSE STRENGTH IS LIKE, etc. For, casting out all the kingdoms of demons, he founded his one kingdom in glory, as of the true unicorn; for the horn signifies kingdom.
06_marg525: He shall eat the nations of his enemies, and shall take the marrow of their fatness, etc. The nations, namely, which his enemies possessed, he shall eat, the power of the enemy destroyed; and shall take the marrow of their fatness, when from these he thins the gross and carnal sense and turns it to spiritual understanding. And fatness is put in a bad sense, according to that: "The heart of this people is grown gross." And elsewhere: "The beloved grew fat and kicked." He eats the nations, therefore, and has as food those who believe in him. Whence: "My meat is to do the will of him that sent me"; whose will, namely, was that the nations should be converted to the faith. And subtlety is praiseworthy, because the spirit of wisdom, which is understanding and holy, is said to be both one and manifold, and subtle.
06_marg526: SEPTUAGINT. And with his darts he shall shoot the enemy. For Christ by his words conquered the devil and overcomes and breaks all who contradict. For everyone who sins is his enemy while he sins. But if, pierced by the words of God, he recognizes his sins and is pricked, and is converted to penance, he is said to be pierced by his darts.
06_interl479: Balaam prophesies also of the passion of Christ:
06_interl480: when, set on the cross, he triumphed over the principalities and powers
06_interl481: Christ a lion in the perfect, a lion's whelp in the little ones.
06_marg527: If you have understood how great rest the journey of wisdom has, how much grace and how much sweetness, do not pretend otherwise, do not neglect it; set out on the journey, nor shudder at the loneliness of the desert; for to one dwelling in such tabernacles the heavenly manna will come, and you will eat the bread of angels. Only begin; soon the angels will come into your fellowship, whom the cedars signify.
06_interl482: Christ the whelp, when, namely, he rose from the sleep of death.
06_marg528: SEPTUAGINT. Who shall rouse him? For now he is said to be raised by the Father, now he himself says he raises up the temple of his body; therefore the disposition is signified as of one asking.
06_marg529: Those who bless Christ bless, taken up into the communion of the Father's blessing. But those who curse are cursed. The Jews who cursed Christ are lamentably cursed. For what could befall those who curse wisdom, truth and life, but that they lie exiled from all these? For all these are Christ.
06_marg530: HE THAT CURSETH THEE, etc. ORIGEN. I think that not only he curses Christ who utters a word of cursing against him; but also he who under the name of Christian does evil, lives foully, and by dishonest words or deeds causes his name to be blasphemed. As he blesses God not only who causes the name of God to be blessed by words alone, but by acts, life and manners.
06_interl484: like things were set down before in the preface above
06_marg531: The Lord shows that even Balac understood that Balaam was no longer deceived by the ministry of demons, but was being transferred to better things by the power of God.
06_marg532: Balaam, knowing that answers were not brought him by the accustomed ministers but by him who has power over all, rightly seems to protest that he cannot go beyond the word of the Lord or utter anything good or evil from his own mouth. For he who speaks cannot be changed by sacrifices or gifts, with whom there is no change. And therefore the priest cannot be changed by reward where God is not moved by gifts. Yet Balaam, about to depart, begins again to prophesy: "And he says: I give thee counsel" etc.
06_marg533: ORIGEN. Come, I give thee counsel what this people shall do to thy people in the last days. And taking up his parable he said, etc. I would ask what is the sense or order of the words. For he does not seem to give counsel, but says what this people will do to thy people in the last days. Since it would seem to have been fittingly said: Come, I will prophesy to thee what this people will do to thy people; and it would be consistent, so that Balaam seemed to prophesy of the things which the people of Israel would do to the people of Balac or to the other nations, that it would leave none safe of the cities of Moab. This prophecy also, which he joins concerning Christ and says: "A star shall rise out of Jacob" etc., would seem fittingly placed if he said: Come and I will prophesy to thee. Counsel, then, is to be understood thus: I give thee divine counsel; namely, what is to be fulfilled in the last days, now revealed to me, I open to thee and make manifest, that thou mayest know what this people will do to thy people; this is the counsel of God I make manifest to thee. Likewise also I think is to be understood what the Apostle says: "Who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor?" For here "who" is taken not for none, but for rare and exceptional. For the Son knew the mind of God, who says: "No one knoweth the Father but the Son, and he to whom it shall please the Son to reveal him." What the Father knows, therefore, the Son knows, both his counsel and his mind. The Spirit too, who searches the deep things of God, knows his mind. The Son, therefore, who knows the mind of God is his counsellor; not that the Son or the Spirit gives counsel to one ignorant what he should do, but is partaker and knower of his counsel and will. Balaam therefore, because he was making Balac partaker of the counsel which God had revealed to him, says: "Come, I give thee counsel"; as one who truly sees and has truly heard.
06_interl486: not "saith": Thus saith the Lord, as is the custom of the prophets.
06_marg534: BALAAM HATH SAID, etc. ORIGEN. Balaam the son of Beor hath said: The man who truly sees and truly hears the words of God, knowing the knowledge of the Most High, etc. I have not easily found this written of any of the prophets. I wonder therefore how it is written of Balaam, to whom it was not even granted to say what is in use among the prophets: Thus saith the Lord; but he says: Balaam hath said, etc. How does he know the knowledge of the Most High, who even taught Balac how to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, that they should eat things sacrificed and commit fornication? For of the apostles it is hardly found said that they know the knowledge of the Most High; although Paul said he had heard secret words which it is not granted to man to utter, he did not profess to have the knowledge of the Most High. In Ecclesiasticus it is said: "All wisdom is from the Lord God." Which perhaps we can understand thus, as though the wisdom of the world, which shall be destroyed, and of the princes of the world, and any by which false knowledge is commended, were also from God. But in what follows it is read: The learning of wickedness is not wisdom; where it is taught that every discipline which asserts falsehood, even if it seems vehement and probable, yet ought not to be called wisdom. But all wisdom is from God; that is, every skill which is held necessary for human use in any art, or the knowledge of anything whatever, is given by God. Whence it is said in Job: "Who hath given to women the wisdom of weaving and the skill of embroidery?" And of Beseleel the Lord says: "I have filled him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, that he may understand every work and be an architect to work in silver and gold" etc. This knowledge, therefore, is from the Most High. How not geometry, from which the knowledge of architecture is derived? In Zacharias too a geometrical line is spoken of, with which the angel measures Jerusalem. What of music, the skill of which, and the discipline of melody and rhythms, David so attained that from all these he found sounds by which he soothed even the king vexed by an evil spirit? Of the knowledge of medicine I think there is no doubt. For what knowledge is more from God than that of health, in which also the powers of herbs and the qualities and differences of juices are known? The knowledge of Balaam, therefore, for which he was called from the mountains of Mesopotamia from the east, has its origin from the Most High. Whence he knew the natures of animals or the movements of birds or the differences of sounds; and what he received for the knowledge of good things he turned to the uses of evil things; as if a physician became a poisoner, and in place of remedies brought diseases, in place of health deaths. But that we may know more fully that the knowledge of all wisdom draws its origin from God, but is turned aside to evil by men of evil purpose or even by demons mingling certain corruptions with the wisdom of God, it is to be noted that the Lord gave Daniel and his companions knowledge and understanding and prudence in every art of letters; and to Daniel he gave understanding in every word and vision and dreams; and they were found by the king ten times wiser than the sophists and philosophers and enchanters and magicians who were in all his kingdom. From all these things it is gathered how Balaam spoke of himself; namely, so that it is understood that the origin of all knowledge took its beginning from him, but by the vice of human malice, with the demons conspiring and stealing in, the things granted for profit were turned to destruction.
06_marg535: The man hath said whose eye is stopped up, the hearer of the words of God hath said, who hath beheld the vision of the Almighty, who falleth, and so his eyes are opened. The wicked man does not know the evils he does except when he has begun to be punished for them. Balaam gave counsel against the Israelites; but afterwards in punishment he saw what he had first committed in fault. But the elect, because they ought not to sin, their eyes, providing, lie open before the fall. But the wicked man opened his eyes after the fall, because after the fault he now perceives in punishment that he ought to have avoided the evil which he did.
06_interl487: because he does not know his own evils which he does, except when he is punished
06_interl489: because he does not lift his intent from earthly things
06_interl490: because by contemplation he stretches his eyes in consideration
06_marg536: Often the wicked man wonders at the eternal judgments; when he hears the preaching of the heavenly fatherland he loves it, and is astonished at the works of the divine disposition. Lying down, therefore, he considers the miracles, because he weighs the power of God in knowing it, but does not love it in living.
06_interl491: Christ, of whom: A star shall rise out of Jacob etc.
06_marg537: I SHALL SEE HIM, BUT, etc. Another text: I shall show him, and not now; I shall bless him, and he does not draw near. These things are referred to those whose person he bears. Because the teachers of the law and the scribes show Christ promised in the law and the prophets, but not now, that is, when he came; but when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in, then they will show, then they will bless him whom now they blaspheme. But the time in which these things shall be is far off, and at the end of the world. Therefore he says: I shall show him, that is, to the people which will then be saved; but not now.
06_marg538: While I speak these things; because when the fulness of time came God sent his Son.
06_interl492: which the magi saw in the east
06_interl494: "There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse."
06_marg539: A STAR SHALL RISE OUT OF JACOB, etc. ORIGEN. Of this star it is said in the Gospel that it came and stood over where the child was. But whether it departed thence, or vanished, or was taken up, or what at all became of it thence, is not said. But perhaps as at the baptism the Spirit descended upon Christ as a dove and remained upon him, and the voice of the Father was heard: "This is my beloved Son", so too the star which came over where the child was and stood remained in Christ. And as we receive that the Spirit of God came upon him there and remained in him, so that the Spirit of God never withdrew from him, so the star which came and stood over him never departed. Therefore I think that star was a token of his divinity. The order of the prophecy too shows the same, when of the divinity it says: A star shall rise out of Jacob; but of the humanity: A man shall rise up out of Israel; so that both may appear evidently prophesied.
06_interl495: of which it is said: "Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron" etc.
06_marg540: Fastening the principalities and powers to the cross; otherwise he could not save the Moabites, unless he had first laid waste the leaders of impiety.
06_interl498: he shall lead captive the one leading captive
06_marg541: THE SAME. And he shall make a prey of all the sons of Seth. This is Seth the son of Adam, of whom it is said: "God hath given me another seed for Abel, whom Cain slew." For from him is the whole human race; for those who were of Cain perished in the flood. The sons of Seth, therefore, are all men. He takes as prey, therefore, all the sons of Seth, the demons conquered; those, namely, who were held under their dominion; whom Christ leads as the prey of victory and brings back as the spoils of salvation. Whence: "Ascending on high, he led captivity captive." The captivity, namely, of the human race, which the devil had taken to perdition, Christ led captive and called back from death to life.
06_interl500: the flesh, which before fought against the spirit
06_marg542: AND IDUMEA SHALL BE. THE SAME. And Edom shall be his inheritance; Esau his enemy, etc. Edom is the same as Esau. He, according to the history, is the enemy of Israel. But at the coming of Christ he himself will be his inheritance; that is, he will be received to the faith, he will not be shut out from the inheritance of Christ. Spiritually, therefore, by Edom is understood the flesh, which is adverse to the spirit and is its enemy. But at the coming of Christ, when the flesh has been subjected to the spirit through the hope of the resurrection, it too will come to the inheritance; for not the soul only, but the flesh too, which had once been an enemy, will through obedience to the spirit be a sharer of the future inheritance.
06_interl501: it shall obey, namely, reason and virtue
06_marg543: ORIGEN. And Israel has done in strength; because, namely, then Edom or Esau, that is, the nature of the flesh, will be called into the fellowship of the inheritance, when Israel, that is, the soul, has been made in strength, fittingly filled with virtues. For if the soul does not come to the virtues, but persists in sloth, neither will the flesh come to the inheritance, but to the judgment of him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
06_interl504: that is, Christ according to the flesh
06_interl506: saying: "He that shall lose his life for me shall find it."
06_interl509: of the heretics or philosophers, who fortify their dogmas against God
06_marg544: AND SHALL DESTROY THE REMAINS, etc. THE SAME. He shall destroy him that is delivered from the city. Let us see if perhaps it can be explained in this way. Let us understand the city here as the world; as in the Gospel it is said of the prodigal son who wasted his father's substance: "He went, it says, and cleaved to one of the chief citizens of that country", by whom, received, he is sent into the field to feed swine. This city, therefore, of which he was a chief citizen, is the world. He therefore who is delivered from this city, that is, whom Christ delivers from this world, he destroys, saying: "He that shall lose his life for me shall save it." Wholesomely, therefore, Jesus destroys him whom he rescues from this world. If therefore we wish to come to salvation and be delivered from the world, let us lose our souls by a necessary and profitable loss. For he loses his soul according to Christ who bridles its desires, cuts away its covetings, chastises luxury and dissoluteness, and in nothing does his own will, but God's. By these things the soul is said to perish. For its former life perishes, and the new begins which is in Christ; with whom if we die, we shall also live together.
06_interl511: the fifth and last vision of Balaam
06_marg545: This cannot be referred to the historical Amalec. For he was not first in antiquity; but to the spiritual one, who is named Amalec by turning peoples aside from God and making Gentiles out of worshippers of God. And he is called the beginning of nations because he gave the beginning for men to become Gentiles, changing the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of corruptible man. For as in the people of God Christ is the beginning, so in the people which turns aside from God and becomes Gentile, Amalec.
06_marg546: Amalec the beginning of nations, and their seed shall perish. It is written in Genesis: "And these kings came together to the fountain of judgment, that is Cades, and they slew all the princes of Amalec and the Amorrhites." But it is asked whether there are two nations of the same name Amalec? For in the catalogue of the sons of Esau it is written: "These are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in mount Seir. And these are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz the son of Ada the wife of Esau. And the sons of Eliphaz were: Theman, Omar, Sepho, Gatham, Cenez. And Thamna was the concubine of Eliphaz the son of Esau, and she bore him Amalec. These are the sons of Ada the wife of Esau." And after a little: "And these are the dukes of the sons of Esau, the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: duke Theman, duke Omar, duke Sepho, duke Cenez, duke Core, duke Gatham, duke Amalec." This Amalec, therefore, was the son of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau by the concubine Thamna. But let us return to the first mention of Amalec, where those who returned "and came to the fountain of judgment, which is called Cades, slay all the princes of Amalec". For Cades is interpreted "sanctification" or "holy"; but Amalec, "licking up the people" or "turning the people aside". Those, therefore, who return to the holy and turn themselves to sanctification slay Amalec, who namely licks up the people or turns it aside. This is the contrary power and the spiritual wickednesses which turn the people aside from God. Their princes are the principalities against which the saints have their wrestling; whom yet they will not be able to overcome unless they are turned to holiness. He has always before his eyes the fountain of judgment; for he looks forward to the day of judgment, and, his heart purified, beholds both the punishments of the wicked and the beatitudes of the godly; and doing this he lays low the princes of the Amalecites. But others are subjected to the princes of Amalec. For these he licks up and consumes, and turns such a people aside from God. These things are referred to that first Amalec. Let us see this Amalec too, the son of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau, whom Thamna the concubine bore him; whose father Eliphaz is interpreted "God hath scattered me"; the mother Thamna, first indeed "degenerate", then "a moved failing"; necessarily he who is begotten of these is the enemy of Israel, licking up or turning aside the people. For he was the first who attacked the Hebrews when they had gone out of Egypt, in Raphidim, when Moses said to Jesus: "Choose out men, and go out and fight against Amalec" etc. And after a little it is written: "That Jesus put Amalec to flight, and his people, by the edge of the sword. And the Lord said to Moses: Write this for a memorial in a book, and deliver it to the ears of Jesus; for I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven. And Moses built an altar, and called the name thereof: The Lord my refuge. Because with a hidden hand the Lord fights against Amalec from generation to generation." See what is to be understood by Amalec, against whom God fights with a hidden, that is, invisible, hand from generation to generation. In Deuteronomy too it is written: "Remember what Amalec did to thee in the way when thou camest out of Egypt: how he met thee, and slew the hindmost of the army, who sat down being weary" etc. Note how Amalec withstood the people of God in the way, yet could not cut off its head, but the tail; that is, those who followed last behind and, not forgetting the things that were behind, did not stretch themselves forth to those before. Whence: "No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God." For he who is found behind in the tail, Amalec will cut him off. In the book of Kings too Samuel says to Saul: "Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I have reckoned up all that Amalec hath done to Israel, how he opposed them in the way when they came up out of Egypt. Now therefore go, and smite Amalec, and utterly destroy all that he hath; spare him not" etc. A little after: "It repenteth me that I have made Saul king." And here too, then, observe how God through the prophet commands Saul to fight against Amalec and spare none; and because he spared, he incurred an inexpiable offence, so that against his own nature God said: "It repenteth me that I have made Saul king." Let us not spare, therefore, him who turns aside the people or licks up and devours it. The invisible Amalec, who resists in the way and assails those who wish to go up out of Egypt and climb from the darkness of the world to the land of promise, and if he finds them weary, failing, looking back, set at the last and in the tail, will cut them off and destroy them. Therefore we must hold to the things before, and go up to the top of the mountain, and the hands must always be lifted in prayer to heaven, that so at last Amalec may be conquered. David, when he had waged many wars and there had been very fierce and frequent conflicts against the foreigners, is not written to have obtained the kingdom until he had first subdued Amalec. Whence also David returned after he had slain Amalec, and took up the kingdom of Saul; though Amalec is written to have first made great slaughter among the people of Israel and burned very many cities. For before the coming of the true David, who was born of the seed of David, the spiritual Amalecites, that is, the contrary powers, made great slaughter among the people of Israel and took captive the two wives of David himself, namely the Jewish and the Gentile people. For it is clear that all were under sin; but the issue of things did not remain in these. But David, coming, found the Amalecites scattered, eating and drinking and exulting in the prey, and slew them; and after this slaughter he returned and took up the kingdom. Of this Amalec, therefore, Balaam says: Amalec the beginning of nations, and their seed shall perish. Their seed is the persuasion and doctrine by which they teach men to turn aside from God. This, therefore, shall perish, not they themselves in whom it was sown; for they, when they are converted and lament, shall be saved. This exposition stands against those who accuse the God of the law of hardness and cruelty, who pronounce that not only the nation of Amalec but its seed too will perish; since the nation is referred to the spiritual wickednesses, and the seed is expounded as the doctrine of Gentile superstitions and the worship of idols and every sect which turns the people aside from God.
06_marg547: THE SAME. And seeing the Cinite he said: Strong is thy habitation, and if thou put thy nest in a rock; and if there be to thee for Beor a nest of cunning, the Assyrians shall lead thee captive, etc. Beor is the father of Balaam, figuring the heretics. And it is said that the Cinite can be safe if he puts his nest, namely his hope, in the rock, that is, Christ; and the cunning of the heretics does not surround and hem him in. For if this happens, it will profit nothing that he seems placed in the rock; for he will be led captive by the Assyrians, namely the evil spirits, by whom the heretics are taken captive. The conjunction too seems to trouble the sense of this exposition; but it is native to the Hebrew tongue to use the conjunction frequently, so that at times it is redundant. For each tongue has something proper to it which among others seems faulty. Here, therefore, the conjunction is redundant and superfluous. Let the Cinite, therefore, who is interpreted "possession", beware; although, if he possesses and turns aside to wicked dogmas, he is delivered to the Assyrians. For those who blaspheme, set in the Church, are delivered to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. And they are delivered to the Assyrians, which is interpreted "directing", not that they may perish utterly, but that they may be directed and corrected and learn not to blaspheme.
06_marg548: He does not seem to name the Cinite very culpably, to whom Saul said: "Go, depart from Amalec, lest I destroy thee with him; for thou hast shewn kindness to Israel" etc. His habitation is strong if he puts his nest in the rock, which is Christ.
06_marg549: The Cinite is "possessor". Those who possess present things, who are strong in wit, who are skilled in the wit of worldly wisdom, truly build themselves a strong habitation if they feel themselves weak, and set the confidence of the mind to be nourished in the lofty humility of Christ, and by the flight of the heart pass beyond all that passes away.
06_marg550: The chosen from the number of the wise, the seekers of truth, live a perpetual life. Whence: "They that explain me shall have life everlasting."
06_marg551: The devil, namely, to whom the heretics are delivered to be directed and corrected.
06_interl516: the conclusion of the prophecy of Balaam
06_marg552: He is often said to speak in parables, lest we take anything in these things not as a parable but according to the letter.
06_interl517: according to God, not by the common life
06_marg553: So happy is he who sees, feels, understands and believes that God has done these things so.
06_marg554: When, namely, a star shall rise out of Jacob, a man shall rise up out of Israel, and shall destroy Amalec, and his seed shall perish; that is, when Christ shall come and destroy the worship of idols and subject the power of demons.
06_marg555: THEY SHALL COME, etc. It seems to signify that about the time of the Lord's incarnation the Romans would come to overcome the Assyrians, the Hebrews and all the eastern peoples, and at last to lose the kingdom, according to the statue of Daniel; or that at the coming of Christ, at the end of times, which the western part signifies, all the kingdoms of the world are overcome by the sword of the spirit, that is, the word of God, and in the time of antichrist the preaching of the Gospel ceases.
06_marg556: And they shall come out of the hands of the Cetheans and shall afflict the Assyrians. Cetheans are interpreted "the blow of the end". Those, therefore, who, converted to God and taught by Christ, escape the blow which shall come upon the wicked at the end of the world, shall afflict the Assyrians; that is, those set in the contest, under whose feet God shall crush Satan, shall afflict the Assyrians, that is, the demons. For they shall tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy.
06_interl519: when they have poured out their strength
06_marg557: He is a Hebrew who passes over from Egypt to the land of promise, from darkness to light, from death to life. But he cannot obtain it without great struggle. He afflicts, therefore, and is afflicted; he strikes the adversary and is struck. The Assyrians, therefore, afflict the Hebrews, that is, the people of God, as they are afflicted by them.
06_interl521: the just Judge saying: Depart, ye cursed, into everlasting fire.
06_marg558: THE SAME. And they themselves likewise shall perish. Not with the Hebrews, namely, but likewise, that is, at once, as soon as they have afflicted the Hebrews. For the Greek word puts likewise for at once. This, therefore, will be the end of all: that Assur, to whom offenders among the people of God were delivered, either for the destruction of the flesh that the spirit might be saved, or that he might learn not to blaspheme, should himself also perish by him who has power to destroy in gehenna, who will say to them: "Depart into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels." One sheep of a hundred perished; but the good shepherd, leaving the ninety-nine on the mountains and coming down to this vale of tears, sought it and found it and carried it back laid on his shoulders. But this Assur, who is said to perish at the end of all things, I do not know whether he can ever be either sought or found; he perished therefore not by straying but by judgment, not moved by a slip but stopped up by perseverance. For as to what is written: "I will kill and I will make to live; I will bring down to hell and bring back again", I do not know whether it looks to all generally or only to those whom the deceit of the devil has brought down to death.
06_marg559: Because Balaam, constrained by the power of God, could not curse Israel, wishing to please the king, he says: "Come, I give thee counsel"; but he did not disclose the counsel; which yet is related at the end of this book, but more fully where John says: "Thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat, and to commit fornication." As if: this people conquers not by its own strength, but by seeking God and by keeping chastity. Cast down its chastity and it will be conquered of itself; the fight must be not by the strength of soldiers but by the comeliness of women; beauty conquers armed men, loveliness takes iron captive. When the women have perceived that they have surrendered to lust, let them not give themselves to them in their desire before they eat of the sacrifices of idols and are consecrated to Beelphegor. And king Balac at once obeyed the counsel.
06_interl522: SEPTUAGINT: Israel put in at Sethim.
06_interl524: Because it did not put in well, it was refuted by God.
06_marg560: ORIGEN. The history itself edifies us, teaching that fornication wars against us. But if we have the arms of the Apostle, the darts of luxury will not harm us; that is, if we have the breastplate of justice, the helmet of salvation, the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God, and the shield of faith, our feet shod in the preparation of the Gospel of peace. If we cast away these arms, we give place to the devil, and the whole choir of demons takes us captive, and God is angry against us; and not only in the present, but in the future we shall be punished. Chastity and justice, prudence and the other virtues make us conquer; but luxury, lust, avarice, impiety and all malice make us be conquered.
06_marg561: THE SAME. John says in the Apocalypse: "Thou hast there some that hold the doctrine of Balaam" etc. He who does what Balaam did seems to teach his doctrine. As the doctrine of Jezabel is mentioned there, not that anyone of the disciples of Jezabel teaches what she handed down; but he who persecutes the prophets as she did, or takes some by guile, or destroys the innocent by false charges, he holds the doctrine of Jezabel. So therefore he who by wicked counsel begets a stumblingblock in the people, and provokes the offence and wrath of God, either by communicating in the sacrifices of idols or by serving lust, holds the doctrine of Balaam. Execrable, then, is even the fornication of the body, which violates the temple of God and takes the members of Christ and makes them the members of a harlot. But more execrable is the general fornication, in which every kind of sin is contained alike; when the soul, namely, taken into the fellowship of the word of God and joined to him in marriage, is corrupted by the adversary of him who espoused her to himself in faith. The bridegroom and husband of the clean soul, then, is the word of God, that is, Christ. Whence: "For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ" etc. While, therefore, the soul cleaves to the bridegroom, and embraces and hears his word, she receives from him the seed of the word, and conceives and bears sons, that she may be saved through the bearing of children, if she continue in faith and charity (even if before, like Eve, she was seduced). Where the union of the soul with the word of God has been made and the embrace given to each other, a noble offspring is born: chastity, namely, justice, patience and all the virtues. But if she prostitutes herself to the devil and the demons, she will bear sons of adultery, namely all sins. Through each thing, then, that we do our soul begets sons, namely thoughts and works. And if what it does is according to the law and the word of God, it brings forth the spirit of salvation and will be saved through the bearing of children, of whom it is said: "Thy children as olive plants round about thy table." But if what it does is against the law, from the conception of the contrary spirit it brings forth sons of sin and cursing. The soul always brings forth, always begets, conceiving either of the word or of the contrary spirit. Perhaps to these generations looks what was said: "For when they were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil" etc. For these generations of the soul, begotten of the Holy Ghost, are loved before they do anything good; but if of the wicked spirit, before they accomplish anything evil, by this very fact that the soul has brought forth a will of this kind, the execrable conception of an evil will is worthily held in hatred. Therefore perhaps the child Chanaan too is cursed before he was born, because his father had sinned; and Noe, prophesying, when he marked out all the best things for each of his sons, when he came to Cham said: Cursed be the child Chanaan. Whence: "O daughter of Babylon, miserable! Blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us. Blessed be he that shall take and dash his little ones against the rock." And if the Babylonian conception has not yet done any work in us, while it is little, do not pity it; kill it at once, for it is hateful; dash it against the rock, lest it grow, lest the works of confusion be increased in it. The rock is Christ; set in the sight of his dread judgment, let this offspring perish. These things have been said of the general fornication, of which bodily fornication is a species. Hence Paul says: "He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit, and he who is joined to a harlot is one body." As if every soul is joined either to the Lord or to a harlot. But by the Lord he meant the virtues: Christ is, that is, the word, wisdom, virtue, justice and the like; but by the harlot every species of malice. Whence: A woman meets him, having the appearance of a harlot, who makes the hearts of young men fly away. This harlot is malice; he who joins himself to this harlot is made one body of malice. As therefore he who joins himself to the Lord joins himself to wisdom, justice, piety and truth, and with them all is made one spirit, so he who joins himself to this harlot joins himself to unchastity, iniquity, lying and all evils, with which he is made one body.
06_interl525: they were consecrated, namely, to the idols of the Gentiles
06_marg562: As though he had eaten even of the things sacrificed to idols, which are execrable before God. For what agreement has God with idols?
06_marg563: The Apostle says: If anyone sees one having knowledge sitting at meat in the idol's temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols? Where he seems to pronounce the thing itself not so much grievous as the offence of him who, seeing these things, is provoked to the same, since he is not fortified by a like judgment; so that he is guilty not so much for himself as for another. Perhaps men studious of Greek letters and lovers of philosophy, held by desire of the old studies, ate the dogmas of the philosophers as things sacrificed to idols; which perhaps did not unsettle those who had received the knowledge of the truth; but those less learned in Christ, if they read such things imitating them, could be wounded. Because, therefore, charity seeks not what is profitable to itself but what is to many, let us take such food of the word as not only edifies and delights us but does not offend those who see. There is, then, a thing sacrificed to idols not only in foods but in words. Every speech which teaches piety, justice and truth is sacrificed to God; but that which teaches unchastity, injustice, impiety, to idols; and he who receives it eats things sacrificed to idols.
06_interl526: not only that, but they ate
06_marg564: Note the order: concupiscence first deceives evil servants, then gluttony, last impiety takes them captive, whose wage, fornication, is paid out.
06_marg565: Solomon, though he was most wise, bowed his sides to many women; therefore he was deceived. Yet I do not think that the many women are not called many dogmas; which, when the most wise man wished to search out and know each, he could not keep himself within the rule of the divine law. The Moabite philosophy deceived him, so that he sacrificed to the Moabite idol, and of the Ammonites and the other nations whose women he is said to have received; he built temples, sacrificed to idols. It is a great work to be mingled with so many dogmas as with women and not turn aside from the truth, but to say steadfastly: "There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and young maidens without number. One is my dove."
06_interl527: because the law reproves them as negligent and slothful
06_marg566: Consecrated, namely, to the mysteries of the idol which among the Madianites is worshipped chiefly by women, and is a species of foulness; but what it is, or of what kind or form, is hardly found written, perhaps lest it pollute the hearer. Since, then, there are many species of foulness, one is called Beelphegor. Everyone, therefore, who commits anything foul in any species of foulness is consecrated to Beelphegor.
06_marg567: And he was initiated to Beelphegor, etc. Through all the sins we commit, above all if we sin not by some stealing upon us but by set purpose, we are consecrated to that demon to whom what we commit is a care. And perhaps we are consecrated to as many demons as the sins we commit, and we receive the mysteries of this idol or that. Whence: "For the mystery of iniquity already worketh." Going about, therefore, they seek how to consecrate each one to their mysteries. If you feel the wicked spirit speak in your heart to lead you to some work of sin, understand that he wishes to bind you over to some demon, that you may receive the mysteries of the devil. There is present to each of us a good angel, who rules, who warns, who for the correcting of our acts and the begging of mercies daily sees the face of God. And according to the Apocalypse of John an angel presides over each Church in general, who is either praised for the good deeds of the people or blamed for its offences. In which I am moved to wonder at a stupendous mystery: that God has such care of us that he suffers even his angels to be blamed and confuted for us. For as when a boy is handed over to a tutor, if he appears trained in less worthy disciplines, the blame is referred to the tutor, and the boy is not so reproved by the father as the tutor; unless the boy, hard and wanton and froward, has spurned the wholesome warnings of the tutor. But what becomes of that soul the prophet teaches, saying: "And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard" etc. For the soul is of its own choice, and therefore the judgment of God is just, because of its own will it obeys either good or evil counsellors. But the salvation of man is a greater care to God than his perdition to the devil. For as though the diligence of the angels were not enough against the snares of the demons and of those who draw to sin, the only-begotten of God himself is present, defends, guards and draws us to himself. Whence: I am with you even to the consummation of the world. Nor is it enough to be with us; he uses force on us and draws us to salvation. Whence: "I will draw all things to myself." See how he draws not only the willing but also the hesitating. Whence to one who wished to bury his father he gave not even a space of time, but said: "Let the dead bury their dead" etc. The Father too draws us. Whence: "No man cometh to me, unless my Father draw him"; who says to his servants: Whomsoever you shall find, compel them to come in. The Holy Ghost also says: Separate me Paul and Barnabas, etc. He also forbids Paul to go into Asia, and compels him to go to Jerusalem, foretelling that bonds and prisons await him there.
06_marg568: TAKE ALL THE PRINCES OF THE PEOPLE, etc. ORIGEN. Perhaps these things are referred to the angels. For they will come to judgment with us and stand before the sun of justice, lest perhaps there was some cause in them of our having sinned, lest perhaps they spent less work to call us back from sins. Whence in the Apocalypse: I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, and the like. For if the angel who received us sealed from God hopes for a reward for the things we have done well, he fears also to be blamed for things done ill. And therefore they are said to be shown against the sun, that it may appear by whose fault the sins were committed through which we are consecrated to Beelphegor or to any idol, according to the quality of the sin. But if the prince, that is, the angel assigned to each, did not fail, but warned of good things and spoke in my heart, at least in that wherein conscience calls me back from sin, and I, spurning his warnings and the rein of conscience, broke out into sins, the penalty will be doubled for me, for contempt of the warner and for the crime committed. Do not wonder if angels come with men to judgment. For the Lord himself will come to judgment with the princes of his people. Let the princes be shown, then, and if the fault is in them, the wrath of God ceases from the people. We ought therefore to be the more anxious, knowing that not only for our own acts shall we stand before the tribunal of the Lord, but the angels too, as our princes and leaders. Whence: "Obey your prelates, for they watch as being to render an account of your souls."
06_marg569: The people sins, and the princes are shown against the sun to be examined, that they may be reproved by the light. For they are reproved not only for their own offences; for the princes are compelled to render account for the people, lest perhaps they did not teach, did not warn, did not carefully reprove those who first sinned, so that the contagion should not be spread among the peoples. For the wrath of God would be turned upon them, and would cease from the people. If men thought on these things they would not canvass for headships. It is enough for each to be reproved and render account for his own sins. What need is there to be shown against the sun for the sins of the people, before which nothing can be hidden, nothing obscured?
06_marg570: And the Lord said to Moses: "Take the leaders of the people and show them to the Lord against the sun, and the wrath of the anger of the Lord shall be taken away from Israel." The Lord was angry at the fornications of Israel, carnal, namely, and spiritual. For they had both mingled themselves with the daughters of Moab and been consecrated to idols. He told Moses to show the leaders of the people to the Lord against the sun, that is, openly, in the sight of this light. For the Greek says paradeigmatison, which could be called "make examples", because paradeigma is called an example. For Aquila said: Fasten, or rather fasten up; but Symmachus: Hang. But it is a wonder that the scripture left off relating whether this was fulfilled according to the Lord's command; which I do not see could have been disregarded, or, if disregarded, disregarded with impunity. But if it was done and passed over in silence, why does the scripture say that the Lord was appeased, and the plague ceased, by Phinees transfixing the adulterers? As though, the leaders having been crucified as the Lord had commanded, the indignation still persisting seemed to need appeasing in another way; since what he had foretold could not be false, saying: "The wrath of the Lord's punishment shall be turned away from Israel." If therefore it had been done, who would doubt that the wrath had been turned away? What need was there, then, that Phinees should take vengeance on the adulterers to appease God, and the scripture testify that the Lord was thus appeased? Unless perhaps we understand that, when Moses was arranging to fulfil what the Lord had commanded concerning the leaders of the people, he wished also according to the law to punish such crimes, so that he commanded each to kill his neighbour consecrated to strange gods; and meanwhile Phinees did that; and so, the wrath of God being now appeased, there was no need for the leaders of the people to be crucified. This severity, surely fitting to that time, shows clearly enough to the prudent of faith how great an evil is fornication and idolatry.
06_interl529: openly, namely, that they may be an example to all
06_marg571: ORIGEN. These things edified the former people; but you who have been redeemed by Christ, from whose hands the bodily sword has been taken and to whom the sword of the spirit has been given, seize this sword. And if you see the Israelite sense whoring with the Madianite harlots, that is, the will with devilish thoughts, do not spare, do not pretend otherwise; strike at once, destroy the sin; striking and piercing the womb itself too, that is, the secret places of nature, cut out the very tinder of sinning, lest it conceive and beget further, and the cursed offspring of sins defile the camp of Israel. For so you will allay the wrath of God. For you have forestalled the day of judgment, which is called the day of wrath and fury; and the tinder of sin, which here is called the womb of the woman, being destroyed, you come secure to the judgment. Let us pray, then, that I may always find this sword of the spirit ready, through which the very seeds and conceptions of guilt may be destroyed, and God become propitious to you through the true Phinees, our Lord Jesus Christ.
06_interl531: we too must rise up against such things
06_marg572: It signifies that through the cross of Christ not only idolatry but every affection or concupiscence of the flesh is destroyed, and so God is appeased.
06_marg573: Because, forsaking the light of truth and justice, they loved the blindness of idolatry and fornication, deprived of the light of the eternal sun they run into the darkness of death. For the visible sun lights the world for twenty-four hours, and by its circuit puts to flight the darkness of night; so too Christ, to put to flight the darkness of sin, lights the world through the apostles and prophets.
06_marg574: Whoever, pricked with the zeal of God, despises and presses down the goads of the flesh, or corrects those subject to him lest they wanton, acquires an everlasting priesthood, belonging to the same one of whom it is said: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech"; with whom they shall possess an everlasting kingdom. Phinees is interpreted "sparing with the mouth", or "rested with the mouth", or "augury of the mouth"; Eleazar, "God my helper", or "help of God"; Aaron, "mountain of strength", or "strong mountain". These names fittingly express the aforesaid sense. For he who spares with the mouth, lest he speak wicked things, and expounds heavenly mysteries, fulfilling a godly labour for his hearers through the help of God, happily ascends to the mountain of strength, that is, Christ.
06_marg575: AND THE NAME, etc. The Israelite who committed fornication with the Madianite woman signifies those who, separated from the Church by error or wicked working, stir up blasphemy of God among the faithful; to whom it is said: Through you the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles; whom they show in name only as Israelites. For Zambri too is interpreted "psalm" or "song"; Salu, "looking to temptation"; Simeon, "he heard sadness" or "name of a dwelling"; Cozbi, "immeasurable cup" or "sacrifice to me"; Sur, "wall" or "straitness"; Madian, "contradiction" or "answer". Zambri therefore signifies the bodily or spiritual fornicator, who stirs up among the enemies of Christ not a song of praise but a psalm of mockery. Whence: "They that drank wine made me their song." This one, then, looking to temptation and consenting to temptation, under the name of a dwelling, that is, of a churchman, brings sadness upon the faithful by his fall; because he is filled with love of the immeasurable cup, that is, serving gluttony, he sacrificed himself to the devil when he gave his members over to lust. This one, by his wicked work producing the answer of contradiction from the adversaries of God, plunged himself into the walls and straitness of the eternal prison, where he will be tormented day and night until the last farthing.
06_interl538: He heard sadness, or name of a dwelling
06_marg576: ORIGEN. Because those who had been enrolled first fell for their sin, a second people now, succeeding in their place, is called to the numbering. And what had not been said of those is said of these, namely: "To these shall the land be divided for a lot according to the number of names" etc. If it had been said of the former it would have been false, because they fell in the desert for their sin; but for these all that is promised was fulfilled.
06_marg577: NUMBER THE WHOLE, etc. Again the people are numbered, and the Levites, that, the first carnal ones having been slain, a new people of God may be enrolled, which passes over through the baptism of the Jordan and receives the promise of the heavenly inheritance.
06_marg578: TO THESE SHALL THE LAND BE DIVIDED. ORIGEN. The former people, which is in circumcision, is rejected, and the second is brought in from the uncircumcision, which obtains the father's inheritance not from Moses but from Jesus. For Moses, if he gives an inheritance to any, gives it not within the Jordan, which he does not cross at all; he gives land outside, not flowing with milk and honey, but fit for cattle, nourishing dumb and irrational animals better than men. My Jesus gives the second people a land flowing with milk and honey, nay rather one that is a honeycomb above every land. And Moses indeed does not give the inheritance by lot, nor can he weigh by peoples, houses, families, names and the merits of each, and by divine lot. This Jesus alone does, to whom the Father has given all judgment. He knows too how to assign each a worthy mansion. Yet there are some among these who stand out above, and are not brought to the lot at all: all the Levites, namely, that is, all who remain intent in the ministry of God, wakeful in his service, keeping the watches; they do not seek or receive a lot among the rest; nor is their lot on earth, but the Lord himself is their lot and inheritance. These are they who, dulled by no obstacles of bodily nature, having passed beyond the glory of all invisible things, have set the use and exercise of living in the sole wisdom and word of God; who seek nothing bodily, but only the knowledge of the secrets of God; and where their heart is, there is their treasure; they will always delight in the Lord and in his word and in wisdom. This is their food, this their drink, these their riches, this will be their kingdom. But those who are lower receive an inheritance of land, though of some more sublime and more powerful land. For the land of the living is promised, which is called of the living because it knows not death. And these indeed are great and blessed; but more blessed are those who shall see God no longer through a glass and in a dark manner, nor in bodily substances, but face to face, irradiated with the light of wisdom and made capable of pure divinity through purity.
06_marg579: The division and inheritance of this land holds the form of the heavenly inheritance which shall be divided to the saints. "There are many there, and there are few, but the few more blessed. For many go by the broad way that leads to death; but those who make for the narrow way that leads to life are called few, because few are they who are saved." And elsewhere: "Because iniquity hath abounded, the charity of many shall grow cold", not of few. In the ark of Noe (where the measure was given from heaven) the length in the lower parts is set at three hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty; but the top is finished in the space of one cubit. For in the lower parts were beasts and cattle; in the upper, birds; but in the highest, rational man. The top itself is gathered into one cubit; for all things are led back to the monad. Set down the whole number of the human race; choose the faithful, they will be fewer than all; from the faithful choose the better, you will find fewer; from these again choose the more perfect, they will be fewer; and the further you proceed in choosing, the fewer you will find, until at last you come to some one who may say confidently that he laboured more than all. Those who in this way are more receive more of land and bodily inheritance; but the few, little, because they have more in the Lord. Others receive nothing at all of earthly inheritance, who are worthy to be priests, ministers of God; for the Lord himself is wholly their inheritance. Yet for their beasts they receive some land, but of that which is adjoining the cities.
06_marg580: That, namely, the more numerous tribe should obtain greater spaces of land, but the one that is less in number of men, a lesser.
06_marg581: One just man, according as he is accepted by God, is held for many. Whence: "By one wise man the city shall be inhabited; but the tribe of the wicked shall be made desolate"; and one just man is for the whole world. "But the wicked, even if they are many, are reckoned small and as nothing with God." There is, then, also a praiseworthy multitude. Whence to Abraham, whom he brought forth abroad, he says: "Look up to heaven, and number the stars if thou canst; so shall thy seed be" etc. In which it is to be noted that the just man always abides in the inner things, because he prays to the Father in secret, and all the glory of the king's daughter, that is, of the royal soul, is within; but God brings him forth abroad when the matter and the order of visible things requires it.
06_marg582: The inheritance is commanded to be divided by lot; but I see Moses himself, to whom these things are commanded, dividing the inheritance not by lot to Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses. Jesus too gives an inheritance outside the lot to the tribe of Juda and to Caleb and to the tribe of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses. For the rest the lot is cast. Whence I think that in the heavenly inheritance some will not come to the lot, nor be numbered with the rest (although they are saints), but their inheritance will be choice, as was Caleb's and the tribe of Juda's and Jesus the son of Nave's. For as, when victory has been won, the spoils are divided, the choice warriors are not brought to the lot with the rest, but receive all the best things by the merit of their virtues, while the rest by lot use the right of victory; so it seems to me Christ my Lord will do. For to those he will decree special and sublime honours whose magnificent deeds and sublime virtues he knows. Whence he says: "Father, I will that where I am, they also may be with me"; and elsewhere: "You also shall sit on twelve thrones"; and elsewhere: "As thou, Father, in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us." All these come down not by lot but by the prerogative of love.
06_interl551: the faithful, namely, of both peoples, or the followers of action or of contemplation
06_marg583: BUT CALEB, etc. ISIDORE. Six hundred thousand armed men are said to have gone out of Egypt, and only two entered the land of promise. For many pass through baptism to the faith, but very few come to the heavenly fatherland, according to that: "Many are called, but few chosen." Only two enter, on account of those who from both peoples obtain the heavenly kingdom, or who through action and contemplation are predestined to eternal beatitude.
06_interl552: because the people of the law is not shut out from the possession of the Gospel
06_interl553: daughters: that is, works accomplished by the ministry of the body.
06_interl554: of him, namely, who has the shadow of the law in his mouth, perceiving nothing deep, nothing spiritual
06_interl556: among the people, namely, not among the Levites, whose inheritance is God alone
06_marg584: ORIGEN. Thou shalt give a possession, etc. What force these things have according to the history is plain to all who know that these laws are kept not only among the children of Israel but among all men who live by laws at all. Whence it appears that the freedom of the daughters of Salphaad not only conferred an inheritance on them but gave perpetual rights of living to the world. You see how great is the usefulness even of the history: who can dissolve these laws which the whole world uses? But let us seek how we may be edified spiritually. For it can happen that I have neither daughters according to the flesh nor a right of inheritance; then for someone the law which was sanctioned by the divine voice will be idle. Let us inquire, then, in the spiritual law, who these five daughters are, who, even if their father died for some sin, yet themselves receive an inheritance by the command of God. The virtues of the soul and the senses of the mind are sons; but the daughters are the works fulfilled by the ministry of the body. For there are five senses of the body, by which every work in the body is accomplished. These five daughters, then, that is, the perfection of works, even if they remain bereft of a father, are not cast off from the inheritance; they are not shut out from the kingdom, but receive an inheritance in the midst of the people of God. Salphaad is interpreted "shadow in his mouth". This is understanding, the father of works. There are many brethren in whom there is no higher and deeper understanding, but the sense in them is deadened; whence his heart too died within him. This one, then, if he savours nothing for spiritual understanding, but is deadened, yet if he has begotten daughters, that is, the works of God's commandments, they will certainly obtain an inheritance with the people of God. He will not indeed be able to be numbered among those whose portion is the Lord himself; for many are called but few chosen. And it is shown by the very name why he could not beget sons. For it is interpreted "shadow in his mouth": he who has the shadow of the law in his mouth and not the very image of the things can perceive nothing spiritual, nothing of deep understanding; only the shadow of the law is in his mouth; he cannot beget manly and spiritual senses, but works and acts, which are the simpler mysteries of life. And therefore it shows in these the clemency of the Lord: that the more innocent, even if they fall short in sense but have good works, are not shut out from the inheritance of the saints. Rightly, then, did the daughters of Salphaad speak.
06_interl557: who is strong in wisdom and understanding
06_marg585: ORIGEN. A law of succession is set down: that first the son, in the second place the daughter should succeed, third the brother, fourth the father's brother; the fifth degree does not mark out anyone certain, but whoever is nearer out of the whole family should succeed. In these the sense of the history is whole and perfect, so that it seems to require nothing. But he who is learned in the spiritual laws can understand the different degrees of succession, and how the first degree of obtaining the heavenly inheritance is by merit of doctrine and knowledge, which is the male son; the second by the prerogative of works, which is the daughter; the third of fellow-feeling and imitation, whence it is also named brother. For there are some who do nothing of their own accord and by their own understanding, but, set among brethren, by imitation seem to do the things which those do who are moved by their own understanding. To these too the third degree of inheritance is given, as to brethren. The fourth, which he names the father's brother, can be understood as the order of men who try to fulfil the things heard from the fathers, moved not so much by their own senses, nor stirred by present doctrine, as by the tradition of the elders; yet they do something good. But the last degree is written as whoever in any way shall have been next to these; as if he said: whether by occasion or by the truth of doctrine anyone has done something good, he shall not lose his reward.
06_interl558: him, namely, who is strong by the prerogative of works
06_interl559: who act by imitation of the wise
06_interl560: those, namely, who do something good by the tradition of the elders, not by their own sense nor by the admonition of present doctrine
06_interl561: namely, those who do something good either by occasion or by the truth of doctrine: for they do not lose their reward.
06_interl562: The perfect man dies not in the valley but on the mountain, that is, in a high place: because the perfection of his life was held on high.
06_interl563: It was fitting that nothing should remain unknown to one about to attain the height of perfection.
06_marg586: GO UP INTO THIS MOUNTAIN, etc. ORIGEN. See how he who is perfect, who is blessed, dies not in a valley, not on a plain, not on a hill, but on a mountain, that is, in a high and steep place; because the consummation of his life is held on high. But he is commanded to behold with his eyes all the land of promise and diligently survey all things from on high. For it was fitting that nothing should remain unknown to one about to attain the height of perfection, but that he should have knowledge of all things that are seen and heard. Therefore I believe it was so that, of all the things which, set in the flesh, he took in by bodily sight, when made in spirit and with naked mind hastening to the lecture halls and discipleship of wisdom, he might swiftly attain their reasons and causes. For what use was it to show one about to depart from the world lands and places whose toil he would not undergo nor glory receive? It terrifies me that things so perilous are said of Moses, the servant and friend of God, to whom the Lord spoke face to face, through whom he did signs and wonders. Thou shalt be gathered, he says, to thy people, as Aaron thy brother was gathered on mount Hor. He sets out the cause, saying: because you transgressed my word in the desert of Sin; you did not sanctify me at the water before them. So not even Moses is without fault; he too transgressed and was made under sin. Whence: "Death reigned from Adam unto Moses"; for it did not spare even him. For God hath concluded all under sin, that he may have mercy on all. But thanks to Christ, who has delivered us from the body of this death. For Moses could not deliver, since he too transgressed. He alone, then, must be sought who did no sin.
06_marg587: THE SAME. The death of Moses is the end of the law which is spoken according to the letter; namely, the breaking off of the sacrifices and of the other things which are likewise commanded in the law. When these, then, receive their end, Jesus receives the leadership; for the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to everyone that believeth. And as it was said of the former: "That all in Moses were baptized, in the cloud and in the sea", so let it be said of Jesus, that all in Jesus were baptized in the Holy Ghost and water. For it is Jesus who crosses the waters of the Jordan and in them in a manner already then baptizes the people. He it is who divides the holy land to all, not to the former people but to the second; for the former fell in the desert for its sin. In the times of Jesus the land rested from wars, not in the times of Moses. But this was said of Jesus Christ, not of the son of Nave. And would that my land might cease from wars! And it would cease if I served faithfully under my prince Jesus; my flesh would not rise up against my spirit, nor would my land be assailed by contrary nations, that is, goaded by divers concupiscences. Let us pray, then, that Jesus may reign over us, and our land cease from wars, namely from the assaults of carnal desires; and then each will rest under his vine and under his fig tree and his olive; that is, under the covering of the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost our soul will rest.
06_interl564: Even Moses transgressed. For all have sinned: Christ alone, then, could deliver from sin, who did no sin.
06_marg588: BECAUSE YOU OFFENDED, etc. AUGUSTINE. The Lord gives the same cause for the death of Moses as for that of his brother: namely, because they did not sanctify him before the people at the water of contradiction; that is, because they doubted that by his gift water could flow from the rock. But mystically it is signified that neither the old priesthood, whose person Aaron bore, nor the law itself, whose person Moses bore, brings the people of God into the land of the eternal inheritance; but Jesus, in whom Christ is signified, that is, grace through faith. And Aaron indeed died before Israel entered any part of the land of promise. While Moses was still alive the land of the Amorrhites was taken and possessed, but he did not cross the Jordan with them. For in some part the law is observed in the Christian faith; but that priesthood and the sacrifices hold no part of the Christian faith today, except that they were done and are past in shadows of things to come. But since it is said to both brothers that they be gathered to their people, it is manifest that the wrath of God, which separates from the peace of eternal fellowship, was not upon them. Whence it is clear: "Not only their offices but their deaths too were signs of things to come, not punishments of God's indignation."
06_marg589: Note: he does not choose his sons, nor his nephews, nor ask that they be appointed leaders; he commits the choice to the judgment of God.
06_marg590: May the Lord God provide. About to depart from this world, namely, he prays God to provide a leader for the people. He had sons, Gersam and Eliezer, and the sons of his brother, great and excellent men; he does not pray God for them that they be appointed leaders of the people; that the princes of the churches may learn not to mark out their successors by a testament of near kinship of the flesh, nor hand down the headship of the Church as an inheritance, nor choose him whom human affection commends, but to leave the choice of a successor to the judgment of God. He could have chosen a prince by right judgment, he to whom God had said: Choose elders for the people, whom thou knowest to be elders; and he chose such that the spirit of God at once rested on them and they all prophesied. But he did not choose, and does not dare, lest he leave to posterity an example of presumption; but he says: May the Lord God provide, etc. Who then will there be from the people, which is often wont to be moved by clamours stirred up for favour or price, or even from the priests, who should judge himself fit for this? Unless it be revealed to someone praying and asking of the Lord; as God says to Moses: Take to thee Jesus the son of Nave, etc. You hear the ordination of the prince of the people described so plainly and manifestly that it almost needs no exposition. No acclamation of the people here, no regard of kinship; to kinsmen let the inheritance of fields and estates be left; let the government of the people be handed to him whom God has chosen; who, namely, has in himself the spirit of God and in his sight the commandments of God; who is known and familiar to Moses, that is, in whom is the brightness and knowledge of the law; that the children of Israel may be able to hear him.
