06_marg591: The Holy, namely. For he would not say this of the spirit of man, which there was no one who did not have. Yet he is commanded to lay his hand on him, that no one, however strong in grace, should dare to refuse the sacraments of consecration.
06_marg592: AND THOU SHALT GIVE HIM PRECEPTS, etc. ISIDORE. Jesus succeeds Moses and teaches what ought to be offered spiritually in the Church. For the Gospel succeeds the law; the law admonishes what is to be done, and grace fulfils it: first, what ought to be offered on each day; then, what on the sabbath, for the hope of eternal rest; what on the calends, for the renewal of life; what at the Pasch, in which we are buried together with Christ by baptism, as passing from the dead to newness of life; what at Pentecost, for the grace of the Holy Ghost and the remission of sins, etc.
06_marg593: As if: thou shalt make him a sharer of thy glory. For things of this kind are not lessened as though divided into parts, but are whole to all and whole to each who have fellowship in them.
06_marg594: THAT THEY MAY HEAR, etc. ORIGEN. If the sacrifices and legal institutions had remained until the present, they would have shut out the faith of the Gospel. For there was in them a magnificent religion, full of reverence, which at first sight would astound the beholder. For who, seeing the sanctuary, the altar, the priests completing the sacrifice, and the whole order of that thing, would not think this the fullest rite by which God the creator of all should be worshipped? But thanks to the coming of Christ, who destroyed those things which seemed great on earth and transferred the worship of God from visible things to invisible, and from temporal to eternal. But Christ himself requires ears that hear these things and eyes that see them.
06_marg595: IF ANY THING, etc. Morally we are instructed that whoever receives power among the people of God should order and rule his own life and that of his subjects according to the teaching of the divine law, which is commended above all in the office of the priest.
06_marg596: ORIGEN. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel and thou shalt say to them: My gifts, my presents, my victims for a sweet odour, observe to offer to me on my festival days. And thou shalt say to them: These are my victims which you shall offer to the Lord, etc. No one offers anything of his own to the Lord, but what is the Lord's; nor does he so much offer as render. Therefore he says: My gifts, my presents, etc. As if: the things which I am about to command you to offer on my festival days are my presents, that is, they are given you by me; lest anyone believe that in offering he offers something of his own to God. For he is impious who thinks he bestows anything on God as on one in need.
06_marg597: On my festival days. God has his festival days; for human salvation is a great festivity to him. I think that through each of the faithful, through each who is converted to God and advances in faith, a festivity arises for the Lord. The unchaste man gladdens him if he becomes chaste, and the unjust when he cultivates justice. Christ, who pours out his blood for our salvation, keeps a feast when he sees that it profits that he, the holy one, humbled himself, obedient unto death. The Holy Ghost keeps feasts when he sees temples prepared for himself in those who are converted. The angels rejoice, to whose festivity the converted come. For there is joy in heaven upon one sinner that doth penance. We give God and his angels occasion of gladness when, walking upon the earth, we have our conversation in heaven. I fear lest, on the contrary, our evil conversation bring lamentations not only to the earth but to heaven too, and perhaps to God himself. For why does he say: It repenteth me that I have made man on the earth? And Christ, seeing the city, wept over it, saying: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killest the prophets and stonest them" etc. And I today, if I do not hear the words of the prophet and spurn his warnings, stone the prophet, and as far as in me lies kill him, whose words I do not hear, as though he were dead. That too is the voice of God lamenting: "Woe is me, for I am become as one that gleaneth stubble in the harvest, and as the clusters in the vintage" etc. But because Jerusalem sinned a great sin, all her festivities perished; because in the holy place and on the festival day they killed Christ. Therefore it is said to them: Your new moons and your sabbaths and festival days my soul hateth. Where he commands concerning gifts, where as yet there are no sins, he says: my festival days.
06_interl565: All that we offer is God's: we give him nothing, then, but render.
06_marg598: Let us seek diligently, then, what is the order of the festivities, that from the orders themselves and the rite of the sacrifices we may gather how each one by his deeds can prepare a festivity for God. The first festivity of God, then, is the one called unceasing. For concerning these it is commanded that they be offered unceasingly in the morning and evening sacrifices. He does not command first concerning the festivity of the Pasch, or of the unleavened bread, or of tabernacles; he set this first, in which he commands the unceasing sacrifice to be offered; that he who wishes to be perfect may know that the festivity is not to be interrupted but always and unceasingly kept; which the unceasing sacrifice signifies, that is, one offered in the evening and the morning; that he may persist with unceasing intent in the law and the prophets (which show the morning time). But he who sins and keeps days of sin cannot keep a festival day and offer the unceasing sacrifice. But he who unceasingly keeps justice and abstains from sin offers the continual sacrifice. If the prayer of the just is offered as incense in the sight of the Lord, and the lifting up of his hands is an evening sacrifice; since the Apostle says: "Defraud not one another, except perhaps by consent, that you may give yourselves to prayer"; and again: "Return together again"; it is certain that the unceasing sacrifice is hindered for those who serve marriage. He alone, then, seems to offer the unceasing sacrifice who is devoted to perpetual chastity. But there are other festival days for those who cannot unceasingly sacrifice the sacrifice of chastity.
06_interl566: attending to the law and the prophets
06_interl568: that we may pray without ceasing, and our prayer ascend as incense in the sight of the Lord.
06_interl569: in which one ceases from every work of the world
06_marg599: The second festivity, then, is of the sacrifice of the sabbath; and every just man ought to keep this festivity, of which the Apostle says: "There remaineth therefore a sabbatism", that is, an observance of the sabbath, for the people of God. Leaving aside, then, the Jewish sabbath, let us see what the Christian's observance of the sabbath ought to be. On the sabbath day one must do nothing of worldly acts. If, then, you do nothing worldly, but give yourself to spiritual things, come to church, lend your ear to the word of God, think on heavenly things, take care for the future hope, keep the coming judgment before your eyes, look not to things present and visible but to things invisible and to come: this is the Christian observance of the sabbath. These things the Jews ought to observe. Among them too the smith and the builder and workmen of this kind are idle on the sabbath day; but the reader of the divine law or the teacher does not cease from his work, and yet the sabbath is not defiled. Whence: "The priests in the temple break the sabbath, and are without blame." He, then, who ceases from the works of the world and gives himself to spiritual things keeps the sacrifice of the sabbath and the festival day. Nor does he carry burdens on the way; for every sin is a burden, according to that: As a heavy burden they are become heavy upon me. Nor does he kindle fire, of which it is said: "Walk in the light of your fire" etc. Each one sits in his place and does not go out of it. The place of the spiritual soul is justice, truth, wisdom, sanctification, and all that Christ is: this is the place of the soul. From this place it must not go out, that it may keep the true sabbaths and carry out the festival day with the sacrifices of the sabbaths; according to that: "He that abideth in me, and I in him."
06_marg600: But let us go back higher to what the observance of the true sabbath is. It is beyond this world. For as to what is written, God rested on the sabbath day from his works, we do not see either that this was done then on the seventh day or that it is done even now. For we always see God working, nor is there a sabbath on which he does not work, bringing forth grass on the mountains and herb for the service of men, striking and healing, bringing down to hell and bringing back. Whence, when the Jews laid down rules to him about working and healing on the sabbath, he answered: "My Father worketh until now; and I work"; showing that God rests on no sabbath of this world from the governing of the world. That, then, will be the true sabbath on which God shall rest from all his works, when sorrow and sadness and groaning shall flee away, and God shall be all in all. On which we shall celebrate the festival day and the true sabbath with the angels, offering the sacrifice of praise through the great high priest, who is a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.
06_interl570: He offers two lambs of a year old who shows God simplicity of mind and innocence of work.
06_marg601: AND TWO TENTHS, etc. He offers these who, filled with spiritual grace, the Holy Ghost teaching him the knowledge of the two testaments, teaches his hearers by words and examples, not for temporal gain but for the reward of eternal life.
06_marg602: That is, at the new moons, when the Church or any soul so draws near to the sun of justice that it becomes one spirit with him, and, renewed by him, casts off the old man.
06_marg603: THE SAME. The third festivity is the day of the new moon, on which a victim too is offered. Neomenia is called the new moon; and it is called new when next to the sun, so that it lies hidden under its brightness. But this festivity is a shadow of things to come, as the others are. The sun of justice is Christ; if the moon, that is, the Church, which is filled with his light, is joined to him so that it becomes one spirit with him, then it keeps the festivity of the new moon. For then it is made new, when it casts off the old man and puts on the new, which is created according to God. Then it can neither be seen nor comprehended by human eyes. For when it has wholly joined itself to the Lord and wholly yielded itself to his splendour, it thinks or seeks nothing at all earthly, nor studies to please men, but gives itself wholly to wisdom, wholly to the light, wholly to the warmth of the Holy Ghost, made subtle and spiritual. Therefore most worthily it keeps the festival day and slays to the Lord the victim of the new moon, as one renewed in spirit.
06_marg604: In the two calves can be marked the gladness of good work in the soul or in the body; which is offered to the Lord according to the two testaments, or to God in the two precepts of charity.
06_marg605: In the ram, the rule of discipline, strong and immovable according to the unity of the catholic faith.
06_marg606: Simplicity and meekness of manners, for the heavenly rest, through the grace of the sevenfold spirit.
06_marg607: He offers this who, enlightened with the oil of gladness, shows spiritual knowledge in the faith of the holy Trinity, with good work.
06_marg608: He does this who studies to turn the Decalogue of the law, in the two precepts of charity, to his own and his neighbours' profit, and so to dedicate his whole life to the Lord for a sweet odour.
06_marg609: This is done when simplicity of manners is instructed and adorned according to the rule of the scriptures, the grace of the Holy Ghost working with it. And well are all these commanded to be offered to the Lord in holocaust; because we ought to do these things not that we may seek human praise or present recompense, but that we may please God, the giver of all good things, in all things, and merit the recompense of eternal life.
06_interl572: The Pasch, when the true Lamb is slain who taketh away the sins of the world.
06_marg610: AND IN THE FIRST MONTH, etc. ORIGEN. In the fourth place among the festivities of God is set the solemnity of the Pasch, in which the lamb is slain; the lamb, namely, the true Lamb who taketh away the sins of the world; because Christ our Pasch is sacrificed. The Jews with carnal sense eat the flesh of the lamb; but we, the flesh of the word of God. For he says: Unless you eat... the flesh is that of the word of God. If we set forth herbs as for the weak, or the nourishment of milk as for children, [it is not flesh]; but if we speak perfect things, robust, strong things, we set out the flesh of the word to be eaten. For where a mystical speech, full and solid with faith in the Trinity, is brought forth; where, the veil of the letter of the law being removed, the spiritual sacraments of the world to come are laid open; where the hope of the soul, torn away from the earth, is set in those things which eye hath not seen nor ear heard: all these are the flesh of the word of God. He who can feed on the perfect, and with purified heart, truly sacrifices the sacrifice of the festivity of the Pasch and keeps the festival day with God and his angels.
06_marg611: THE SAME. There follows on this the continual festivity of the unleavened bread, which you will rightly celebrate if you drive out every leaven of malice and wickedness from your soul and keep the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. For it is not to be thought that God writes laws for men about leaven, and commands a soul to be cut off from his people if it has had a little leaven in its house, and is so offended for the sake of this leaven that he commands the soul which he made to his own image to be cut off and overthrown. But this God abhors: if the soul is leavened with the malice of anger or the wickedness of the spirit and swells to crimes. If we do not cast these out of the house of our soul, we shall rightly be cut off. But do not despise it even if you see a little malice leavening within you; because a little leaven corrupts the whole lump, and one sin begets another. For as one who has received the leaven of chastity is made daily more chaste, so one who has received the leaven of wickedness is made daily more wicked and worse.
06_marg612: THE SAME. All who are to be trained in higher disciplines find the labour of the rudiments irksome, since they do not know the usefulness of the discipline. Irksome, then, seem to us the rudiments of the Jews, who were trained in the first elements, when they are first heard. For each one wishes to learn of the things that pertain to salvation; but when the sacrifices of rams, goats and calves are recited, he thinks there is nothing useful in them. But if he can remove the veil of the old testament, he will see how magnificent are the things that are reckoned superfluous and superstitious. In the festivity of the Pasch it is a lamb that purifies the people; in others a goat, in others a calf or a ram or a she-goat or a heifer. One, then, of those which are taken to purify the people is the lamb, that is, Christ himself, who taketh away the sins of the world. But if the lamb which was given to purify the people signifies Christ, consequently the other animals too appointed for purification are referred to other persons who confer some purification on the human race. For as Christ, offered in sacrifice, granted remission of sins in the whole world, so perhaps the blood of the other saints which was shed, of one as of a heifer, of another as of a goat or she-goat or one of these, was shed to expiate the people in some part. Whether these are to be referred to the persons of the just and the prophets who were slaughtered in this world, or of those who say: "For thy sake we are put to death all the day long; we are accounted as sheep" etc., or to the higher powers to whom the care of the human race has been given, who would easily dare to affirm? For these animals are referred to this or that person not by appearance but by figure. As Christ himself is not called a lamb because he was changed into the appearance of a lamb, but because his will and goodness, by which he made God propitious to men and blotted out sins, was as the victim of a lamb, spotless and innocent, by which the divine is believed to be appeased toward men; so perhaps, if any of the angels or of just men intercedes more earnestly for the sins of men, for the divine propitiation he can be received as a ram or goat or calf offered in sacrifice to purify the people. Does not Paul seem to have offered himself as a ram or goat in holocaust for the people of Israel when he said: "I wished myself to be an anathema from Christ for my brethren" etc.? And elsewhere: "For I am even now ready to be sacrificed" etc. Figuratively, too, it can be seen that one is offered for the festivity of the sabbath, another for the festivity of new fruits, another for the festivity of tabernacles, as a goat or calf or ram, to reconcile God to men. For while there are sins, it is necessary that a victim for sins be sought. For if there had been no sin, it was not necessary for the Son of God to become a lamb and, set in the flesh, be slaughtered. But since sin entered into this world, whose necessity requires propitiation, which yet is made through a victim, it was necessary that victims be provided for sin. And because there were divers qualities of sin, victims of divers animals are provided. So, then, one of the angels or saints becomes a calf, who intercedes for the offences of the people at that festivity, another a ram at another festivity. But if men can be purified from sins, the victims are lessened. For as for the multitude of sins the victims are multiplied, so for their fewness they are lessened. Whence in the festivity of tabernacles, when victims are commanded to be offered for eight days, on the first day, as though in the abundance of sins as yet, fourteen calves are commanded to be offered; on the second, as though sins had been lessened, the victims are lessened and thirteen calves are offered; on the third twelve, after these eleven; as though, the multitude of sins failing day by day through the purifications, the number of victims is lessened. So too understand the reason of purification for the ordering of the whole world. For not only the things on earth need purification, but also the things in heaven. For perdition hangs over the heavens, because they shall perish, and all shall grow old as a garment, and shall be changed. Behold, then, the purification of the whole world, that is, of things in heaven, on earth and under the earth. See of how many victims all these have need, how many calves they require, how many rams, how many goats. But in all these there is one Lamb who could take away the sin of the whole world. Therefore the others ceased, because this one victim sufficed for the salvation of the whole world. For the others remitted sins by prayers, this one alone by power. For he said: Son, thy sins are forgiven thee. So, then, the world is trained, first to seek remission of sins through divers victims, until it comes to the perfect victim, the perfect lamb of a year old, who taketh away the sins of the world; through whom it may keep spiritual festivities, not to the satiety of the flesh but to the perfection of the spirit, with spiritual sacrifices offered in the purification of the mind.
06_interl574: all the time of the present life
06_interl575: sin, namely: "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin."
06_interl576: the fruits, namely, of the spirit: joy, peace, patience and the like.
06_marg613: ORIGEN. The sixth festivity is called that of new fruits, because firstfruits of the new fruits are offered. For where the field has been sown and diligently tilled, and the crop has come to ripeness, a festivity of the gift is kept at the perfection of the fruits. If you wish, then, to keep the festival day of new fruits with God, see how you sow or where, that you may reap such fruits as will make God glad and keep a festival day. Which you will not be able to fulfil unless you sow in the spirit, that of the spirit you may reap life everlasting and truly keep the feast of new fruits. Whence: "Break up your fallow ground", and "sow not upon thorns", but upon good ground, which will yield him fruit thirtyfold or sixtyfold or a hundredfold. He, then, is the one who sows in the spirit and gathers the fruit of the spirit. And the fruit of the spirit, first of all, is joy; and rightly does he keep the festival day of new fruits who reaps joy; above all if he reaps together peace, patience, goodness, mildness and the like.
06_marg614: ORIGEN. There follows the festivity of the sevenths. For as among days every seventh is observed as a sabbath and is a festivity, so among months every seventh month is the sabbath of months. A festivity is kept, then, which is called the sabbath of sabbaths, and on the first day of the month there is a memorial of trumpets. But who is it that keeps the festivity of the memorial of trumpets, but he who commits to the treasury of memory the prophetic and apostolic scriptures (which sound like a heavenly trumpet), and meditates on the law of God day and night, and who can merit the graces of the Holy Ghost by which the prophets were inspired, and say in psalmody: Blow the trumpet at the beginning of the month? There is also another festivity, when those celebrating the feast afflict their souls and humble them. O wondrous festivity! the affliction of the soul is called a festival day. For this, it says, is the day of propitiation, the tenth day of the seventh month. See, then: if you wish to keep a festival day, if you wish God to rejoice over you, afflict your soul and humble it, lest it fulfil its desires, lest it wanton. Indeed the festivity of the Pasch and of the unleavened bread are said to have the bread of affliction; nor can anyone keep the festival day unless he has eaten the bread of affliction. And the Pasch is eaten with bitterness. You see, then, what the festivities of God are like: they do not admit bodily sweetness; they want nothing slack, nothing voluptuous; but they demand affliction of soul and bitterness and humility; because he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. This, then, the day of propitiation requires. For when the soul has been afflicted and humbled in the sight of the Lord, Christ is propitious, whom God hath proposed to be a propitiation in his blood, through faith.
06_marg615: ORIGEN. The last festival day, of which he rejoices in man, is that of tabernacles. He rejoices over you, then, when he sees you dwelling in tabernacles, not having a mind fixed and founded upon the earth, nor possessing earthly things, and as it were a shadow, for an inheritance; but set in passing and saying: "I am a sojourner and a stranger, as all my fathers were." "For Abraham, Isaac and Jacob dwelt in tabernacles." When, then, you are ready to stretch yourself forth to the things before, until you come to the land flowing with milk and honey, God rejoices in you and keeps a festival day over you; this indeed in the present. But in the future, if you wish to consider how the festival days are kept, forget all worldly things; picture to yourself how heaven and earth pass away, and the whole fashion of the world passes. But a new heaven and a new earth is founded. Remove the light of this sun, and give to that world which is to come sevenfold the light of this sun, nay, God himself. Set there the angels of glory standing by and all the powers of the heavens. Consider how the festival days of the Lord can be kept there, what festivity is there, what joys there, what greatness of gladness. For although the festivities which are carried on spiritually in the soul are great and true, yet they are in part, not wholly; as we know in part and we prophesy in part. Whence: "Let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of a festival day." He did not say: on a festival day. For in part we celebrate the festival day in this world; for the corruptible body is a load upon the soul, and presseth down the mind that museth upon many things. "But when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away."
